title: Upstream asupersync: public per-stream retained/acknowledged send query (QuicRecords stop-and-wait epochs cost up to one RTT per record)
description: WHAT: fr-transport QuicRecords proves a sender's records are acknowledged only by comparing the live QuicStream with an EMPTY snapshot (EmptySendState, quic.rs), because asupersync 0.5.0 exposes no public retained-bytes or acknowledged-offset query (sent_stream_frames / pending_send_frames are private). Consequence: per stream, records are staged in epochs and a new epoch waits until the previous one is fully acknowledged - stop-and-wait. A record admitted while an earlier epoch is unacknowledged waits up to one more RTT before it is even staged. EVIDENCE (2026-09-28 namespace tc netem, diagnostic build): remaining sender-deadline expiries at 100 ms RTT had epoch=true, a staged frame awaiting acknowledgement and records pending behind it (PRESENTATION_FRESHNESS.md; the separate media-queue starvation was fixed in faae064). ASK (smallest): a public QuicStream (or StreamTable) method returning retained-for-retransmission bytes/frames or the highest contiguously acknowledged send offset, documented as stable; then QuicRecords retires records individually by offset and drops the stop-and-wait epochs. No second QUIC stack, no parsing Debug output. ACCEPTANCE: upstream API at a pinned revision (ties to fr-rc-transport-adopt-pin-7bn); QuicRecords uses it with a unit test that a record admitted behind an unacknowledged one is staged immediately; impairment rows re-measured.

Still to do for this bead: QuicRecords retiring records by offset instead of stop-and-wait epochs.

title: Every connect waits the client's 1.5 s handshake PTO: the host consumes the first Initial (upstream accept_with_initial)
description:
Every connect pays the client's 1.5 s handshake PTO because the host discards the client's first Initial.

MEASURED 2026-10-15 (ts1, loopback, fr-transport native_cold_accept discovers_unknown_peer, 3 runs): the cold accept handshake takes 1.556-1.559 s. Mechanism: fr-transport quic/accept.rs discovers the candidate by consuming the client's first Initial (to learn its address and DCID before admission), and the pinned Asupersync accept API cannot take that consumed packet. The canonical handshake therefore waits for the client's retransmission, and Asupersync's client HANDSHAKE_PTO is 1500 ms (handshake_driver.rs). This applies to every `fr connect`, `fr displays` and every reconnect attempt, and explains most of the 1.7 s live first dial (2026-10-12).

UPSTREAM ASK (bounded, AGENTS.md 3.1): `NativeQuicUdpConnection::accept_with_initial(cx, endpoint, driver, initial_dcid, local_cid, config, alpn, initial: ReceivedPacket)`; server_handshake_over_udp_with_early_data takes `first: Option<ReceivedPacket>` and processes it before the first receive (existing callers pass None). About 67 added lines; a diff is in the 2026-10-15 session scratch (asupersync_accept_with_initial.diff). FrankenRemote then keeps the discovered packet and calls accept_with_initial (a 10-line change in accept.rs).

SCRATCH EVIDENCE (local [patch] path override on ts1, never committed or pushed): with the patch the same handshake takes 57 ms (3 runs), fr-transport native_cold_accept 9/9 pass; full-workspace namespace suite result in the next comment.

NEEDS: owner approval to land the change in the asupersync repository and repin.

Each test's connects no longer wait the 1.5 s handshake PTO. Cold accept handshake 57 ms (was 1556 ms). The patch is ~67 added lines in asupersync (handshake_driver.rs, udp_connection.rs) plus ~10 in fr-transport accept.rs. Ready to land when the owner approves the upstream change.

title: Upstream asupersync: refuse a foreign-source Initial with CONNECTION_REFUSED and surface the peer close code on connect (enables host_busy)
description: From the v1ee spike (2026-10-13): while a share is active the host's NativeQuicUdpConnection silently drops datagrams from any other address (udp_connection.rs:1065), so a second client times out as host_not_answering. title: A controlled viewer loop that stalls past 100 ms ends control on aged captured input (Capture(Expired), named input_dispatch_stalled)
description:
Observed in the 2026-09-30/10-01 namespace control matrices on 33c2bd0, 70a53a8 (suspension), 8052213 (fr-4vf5): a lossy control row (6 ms RTT + 5% loss; also 40 ms + 1%) ends with Observation(Streaming(Control(Capture(Expired)))). It was fr's untyped native_session_failed and aborted most matrix runs. Since 46a5891 it is named input_dispatch_stalled: a typed refusal, which does not make the row hold.

Mechanism, from FRDIAG diagnostics (a scratch build, never committed; 2026-10-01 runs 1-11, 5 occurrences): frd viewer/controlled/events.rs MAX_EVENT_AGE_US = 100 ms. In every occurrence the capture queue held ONE event aged 101-105 ms, there was NO pending encoded input record (pending=false, so transport admission was not holding it), no suspension, and the viewer's event dispatch had not run for 108-140 ms. The controlled viewer loop itself was not driven for more than 100 ms.

Ruled out: the local cursor apply (apply_cursor, timed), controlled reference recovery (none in those sessions), the transport wait (a viewer network turn waits at most 5 ms, streaming.rs network()), and presentation (decode and present run in the media worker process).

Remaining candidates: synchronous work inside one poll of serve_inner (the UI callback in acquisition::notify, the decode job's own poll, job.complete), or scheduling starvation under namespace load. The cause is NOT yet isolated.

Wanted:
1. Find the stall: time each phase of the controlled viewer turn and name the one over 100 ms in the lossy row.
2. Fix it at the root: no blocking work on the input dispatch path (AGENTS.md 3.2).
3. Separately decide the aged-event policy. An aged press or motion is obsolete work (AGENTS.md 5), not a reason to end the grant: drop it with a typed count in the completion record. Releases must never be silently dropped: deliver them, or reconcile held state (reconcile_held) so no key stays held on the host.

Tests:
- unit: a viewer turn that stalls past 100 ms -> presses dropped and counted, releases still delivered, grant continues;
- namespace: the 6 ms + 5% loss control row holds (not merely ends typed);
- planted negative: restore the terminal expiry -> the unit test fails.
close_reason:
The cause this bead names is fixed (7a2a86a): aged captured input is dropped and counted (input_dropped_aged), a release of a held key or button is still delivered, and the terminal end 'input_dispatch_stalled' / Capture(Expired) no longer exists in the code. Unit tests an_aged_release_of_a_held_key_is_still_delivered and an_aged_press_is_dropped_with_its_release_and_control_continues, each with a planted negative.
Re-run on the asupersync pin, 2026-10-13 (ts1, load ~8 of 64, HEAD e445fda, real_impairment matrix twice, 162 s each):
- 6 ms RTT, 0% and 1% loss, both rates: held 8/8 in both runs.
- 6 ms RTT, 5% loss: held 8/8 in 3 of 4 samples. One sample (run 2, unlimited rate) ended at step 2 with transport_deadline_expired.
That one end is NOT this bead's cause: it is a session record missing its transport deadline under loss, tracked by fr-xfvs. No run ended on aged input. So the acceptance line 'the 6 ms + 5% loss row holds' is met for this bead's failure mode only; the row is still not reliable until fr-xfvs.

title: Keep remote sessions alive when optional cursor updates expire before transport admission
description: Plan 11.4 and 12.3; implemented remote-cursor profile. HostLane currently treats zero-admission Expired for an optional reliable cursor shape or replaceable cursor-position datagram as a terminal session error, even when QuicRecords remains open. Under host load or send delay, a missed 100ms position deadline can therefore end viewing/control. Preserve the latest bounded cursor target and retry its current state on a later turn without marking failed shape/position admission as delivered. Only zero-admission expiry with an open transport is nonterminal: retained reliable-record expiry, closed transport, authority refusal, and malformed routes remain terminal. Add real HostLane/QUIC regression cases for shape and position misses, successful later current-state admission, and terminal negative cases. This does not close the broader live-network qualification or cursor-polish work.
notes: Source implementation and independent review complete. HostLane now treats only open-transport pre-admission Expired as pending optional shape/position work; no admission count, delivered-shape cache, or sent-position state advances. A skipped position sequence stays consumed and the next turn encodes current target state. Retained reliable-record expiry still closes QUIC and propagates, as do closed/cancelled/unauthorized transports. Four actual HostLane/UDP/TLS regression tests cover final-check shape expiry, partial shape success plus expired position, newest-state peer delivery, retained expiry and authority/cancellation/closed negatives. These four network tests are authored but NOT EXECUTED: the real frd build is blocked by shared memory pressure before the Asupersync dependency completes. Keep in progress for runtime verification. title: Capture stall during motion ends the session: a late encoded picture is fatal instead of dropped with recovery
description:
Found 2026-09-30 while qualifying fr-suspend-o37f (stale view suspends input, plan 11.3).

When the host capture worker stalls past the 250 ms reference horizon, its result arrives already expired.
- An UNCHANGED result is now dropped as obsolete evidence (frd Subscription::admit_unchanged, same rule fr-media applies to queued metadata that expires).
- An ENCODED result is still fatal: SendCache::push refuses it with OriginalExpired, the frd caller propagates it, and the session ends (MediaTransport(Media(Send(...)))).

So a host stall of about 250-450 ms during screen motion ends the session, although suspension is meant to survive exactly that transient. A late encoded picture cannot simply be skipped: later P-frames reference it (AGENTS.md section 5: raw captures are replaceable, encoded references are not).

Wanted: drop the late picture, and have the next capture be a recovery IDR, through the existing source-owned recovery demand (CaptureSource recovery / needs_recovery), not a new path. The view stays stale until that IDR is presented, and input stays suspended meanwhile.

Tests:
- a real-worker unit test (native_recovery fixture): stall past the horizon with an encoded result; the subscription survives and the next capture is an IDR;
- namespace e2e: freeze capture during continuous motion; control resumes on the same lease.
Planted negative: propagate OriginalExpired again.

Pointers: SendCache::tick already turns an UNSENT expired reference into clear() + needs_recovery + OriginalExpired, and frd's reference-recovery path (media/recovery.rs request_recovery/recover, streaming/recovery/handoff.rs) handles needs_recovery for sessions that negotiated recovery (NeedsRecovery is terminal only without it). A late push should enter that same state rather than a new path; check whether controlled sessions negotiate recovery.
close_reason: Acceptance met. Unit/fixture: fd23f5e + b02a4f3 late_capture tests pass (ts1, CI). Namespace e2e: real_control::a_capture_stall_during_motion_recovers_with_an_idr_on_the_same_lease (f8bb0f7) passes 10/10 since 81c288e (recovered_streams 1, same lease) and in every full serial suite since (61/68 at 2d216d1; failures only real_audio, no PulseAudio on ts1). title: Rare view-only impairment failures: ingress cleanup failure; busy-screen reference loss at 40 ms / 1%
description:
Two rare failures in the namespace view-only impairment rows on ts1 (2026-10-14). Neither reproduces in isolation, and neither is tied to a specific commit.

1. real_impairment::view_only_session_under_namespace_delay_and_loss ended with frd run returning Err(Cleanup("ingress")) and an Event::CleanupFailed { stage: "ingress" }. This happened in 2 of about 17 runs on the build with the unanswered-approval fix (9459e63), and 0 of 10 on the older 41c3233 bundle. Nothing in that fix touches ingress, and the numbers are too small to separate the builds. A likely suspect is the ingress command timeout: fr-tailnet local/ingress.rs gives ip/nft 1 s (COMMAND_TIMEOUT). The same CommandUncertain end was seen live on a loaded ts2 (fr-idle-frd-cpu-icui comment, 2026-10-13), and fr-ingress-revalidation-load-qelg has a related case.

2. real_impairment::view_only_busy_screen_under_namespace_loss: the REQUIRED row at 40 ms RTT with 1% loss ended video_reference_lost (4 of 6 changes shown) once, in the full suite at c70a82b (72/73 passed). A/B right after: 5/5 passed with the media worker from before be372c9/bf17775 (reference-only decode), and 5/5 with it. So it is not a regression from that change. This is the recovery-speed family in fr-xfvs, where a lost reference under loss is not recovered in time.

Next: run the impairment file 20x under suite-like load with timestamped host diagnostics for the ingress stage (which command, how long it took, timeout or error). Then fix or bound the cleanup path, or document it as a known limit with the measured rate.

comments.text: 2026-10-15 ROOT CAUSE of the report-vs-close race (scratch diagnostic build on ts1, never committed: prints which terminal_sender condition refuses). Reproduced in isolation: real_audio::controlled::local_host_stop_fences_control_and_audio_together failed 1 of 3 and 1 of 6 runs; the lock e2e passed 3/3. In both failures there were no queued datagrams, no partial writes and no unsent stream bytes. One host Critical stream held only bytes ALREADY SENT whose ACK had not yet arrived: binding 4 in one run, the session-control stream itself (binding 1, one record, unsent_bytes=0) in the other. asupersync ACKs at the receiver's next flush, so the window is RTT plus the client's turn latency, which grows under suite load. My earlier guess (queued audio/video datagrams) was wrong. FIX OPTIONS (owner decision; both touch the documented terminal contract that 'native pending/retransmission payload' is Backpressure because flushing it after the fence would violate the fence): (A) upstream asupersync: a receive-only step that processes incoming packets and sends only ACK frames, with no loss-timer retransmission and no STREAM/DATAGRAM data. The registered report could then wait, bounded at e.g. half its 250 ms budget, for those ACKs and send the record, falling back to the close packet at the bound. This keeps the contract. (B) allow that bounded settle through drive_io_once when no unsent data or datagrams exist. A PTO during the settle could then resend pre-fence bytes after the fence, which is a contract change. Recommendation: (A). Not implemented.

comments.text: 2026-10-15 CENSUS of terminal decisions in 2 full namespace suites (ts1, diagnostic build logging every terminal_sender decision to a file; both suites 79/79). Per suite, 40-45 of about 170 registered-report and close-exchange decisions fell back to the close packet (server about 1 in 3, client about 1 in 9). Only 3 per suite had real backlog: in both suites together, 5 partial writes with 9-15 queued writes (mid-transfer) and 1 queued datagram. Every other fallback (37-42 per suite) was a stream whose bytes were ALL SENT (unsent_bytes=0) and awaiting only the peer's ACK. Host lanes: SessionControl, MediaConfiguration, Exact(0x0037), Clipboard. Client lanes: SessionControl, DecoderReplies, Clipboard. Most tests do not assert the report-vs-close distinction, so this shows up only as rare failures in the few that do (local_host_stop, the lock e2e, likely fr-close-exchange-flake-h5jl). PROPOSAL for the owner, option A made concrete: an upstream asupersync method on NativeQuicUdpConnection, e.g. acknowledge_io_once(cx, receive_timeout). It receives and processes at most one batch exactly as drive_io_once does, but transmits only ACK frames (generate_pending_ack_frames). It does not service the loss timer: no PTO probe, no retransmission, no STREAM, DATAGRAM or other control frames. fr-transport would then, for both the host's registered report and the client's close exchange, treat 'all sent, only unacknowledged' as settleable. It would wait up to half of the frozen 250 ms budget using that method, then send the record. At the bound, or on any real backlog, it falls back to the close packet as today. This keeps the documented contract (nothing new is sent after the fence) and should turn about 90% of today's fallbacks into delivered typed reports. Not implemented: needs approval to change asupersync.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 2026-10-15 CORRECTION of my census comment, plus prototype v1 results. The earlier diagnostic did not check termination, so its 'all sent, only unacknowledged' class mixed two causes. (a) Lanes still awaiting ACKs. (b) Lanes already TERMINATED (FIN'd or reset), with nothing unsent and nothing unacknowledged. EmptySendState::matches treats any terminated stream as never empty. So once a lane is finished or retired (the media-configuration stream after a handoff, decoder replies, a reset clipboard lane), no registered report on that connection can ever be the record: it is always the close packet. Measured on the prototype: about 13 of 23 fallbacks per suite are (b). PROTOTYPE v1 (scratch only, never pushed; ts1 ~/fr_chk/asupersync_ack plus ~/fr_chk/franken_remote_ack with a [patch] path override). asupersync NativeQuicUdpConnection::receive_io_once: drive_io_once's receive half with no loss timer and no flush. fr-transport: registered reports and the client close exchange settle, up to half their frozen 250 ms budget, on lanes that hold only sent bytes. At the bound they fall back as today. fr-transport 206/206, both new tests have planted negatives, and 2 full suites passed 79/79 each. Fallbacks per suite: 23 and 23 (baseline 45 and 40). Settled: 15 and 12. Still unsettled: 9 and 7. In at least one pair the client and host settled at the same moment. Receiving only, neither ACKed the other, so both timed out. v2 (running now): (1) acknowledge_io_once sends ACK frames only (no data, probes, retransmissions or other control frames), so peers settling together ACK each other; (2) a public QuicStream::retained_send_bytes() (the fr-00nc ask), so a drained lane passes even if terminated. Only unsent bytes, or a terminated report route, refuse.

title: Audio reconfiguration exhausts restart budget while the old worker is still cleaning up
description: A valid replacement Opus configuration can permanently disable Linux playback while the preceding decoder worker is still completing its bounded cleanup. Repeated service ticks incorrectly charge the wait as failed restarts and exhaust the restart budget before the old worker exits. Wait for bounded cleanup without spending restart attempts, preserve the latest valid restart intent, and start its worker after cleanup. Real restart failures and cleanup timeout must retain their existing failure bounds.
notes: 2026-10-26: Implementation completed and committed directly to main in e7468eecce59a0e2a52c14f48ec6cca7fb2f1172. Valid replacement audio configuration now waits through bounded old-worker cleanup without prematurely spending restart attempts; the restart budget remains reserved for actual failures. Six focused regressions were added. These new runtime regressions remain unrun; keep in_progress pending full runtime qualification.

title: Reference recovery for controlled sessions: a lost video reference suspends input instead of ending control
description:
Since fr-suspend-o37f, a stale view SUSPENDS control input (plan 11.3) instead of ending the lease.

Reference recovery (854f2e9, RECOVERY_HOST.md) is still enabled only for observation sessions: publisher.rs enables it only `if !controlled`. StreamingHost::enable_reference_recovery also requires Host::Observe and refuses alongside the cursor lane. The 2026-09-19 reason was that recovery fences input and readiness, which was then terminal for a controlled session.

Result: in the 2026-09-30 namespace matrix (suspension build), the top control-ending cause at 40 ms RTT with loss is `video_reference_lost`, a reference loss the session cannot recover from. View-only rows at the same impairment recover and hold.

Wanted:
- Negotiate and run the existing recovery path in controlled sessions (Host::Control, alongside the cursor lane).
- Recovery's fence becomes a suspension: tickets invalidated, held input released and confirmed (ReleasePending).
- The recovered IDR's presented evidence plus a ticket issued after the host's lapse resume input on the same lease.
- One original failure deadline still bounds recovery; renewal never buys recovery time.
- No new grant, no replay, no implicit reconnect.

Tests:
- unit/fixture: a controlled host recovers a deliberately lost reference with the lease intact and input refused until resumed;
- namespace e2e: the 40 ms RTT + 1% loss control row holds;
- planted negative: controlled sessions without recovery end with video_reference_lost.
notes:
2026-10-01: implemented in 8052213 (with 46a5891 names). Gate: fmt, workspace clippy, tests of every touched crate. Planted negatives: 4 generation guards, each fails its test. Namespace on the working tree: full suite 63/63, stale-view suspend e2e 2/2.

NOT met: the e2e acceptance. No namespace row recovered a reference (recovered_streams 0 in every held row, 2 runs vs 2 of 67acc95). The lossy rows end first on the host's own send starvation (OriginalExpired in the first serving round; see the new P1 starvation bead). The frd-level controlled recovery fixture is also not written: only the negotiation test was restated; fr-core and fr-client unit tests cover the generation fence. Keep open until a namespace row shows a controlled recovery on a held lease.

comments.text:
2026-11-08: d324bf6c fixes a control-ending bug in the suspension this bead builds on (plan 11.3).

The bug: a key or button pressed while a stale view suspends input is refused and dropped, and nothing remembered the press. If the view recovered on the same grant before the user let go, the release was dispatched. fr-client's input model had never seen the key held, so it refused the release as InvalidTransition, and the controlled drive failed, ending the session. Any keystroke that straddles a suspension's end does this. That includes a recovery's resume here: "input resumes on the same lease" is exactly when a held key's release arrives.

The fix (events.rs): a refused press is marked like an aged one (refused_keys/refused_buttons), so its release or repeat is dropped too, even after input resumes. A press that later reaches the host clears the mark.

Counting: suspension drops were not counted anywhere. ControlledViewer::input_dropped_suspended, and fr's `input_dropped_suspended` in the control completion and each fresh attempt's record, now count them. Found from live run B4 (a6ug, 11-08): the host saw `hel` of `hello`, the completion showed 10 suspensions (2386 ms), and input_dropped_aged was 0.

Test: tests::events::a_press_refused_by_a_suspension_takes_its_release_after_input_resumes. It fails on the previous code with View(Input(InvalidTransition)) and passes 3 of 3 (x2 builds) on the fix, on trj.

Not shown live: the harness's xdotool presses and releases within a millisecond, so it never straddles a suspension's end. Not run: namespace suite, CI (eff459ed queued).

Side finding, for whoever owns those tests: in the trj builder image, these failed under load on both base and fix.
- slow_real_decoder_process_reduces_remote_capture_without_stopping_session_service (base 1 of 2).
- fr's spent_file_consent_is_omitted_without_changing_control_or_original_reports, every time, with files_directory_writable_by_others: the image's /tmp carries an ACL.
- withheld_file_offer_expires_even_while_input_and_observation_are_serviced failed 3 of 45 on the fix and 0 of 43 on base, all at load 60-120 (Cancelled, not Expired). Its fixture captures no local input, so the changed receiver does not run in it. I treat it as load-sensitive, unproven.

title: Implement authenticated local close of a running native connection
description: Implement real fr disconnect and fr robot session close for the original foreground fr connect owner. Use bounded same-user authenticated local IPC, exact target binding, no PID signaling or bearer authority, and the original cancellation/drain path. Reply with observed cleanup outcome, never synthetic success; no new remote control or replay. Owns plan 7.3 and 18.1 and a concrete slice of fr-agent-robot-surface-3o3. Validate socket credentials, wrong target/protocol/bounds, duplicate owner, interrupted requester, cancellation before native setup, and actual completion before close confirmation.
notes:
2026-10-28: Implemented the actual Linux foreground connection lifecycle slice: fr disconnect and fr robot session close reach the same-user, kernel-authenticated original owner through a bounded abstract Unix socket. Exact target and fresh local instance checks prevent stale retargeting; one owner per exact target; no PID signals, new remote authority or replay. The owner cancels and drains its original supervisor, then returns confirmed/unconfirmed local native cleanup. Missing replies after stop submission are unknown_external_effect, never refusal or success. Local shutdown works without LocalAPI and rejects unissued robot lease handles. Nine actual-socket regression tests plus cancellation/output/CLI regressions are added in source. Pinned workspace formatting, documentation-link checks and diff checks pass. Runtime tests, workspace check and strict Clippy remain UNRUN/BLOCKED because the shared disk is full and building the exact pinned Asupersync dependency was SIGKILLed under the executor memory limit. Keep in_progress for native qualification; full robot open/observe/input remains unavailable.
2026-11-08 macOS continuation: the native client now binds the original bounded local session owner and services local instance-qualified status/close before tailnet access. Local disconnect cancels/drains the original supervisor and confirms only actual media/input/window cleanup. macOS pathname publication/reclamation holds one nonblocking lifetime file lock and retains same-user kernel peer credentials plus exact target/instance checks. Real-socket regressions cover concurrent owners, stale reclamation, legacy live listeners and unsafe paths. Native macOS end-to-end execution remains pending; no new remote connection, input consent or PID signal path is introduced. Keep in_progress.

2026-11-09 implementation slice: in-process media uses one drained blocking owner with bounded queued work and resumable cleanup; a blocked native call/destructor never becomes successful cleanup merely because cancellation or a deadline fired. Mac UI no longer takes render lock or calls nextDrawable in resize/expose; geometry revision must have a submitted real picture before local input eligibility. Eleven actual-runtime worker regressions are included but not executed here (pinned dependency compiler SIGKILL); Mac native execution remains unqualified. AppKit/window retirement OS calls remain main-thread trust boundaries.

title: macOS client: fr connect --control natively on macOS (VideoToolbox decode, Metal presentation, AppKit input)
description:
OWNER DIRECTION 2026-11-08: FrankenRemote must work natively on macOS and Windows, as host and as client, and on macOS it must use Metal. The test pair is mac-studio (Apple M-series, macOS 27.0.1, Tailscale.app) and surfacebookje (Windows 11 Home, Intel Iris Plus, Tailscale "windows", relay path today). Goals: control surfacebookje from the Mac, and the Mac from surfacebookje. Order of work: (1) macOS client, (2) macOS host, (3) Windows host and client.

This bead is step 1: `fr connect --control HOST` runs natively on macOS against today's Linux host.

Design (from a read-only porting map of the connect path):
- Presentation is in-process on macOS. VideoToolbox HEVC decode outputs IOSurface-backed CVPixelBuffers into CVMetalTextureCache, and a Metal render pass draws them into a CAMetalLayer in an AppKit window. No CPU readback or copy. An NSWindow cannot be drawn into by another process, so the Linux "worker draws into the parent's window by ID" model does not carry over. To verify: I understand VideoToolbox hardware decode runs in Apple's VTDecoderXPCService, outside the app process; confirm on this Mac before relying on it as the isolation argument.
- Input: AppKit NSEvent capture behind the existing frd controlled::events Source/NativeCapture interface. HID usages come from inverting session_agent/macos_injection.rs hid_to_macos_keycode.
- Tailscale: this Mac runs Tailscale.app (no /var/run/tailscaled.socket), so fr-tailnet needs a macOS LocalAPI transport and trust check.
- Otherwise mostly cfg widening (frd session_startup/native_connection/media_quic/input_quic, fr-tailnet local, fr-files sender). Linux-only IPC (abstract sockets, SO_PEERCRED, prctl) needs path sockets + getpeereid, or kqueue.
- Clipboard, files and audio stay off on macOS in this bead (the existing flags already allow that).

Acceptance:
- On mac-studio, `fr connect --control <linux host>` shows the host desktop in a native window through VideoToolbox + Metal.
- Keys, pointer and wheel reach the host.
- Closing the window ends the session with a typed outcome.
- Unit tests cover the HID/keycode mapping and the hvcC to format-description path.
- A recorded live run with screenshots.
- Planted negative: an hvcC with a parameter set outside the admitted subset is refused before VideoToolbox is configured.
notes:

comments.text:
Owner decision 2026-11-08 ("you have to overrule the other contributor!"): macOS lookups read Tailscale.app's loopback LocalAPI directly, not a signed CLI child per read. On main as f5b33bac (preceded by df4cce7c, which makes main pass CI's fmt/clippy/test gates again after 9e4413e8/64416842).

Why: the signed CLI is itself a loopback LocalAPI client (lsof: 127.0.0.1:N -> 127.0.0.1:49280, same token), so its SecCode check authenticated only our own client binary, at 60-80 ms CPU per read x3 per renewal. An unprivileged client cannot authenticate the listener either: net.inet.tcp.pcblist_n returns only the caller's own sockets to non-root.

Kept from 9e4413e8: status/WhoIs/status binding and identity comparisons, Selector, the one-second Clock, the global lookup slot. SourceIdentity is now the endpoint run identity (i32 hash of port, token, publication time). fr-tailnet no longer depends on fr-tailnet-platform; that crate is unused and kept pending the owner's call on deleting it.

Evidence (owner's Mac, macOS 27, Tailscale 1.104.1): fr hosts and fr inspect (identity_checked, default and macos-desktop builds) live; 20 inspections = 0.23 s CPU total incl. process start (~12 ms per lookup vs 180-240 ms via CLI). Desktop sessions to ts2 opened and ran ~1 min until ts2 (25-45% memory stall from other workloads) ended them; no frame captured from this build. Mac fmt/clippy(default+desktop)/workspace tests/desktop tests green; trj Linux fmt, all-features clippy, fr-tailnet 145, fr CLI 17+7 green.

Still open here: the remaining-trust gap (no listener authentication when Tailscale is not listening) is documented, not closed. Not self-closing.

title: Upstream asupersync QUIC work from the fr-p0-quic-native-aqy gate (D1-D6): RFC padding/HP/coalescing, datagram admission bound, reactor suspension, loss-detector at real RTT
description:
WHY: The fr-p0-quic-native-aqy live-wire gate produced a NO-GO for external interop and a CONDITIONAL for the native asupersync<->asupersync profile; six named upstream defects block enabling any native QUIC profile. Full evidence: spikes/quic-native/RESULTS.md (asupersync rev 02df0613e).

GITHUB ISSUES (Dicklesworthstone/asupersync):
D1 = #66 send_datagram admits 1180B -> fatal 1212B protected packet (>1200 cap), connection-killed instead of typed refusal. Deliverable payload measured <=1150B.
D2 = #67 caller-driven receive path busy-polls a full core while idle (6s silence = 6s CPU in drive_io_once) — violates the <0.1%-core idle daemon objective.
D3 = #68 client Initial datagrams unpadded (288B measured; RFC 9000 §14.1 minimum 1200) — compliant servers drop silently.
D4 = #69 decode_long_header validates reserved/pn-length bits BEFORE header-protection removal (RFC 9001 §5.4) — rejects every compliant peer (packet_header_decode vs quinn).
D5 = #70 one-packet-per-datagram parsing breaks RFC 9000 §12.2 coalescing; packet_unprotect misclassified as retryable 'stale'.
D6 = #71 ~71% spurious loss + cwnd collapse to 2400B at ~29ms real RTT (1 MiB took 14.3s on a clean direct tailnet path).

ACCEPTANCE: fixes land upstream (or as reviewed patches counted to the plan's 15k transport allowance) AND the spikes/quic-native harness re-runs green on RESULTS.md rows 8-13, including quinn interop both directions. NEVER a second QUIC stack (AGENTS.md §3.1).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
2026-10-14 findings (ts1 namespace, tailnet-path emulation; scratch client printing its final typed failure; nothing below is committed except where noted).

What the 'control_renewal_failed' / host-ended controlled ends are, after fr-oj9u (2 runs, 13 ends): 9 were the HOST ending the lease, now visible through the close code (c078b34): PeerClosed(Lease(SessionEnded)) 6, HostFailure 2, ViewInvalidated 1; 4 were the client stopping with Stopped(InvalidControl).

Mechanism found for SessionEnded: all critical lanes of a connection share ONE admission budget (Policy::default: 16 records / 8 KiB). Under loss the per-picture progress lane is held behind a lost packet's stop-and-wait epoch and its admitted records pile up (an earlier host expiry dump: 12 progress + 2 session-control + 2 input-feedback = 16). The host's renewal challenge must be ADMITTED within 1 s (renewal.rs send_by); it meets backpressure until that passes, and the host ends the session.

On the client, renewal RESPONSES share the session-control outbound lane with presented reports (ViewerPresentation uses routes.outbound), and the response's local send deadline is 1 s (ObservationResponder until = accept + 1 s). Same starvation, other direction: Stopped(InvalidControl).

Tried and NOT landed: a per-lane reserve in QuicRecords admission (a lane with records queued may not take the last quarter of the critical budget; patch kept in the session scratchpad). frd 1269 passed with it and a new transport test proved the rule, but the matrix was mixed: 36/26/36 of 64 lossy-row steps vs 29-34 before, rows held 2/8 each run (vs 1-2), run 1 had 6 control_renewal_failed, and run 2 showed a NEW unnamed end Control(Session(Transport(Handler))) twice. The rule penalises the client's renewal response whenever presented reports are queued on its lane, so it cannot help that direction.

Suggested direction: give renewal challenges/responses their own critical lane (or an explicit per-record-class reservation keyed by message kind, not by lane), so per-picture metadata can never starve session renewal; and coalesce progress/presented metadata above the transport so it does not pile up behind one epoch. Both are protocol/session-layout changes worth an owner look.

title: Qualify macOS graphical screen-lock revocation without treating keybag state as an unlocked session
description:
Qualify a supported macOS graphical screen-lock authority boundary, including startup while already locked, lock+unlock between samples, Fast User Switching, same-UID remote login and pending/entered input operations. The new read-only console/sleep monitor intentionally does not claim screen-lock coverage.

Public CGSession properties provide UID/on-console/login-done, not a documented screen-lock state. NSApplication protected-data availability concerns keybag state and Apple DTS explicitly does not guarantee it becomes unavailable for every graphical lock (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/850327). A negative protected-data notification is sufficient to stop a session, but a positive value is not proof of unlocked graphics. Do not rely on absent CGSSessionScreenIsLocked or undocumented notifications as a complete gate. Keep platform capability/refusal honest until native evidence supports the selected contract; preserve terminal old grants and submission-time input fences. This is a release/qualification gap, not a completed feature.

title: Host capture deadline depends on the admission-refresh phase (floor ~500 ms, not the documented 2 s)
description:
Found 2026-09-30 while qualifying fr-suspend-o37f.

ObservationControl::deadline caps every worker exchange (capture, poll) at the current tailnet admission proof's expiry (peer_until). The running session refreshes that proof only when 500 ms remain (running.rs REFRESH_MARGIN_US), and the proof lives about 3 s. So a capture issued just before a refresh gets a deadline of about 500 ms, not the documented 2 s. A worker stall longer than that then fails with Worker(Deadline) and ends observation. Whether it does depends only on phase.

Observed: a 600 ms SIGSTOP of the capture worker ended the session when the capture was issued with 569 ms of admission left, and not otherwise.

The cap itself is deliberate: no worker exchange outlives the current admission proof.

Options:
(a) refresh admission earlier (e.g. at half its life), so the floor is about 1.5 s;
(b) recompute a waiting exchange's deadline after a successful refresh;
(c) document the ~500 ms floor as the effective hung-worker bound.
Measure LocalAPI cost before (a).

Test: a unit test with a fixture admission near its refresh margin and a worker delayed past it.
notes: 2026-11-08 continuation: supervised capture, selected-monitor discovery, decoder/presentation, and audio process creation now run on the exact pinned Asupersync drained blocking pool, outside the authority poll. The original deadline covers queueing, fork/exec and configuration; original caller and task cancellation plus live authority are checked before submission, at claim, after spawn and before publication. A Launching retirement phase preserves queued/unpublished custody; cleanup waits within its existing absolute bound for positive no-child retirement or the actual late-child exit receipt. Added actual bounded-pool queue expiry/cancel/drop, real post-spawn late-child/drop/deadline, and renewed queued-start regressions. Existing IPC cancellation test now waits for the real configure receipt. Independent source review, pinned full-workspace formatting, fixed source count (499979 Rust; 17756 glue), and docs check pass. Runtime tests of this revision remain pending: shared local storage is full and earlier builds of unchanged Asupersync were killed under the 8 GiB memory cgroup. This fixes a source-proven authority-stalling path but does not establish the cause of E2 or complete the live startup acceptance; retain in_progress. comments.text:
2026-11-09 regression from the 2026-11-08 continuation (9822d336), found live and fixed in 7a5bdbdb (Claude): worker fork/exec ran inside Asupersync's drained blocking pool, and a Linux worker's PR_SET_PDEATHSIG (fr-native bind_parent) is bound to the THREAD that forked it. Production runtimes use the default pool (0 min threads, 10 s idle timeout), so every worker (capture, decoder/presentation, audio) was SIGKILLed ~10 s after launch. Evidence: strace on a live viewer worker, "killed by SIGKILL" 9.997 s after start, no kill syscall, no OOM/CPU limit; a Python fork-from-exiting-thread check on trj reproduces the kernel behavior. Tests missed it because their runtimes use blocking_threads(1, 2), whose one thread never retires. Asupersync documents the caveat on Command::parent_death_signal.

Fix keeps the launch off the authority poll on the drained pool (deadline, cancellation and late-child custody unchanged); only the fork runs on one process-lifetime launcher thread under the launch's ambient Cx. New test a_child_outlives_the_thread_that_requested_its_launch passes, and fails without the launcher thread (planted negative run on trj). Live after the fix: the viewer worker lived 49 s of a 51.5 s session (was ~10 s).

title: Hosted share dies: viewer Expired after the ~3s initial lease, and a departed viewer's Transport(Expired) tears down the whole shared desktop

That 4 s extension is still uncommitted in crates/frd/tests/native_host_linux_serial/host_run.rs.

REPRO 2 (731e5f4 + crates/frd/tests/native_host_linux_serial/shipped_client.rs): the real shipped `fr displays n-host --experimental-native --json` binary against host_run::run succeeds. It negotiates with the shipped client offer, gets a 1-display catalog and exits 0. But the host never reports PeerFinished for that peer, and within about 10 s the whole share ends with Desktop(Err(Desktop(Publication(Display(Transport(Expired)))))).

(a) viewer observation / stream renewal expires at about 3 s. A background investigation is tracing an unacknowledged stream epoch in fr-transport/src/quic.rs.
(b) one viewer's transport expiry ends the shared desktop instead of finishing only that peer. This violates AGENTS §4 ("closing one viewer never cancels another's encoder"; the shared pipeline belongs to the OS share region, not one viewer).

title: Send new host file selections during an existing controlled session
description: Plan 15.6: let the host operator select new files or portable directory roots during one original controlled session using an opt-in same-user local frd send endpoint. Establish an idle FilesDownload attachment promptly after the original grant, reuse existing bounded ATP sender batches, preserve absolute selection deadlines and cumulative recipient quotas, retain each command's actual publication/cleanup receipts, and fence intake on session end. Host --send-control NAME requires --once and --input-agent and cannot combine with startup --send. Local commands use peer credentials, random owner-instance comparison, bounded paths/peers/history, and no automatic retry or reconnect replay. Include source/slot lifecycle, real controller/ATP regressions, and actual local Unix IPC checks; does not claim folder synchronization or durable reconnect resume.
notes:
Implemented the complete Linux live host-send slice: --send-control NAME on one --once/input-agent host; frd send submission, current/history status and exact-request cancellation; idle original FilesDownload attachment; repeated existing ATP sender batches; original transfer IDs, authority, immutable submission deadlines and cumulative receiving quotas. Sources are selected off the authority path on one fixed worker. Same-effective-user abstract Unix IPC bounds peers, paths, deadlines and 64 retained original controls; replacement instances refuse old commands. Admission is distinct from publication, failure, durability uncertainty and actual cleanup. Lost/malformed command replies preserve the exact original target/instance without resending. Active cancellation retires only the original download lane; completed old handles cannot cancel successors. The local cleanup reaper publishes completion only after both actual worker joins, including thread-local destructors.

Validation on the pinned 2026-08-31 toolchain: combined actual-source component passed 20 tests (14 real Linux Unix-socket/credential/protocol/worker-ownership cases, 3 production CLI parser cases, 2 command-evidence cases and 1 invalid-command-before-I/O smoke check). Strict pedantic Clippy with -D warnings passed for that component; full workspace formatting passed. The previously hanging thread-local-destructor regression remains intact and now passes. Added 4 HostSendIntake tests, 4 real controller/TLS/UDP/ATP/disk tests (idle and repeated file/tree batches, absolute expiry, cumulative quotas, active cancellation/cleanup with continued input), 4 real native selector/history adapter cases and host RunOptions regressions; these full-frd tests are authored but NOT EXECUTED here because the exact pinned Asupersync compilation exceeds the shared local memory limit. No stub substitution, full workspace test pass, live-tailnet or physical-desktop qualification is claimed. Keep in_progress until those actual runtime gates run. Full-object sends do not implement folder synchronization, durable reconnect resume, multi-viewer sharing or microphone forwarding.

2026-11-09 macOS extension: replaced the Linux-only command transport boundary with a shared authenticated native Unix endpoint. Linux keeps abstract sockets; macOS uses bounded fixed names in a private same-UID directory, a no-follow private publication lock retained by the actual listener, and inode/UID checks before reclaiming a positively refused stale socket. Connections are nonblocking under the original two-second deadline; peer UID and random instance validation remain mandatory. Closing an owner never unlinks a replacement. The existing two fixed workers, bounded selections/history, original intake, pause/resume/cancel, retained publication/uncertainty and actual-join cleanup semantics are reused. macOS frd run --once --input-agent --send-control and frd send now reach the real host owner instead of a platform-refusal stub. The shared read-only latest-batch snapshot also supports native progress without granting selection authority.
Validation: exact production IPC subtree compiles with pinned rustix/getrandom and passes strict all-target Clippy. Fifteen distinct tests passed (five pathname validation/privacy/deadline/object-preservation cases, three real Unix socketpair protocol cases, seven credential/framing/bounds cases). Twenty-one listener cases (four pathname, seventeen existing abstract socket) remain unexecuted because the managed executor rejects bind with EPERM; no skips or substitute listener implementation were added. Independent source review of the pinned macOS Asupersync peer-credential adapter found no reactor registration or original-socket ownership change. Full pinned-runtime/native integration and real macOS runtime/tailnet execution remain unverified; keep in_progress.

title: Agent observations with validity boundaries and preconditioned actions
description:
WHY: An agent clicking an old coordinate system is the automation version of the stale-click bug. Observations carry validity metadata; actions carry preconditions; violations refuse rather than guess.

SCOPE: Observation payloads: display geometry + generation, configuration generation, frame identity, source-freshness status, capture/presentation timestamps with uncertainty, current control authority; optional screenshots as user-requested artifacts bound to the producing observation, labeled by evidence level (decoded / submitted-to-compositor / instrumentally observed); actions accepting preconditions (expected geometry generation, current lease, maximum observation age) refused with typed reasons when stale — the client never auto-refreshes a precondition to repeat a potentially destructive action; window/focus preconditions labeled best-effort unless the platform is genuinely atomic; partial batch submission and unknown effects explicitly labeled; "submitted to OS" reported separately from "observed application result" (new pixels do not prove semantic success).

ACCEPTANCE: precondition-violation tests (geometry change between observe and act -> refusal); artifact-binding tests; an agent-driven e2e that survives a mid-task resize by re-observing rather than misclicking, fully logged. Provenance: plan section 18.2.

title: fr robot surface: JSON session/observe/input commands with staged acknowledgements
description:
WHY: Agents are first-class operators. The plan's command surface (fr hosts/status/doctor/inspect + fr robot session open/observe/input/close, frd status/approval/sharing) makes automation useful without an MCP server or workflow language — if the envelope is honest about what actually happened.

SCOPE: The robot envelope (schema version, timestamps, typed error code, specific next action) on every command; every response distinguishing success / partial submission / cancellation / refusal / unknown external effect; acknowledgement stages named admitted / submitted-to-OS / observed — never "exactly once"; an explicit robot session with view/control role returning status, limits, and an opaque local lease handle; commands reuse the live local client session (never a secret new host controller per input); the local client authenticates its caller — a handle printed on a command line is not authority, and bearer material stays out of argv and ordinary JSON; local-approval mode identical for humans and agents; automation cannot set host approval or sharing policy remotely; frd sharing set own-user|tailnet and frd approval set local|none as local-only commands.

ACCEPTANCE: schema-versioned golden JSON fixtures; partial-batch and unknown-effect cases each producible in tests with the correct disposition; a scripted agent drives open->observe->input->close against a real host with the full envelope log. Provenance: plan sections 18.1, v1.2 CLI addition.

title: asupersync 0.6 composition: the post-session closure drain is never re-polled after the peer region is cancelled (6 namespace e2e regressions vs 0.5)
description:
PROBLEM: With the asupersync pin required for live tailnet use (git rev ee72b665e, 0.6.0; 0.5.0 cannot send a real Tailscale certificate chain), six namespace e2e tests regress versus the 0.5.0 baseline on a clean host (ts1, Ubuntu 26.04):
- shipped_client::shipped_fr_displays_negotiates_with_frd_run, shipped_client::frd_run_keeps_serving_sequential_viewers_and_departing_inspections, shipped_client::recovery::six_shipped_inspections_do_not_exhaust_the_host_and_a_fresh_viewer_still_streams (host never reports PeerFinished after a departing inspection);
- persistent_desktop::peer_refusal_keeps_cold_desktop_available_for_next_authorized_client ("report the admitted peer too": the admitted peer's completion is never reported);
- real_impairment::controlled_session_under_namespace_delay_and_loss (untyped end at 40 ms RTT, 5% loss, 5 Mbit/s) and real_impairment::view_only_busy_screen_under_namespace_loss (1% loss).
Attribution (bisect, 2026-10-12): b2181e2 (HEAD + compile fixes, asupersync 0.5.0) passes all six; the SAME source with ONLY the asupersync pin moved to ee72b665e fails them (variant "V2"); asupersync main f86413d0 (2026-10-12 19:49) also fails them. So the cause is asupersync behavior since 0.5.0 in FrankenRemote's composition, not the datagram cap, identity or fixture changes.

DIAGNOSIS (inspection case, instrumented scratch copies, never committed):
- The host's application ends (ShareEnded PeerClosed at +1.55 s); host.rs's Scoped wrapper then cancels the peer Cx (cancel_fast User), and the one-record closure drain (fr-transport quic/lifetime/terminal.rs Drain::run, 250 ms bound) starts with 249.7 ms left on a NON-cancelled connection Cx while the ambient Cx (peer) IS cancelled (printed: ambient cancelled at drain start: Some(true)).
- The drain runs exactly two loop turns (+2 us, +180 us) and is then NEVER polled again: its own 250 ms timeout never fires, PeerFinished is not seen after 40 s, the process is idle (~1 tick/s), clocks agree (drain cx.now, driver now, ambient now all ~1.69 s), and the User cleanup budget is 1000 polls (not exhausted).
- Rebinding the ambient Cx to the drain's own Cx during polls did not help; an explicit task.waker().wake_by_ref() on Pending did not get the future re-polled either -> the task is not being scheduled after the peer region's cancellation (lost/ignored wake), not a timer-domain or quota issue.
- Live impact (observed): after `fr displays` the live host still relisted later; the next client's packet on the shared listener socket presumably wakes the stalled task. So serial hosting stalls until the next packet after a ClientRequested close; PeerFinished is late or missing.
Relevant asupersync changes since 0.5.0: Sleep completes early under an explicitly cancelled ambient task (4d6ec8cfb), protected close on endpoint shutdown (3621edd9c), idle expiry on standalone UDP owners (60f61e3d0), cancellation wake-target pooling (d754de593, f0943a787, c7d646a6f).

REPRO: build the namespace suite at the current tree (cargo build -p fr-native --features linux-desktop,linux-displays --bin fr --bin fr-media-worker; cargo test -p frd --test native_host_linux_serial --no-run), then run one test in the namespace (scripts/test_linux_serial_lifecycle.sh with a test-name filter, FR_NS_SUDO=1) on a host whose /usr is root-owned.

WORK: find which task is parked and why (scheduler state of the task owning serial.rs `running` after the peer region cancel); fix in FrankenRemote's composition (e.g. run the bounded drain in a region/task that is not the cancelled peer's, keeping the fence order: session fenced before the drain) or upstream in asupersync with a regression test there. Then re-check the two impairment rows (they may share the cause: timers/wakes under cancelled regions during recovery) or split them out with their own evidence.
ACCEPTANCE: the six tests pass on the pinned (or newer) asupersync on a clean host; a planted negative (reintroducing the stall) fails at least the inspection test.
close_reason: Fixed in a496ec9. Root cause was not a lost scheduler wake: native_connection/host/desktop.rs Run::poll polled the listener ONCE after the desktop completed and then dropped it; on asupersync 0.5.0 the peer's closure drain finished inside that poll (its timeouts elapsed instantly under the cancelled ambient Cx), on the pinned rev it yields and was dropped mid-flight, losing completed()/PeerFinished. Now the admitted peer is finished within the fixed 2 s drain budget (desktop released first, new requests fenced). Unit tests + planted negative (frd lib); namespace e2e under tailnet-path emulation on ts1, both runs: shipped_fr_displays_negotiates_with_frd_run, frd_run_keeps_serving_sequential_viewers_and_departing_inspections, six_shipped_inspections..., peer_refusal_keeps_cold_desktop_available... all pass (failed with the pin before). The two lossy rows (real_impairment::controlled_session_under_namespace_delay_and_loss, view_only_busy_screen_under_namespace_loss; also view_only_session_under_namespace_delay_and_loss) pass/fail by chance -> tracked in fr-xfvs.

title: A connection attaches at most 7 channel pairs in its lifetime; each reference recovery takes 3, so full controlled sessions cannot recover at all
description:
A connection can attach at most 7 channel pairs over its whole lifetime, and every reference recovery consumes 3. A long session therefore runs out of recoveries, and a fully featured controlled session cannot run even one.

Mechanism (fr-transport): QuicRecords::remaining_channel_pairs() = min((MAX_STREAMS - streams)/2, (MAX_STREAMS - 2)/2 - attachments), with MAX_STREAMS = 16 (quic.rs). Retired pairs stay as tombstones in `attachments` ("all consumed IDs remain tombstones"; test seven_retired_pairs_are_bounded_and_an_eighth_refuses_without_recycling). A reference recovery (media_quic/negotiated/replacement.rs and media_quic/recovery.rs) refuses with Transport(Backpressure) when fewer than 3 pairs remain.

Arithmetic:
- View-only: 3 media + audio = 4 pairs, so exactly one recovery.
- Controlled with input only (the 68th namespace test, "one recovery per run"): 4, so one.
- Controlled with input + clipboard + files + audio: 7, so NO recovery. A lost reference then ends the session (video_reference_lost), and only the client's reconnect remains.

Evidence: ef0beb3's new test session_startup::running::streaming::acquisition::recovery_tests::idle_broker_survives_two_real_replacements_without_a_grant_or_new_input_lane fails its SECOND replacement: begin_replacement -> Err(Transport(Backpressure)), recovery_tests.rs:134 (ts1, 2026-10-16). It was never compiled by its author. It is left failing, not reduced to one replacement, because it shows this limit. No multi-recovery session has ever been demonstrated.

Options (owner): raise MAX_STREAMS together with the negotiated stream credit (QUIC stream IDs cannot be reused, so the peer must grant more via MAX_STREAMS as retired pairs close), keeping a byte and count bound on tombstone bookkeeping; or recover in place without replacing the three media lanes; or end and reconnect deliberately, with a typed reason, once pairs are exhausted. Acceptance: a controlled session with clipboard, files and audio survives at least 3 consecutive reference recoveries (namespace e2e), with bounded per-connection state.

title: A clipboard item that fails with records in flight closes the whole controlled session (fixed)
description:
A clipboard item whose records were still unacknowledged when the item failed ended the whole controlled session. Seen in the namespace e2e with tc netem delay, fixed 2026-10-14.

Reproduction (scratch rows on ts1, real `fr connect --control --clipboard` against `frd run --clipboard`, xclip on Xvfb):
- Viewer copy, 40 KB, 120 ms RTT: the client ended with `native_session_failed` (outcome "refused"). Typed error `Observation(Streaming(Control(Session(Transport(Unauthorized)))))`. Diagnostic: the bridge's `permits_io` refused with `Session(Clipboard(Expired))` while 3 clipboard records were still in flight past the item's send deadline. Reproduced 3 of 3 on the 6-row sequence.
- Host copy, 1000 bytes, 200 ms RTT: the host bridge refused with `Session(Clipboard(LocalChanged))` (a newer host selection) with one record in flight, and the host closed the connection (`host_session_ended`).

Cause: `Bridge::permits_io` sits in the session's connection-wide authorize callback. Any clipboard admission failure there (item deadline, local change, switch, authority, stopped worker) refused the callback, and the transport closed the connection. `maintain` retires an expired clipboard between turns, but a fault first seen during the ≤5 ms drive closed everything. At high RTT records are always in flight, so ordinary copies hit it.

Fix:
- fr-transport: a `retire_requested` flag on optional attachments. `service_optional_retirements` retires a flagged pair inside the same checked operation, before its I/O: RESET_STREAM, queued bytes and retransmissions dropped, sender deadline cleared. `ClipboardChannel::request_retirement` and `send_prepared` (typed per-record refusal).
- frd: `permits_io` requests retirement and keeps the connection, except for cancellation and a missing clock. The bridge's send checks admission as a per-record refusal, so an item lapsing between admission and enqueue retires the lane instead of closing the connection.
- The clipboard is retired for the rest of that grant (no re-attachment, by design), and the session continues. The completion report does not yet name a mid-session clipboard retirement (separate follow-up).

Tests:
- fr-transport media_attachment `a_retirement_request_in_an_authorization_callback_retires_only_the_pair`. Planted negative: ignoring the flag fails at the route assertion.
- frd `a_clipboard_fault_inside_a_session_drive_retires_only_the_clipboard`, through the real controlled-viewer fixture: the switch flips after the turn's maintenance, the transport drive runs with `permits_io`, and input still crosses. Planted negative: the old `permits_io` fails with `Unauthorized`, the live error.
- Namespace rows after the fix: the 6-row sequence that killed the session 3 of 3 now completes (a later end at ~120 s is the LocalAPI fixture's 1024-request cap, `LocalApiUnavailable`, not product).
close_reason: Fixed in 145df7c (transport retire-request flag + bridge containment, unit tests with planted negatives), completion field and namespace e2e in 9375885 (5/5; old code fails 2 of 3 with the live error). Full namespace suite 71/71 at 9375885.

title: Clipboard items beyond ~one flight fail on WAN paths (receiver capped at the host view window; ~8 KiB/RTT bulk rate)
description:
Measured 2026-10-14. The README says "items up to 1 MiB". On a LAN that holds in release builds. On WAN paths, clipboard items beyond roughly one flight fail. They fail without effect, and the fixed `fr-clipboard-fault-kills-session-sgsw` path means the clipboard is then retired for the rest of that grant.

Method: namespace e2e on ts1 (`frd run --clipboard` + `fr connect --control --clipboard`, xclip on Xvfb), tc netem delay on lo, one row per fresh session. Release builds unless noted; scratch timing prints in the host worker and the core receiver.

Release ceilings, viewer→host (host→viewer similar in debug):
- LAN: 450 KB and 1 MB cross (receive span 47 ms and 154 ms).
- 30 ms RTT: 60 KB crosses; 120 KB 0/3; 250 KB 0/1.
- 120 ms RTT: 20 KB 2/3; 40 KB 0/3; 100 KB 0/1.
Debug builds are much lower on a LAN (~300-400 KB), because each session-loop iteration costs ~4 ms of CPU.

Causes (both measured):
1. The receiver's item deadline is the host's authority deadline at Begin (fr-core `clipboard/receive.rs` begin_before: `.min(authority_deadline)`). That deadline includes the input view window (`view_until`), not just the lease. Measured remaining at Begin: 129-390 ms (130-160 ms at 120 ms RTT). Renewal deliberately does not extend it (PROTOCOL_CLIPBOARD.md "fixed at Begin admission"; tests `renewed_input_authority_cannot_extend_an_old_transfer_deadline`, `renewal_does_not_extend_an_items_original_authorization_cap`). So an item must arrive within about one RTT plus a little.
2. Bulk rate beside video: at 120 ms RTT, Begin plus 3 chunks arrive in the first flight, 4 more one RTT later, then one 8 KiB record per RTT. A 16-record bridge window (instead of 4) and 1 ms session turns while transferring changed neither the pattern nor the release outcomes (saved as scratch `clipboard_window16_fastturn.patch`, not landed). The limit is in the transport: bulk prefixes behind queued datagrams and the congestion window, and the 8 KiB bulk attachment allowance (min with critical_send_bytes). The files lane shares that allowance and is probably as slow on WAN; not measured.

Not causes: the native X11 reader (xclip 1 MB in 18 ms), the process IPC, item byte limits.

Owner decisions:
- (a) Cap the item by the lease/observation deadline, not the view window, or check authority per record (as chunks and commit already do) and keep only the fixed 3 s bound. Either changes the documented "fixed at Begin" invariant and its two tests.
- (b) Give bulk lanes more than one record of flow/scheduling room on WAN paths. This interacts with fr-xfvs (send starvation on lossy paths), which is actively changing the same scheduler.
Until then, README/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS should state the measured ceilings, not 1 MiB.

The original first-byte deadline remains fixed; malformed records, incomplete attachments, critical streams, authority/cancellation and retained-send expiry retain their fences. The exact active pair propagates receive expiry with reset code 0x46524345 and retains an opaque original-reservation tombstone. ClipboardChannel reports Stream(Expired), Bridge reports ReceiveExpired, and native Application collects that terminal cause before the worker's resulting Closed/Stopped cleanup can hide it; actual cleanup and prior publication receipts remain separate. CLI names clipboard_receive_expired, including expiry before worker readiness is observed. No reattachment, delayed OS publication or replay is added.

Added regression sources for real UDP/TLS partial headers (12 bytes under a 512-byte native window), partial bodies both directions, fixed deadline retries, peer cause, reclaimed storage, surviving control/input, malformed negatives, actual worker fencing/cleanup and retained fixture publication receipts. Corrected the owner-reported superseded_unsent_commit regression: 161f637f deliberately fences the stale Commit in the same native-poll turn, so expecting one more successful turn was wrong. title: Main regression: per-route datagram custody dropped a full route's later arrivals (controlled sessions video_reference_lost)
description:
Upstream 02efa56 (per-route datagram custody) dropped every later arrival for a route that already held a blocked record. Partial receives return Blocked for routes they do not own (the controlled viewer's clock-only pass, startup and setup filters), and each examines up to a turn of native datagrams. One such pass held the first video fragment and discarded the rest of the turn.

Effect on main at 02efa56..1fd73cd: on a clean link every controlled namespace session ended video_reference_lost (12 of 79 suite tests: real_audio::controlled x3, real_clipboard x3, real_control x2, real_files x4). The 02efa56 build alone fails real_control::fr_connect_control_drives_the_host_desktop_through_frd_run.

Fixed in 624b9db. A full route's next arrival is parked in one more inline slot, and no further native datagram is read until its route drains, so nothing is lost. 02efa56's per-route isolation, deadlines and bounds are kept. Regression test fr-transport/tests/datagram_isolation.rs a_pass_that_blocks_a_route_loses_none_of_its_later_datagrams received 1 of 6 datagrams with 02efa56's transport.

Known trade-off: a consumer that stays blocked while its route keeps arriving holds other datagram routes back until its record drains or expires (2 s default lifetime). In-tree consumers block for one partial pass, or while the input agent is busy.

description: Plan sections 7, 15.4 and 19.3. Join the existing owners into the canonical control session: bounded host offer/client expectation, original-controller attachment, explicit separate consent and talk control, network I/O gates, original packet deadlines, route isolation, and stop/reaping on original session loss. notes:
2026-11-05 source follow-up for the owner-reported native mute/retalk failures: Host::receive captured the old native Control and deadline fields before dispatch. A valid UserMute/DeviceChanged stopped and removed that process and published the next state, but the next receive-round predicate still inspected the intentionally stopped old handle and permanently fenced the attachment. Receive now samples the current bounded published IoState on every checked round, through the same nonblocking helper as the retained transport guard. It preserves original controller/local-consent fences, original setup and ACK deadlines, immutable packet receipts, one epoch/one handoff, generation tombstones and both-child exit requirements; no automatic talk, consent grant or public capability enablement is added.

Expanded actual native retalk coverage for both UserMute and DeviceChanged: consent remains live immediately after stop dispatch, both original children must be reaped, state returns to Idle, original input/connection survive, the old generation is rejected, and exactly one next explicit generation starts. Corrected the deterministic consent test's ownership violation: each denial case now receives a new run/context pair, instead of reusing c/h after the first session closes and cancels them. No denial assertion or production gate was weakened.

Pinned formatting, whitespace, docs and independent source review passed. New daemon/native execution is pending hosted CI; local normal and metadata-only builds are blocked in unchanged Asupersync at the 8 GiB memory limit. The separate standalone PipeWire supervisor's early child exit does not traverse this QUIC gate and remains under investigation with an exact-source native-only harness; do not claim this patch fixes it. Public CLI microphone offers and physical/live-tailnet qualification remain outstanding; keep the bead in progress.

2026-11-05 native startup implementation: the first real 10-ms Opus PCM contains 480 samples per channel, while a supported native quantum can require 512 or 1024. Admitting that incomplete first quantum armed the strict native underrun fence before the asynchronous decoder could supply the rest. The original Uplink now prepares the smallest consecutive group of real frames covering the first quantum, then selects one fresh demand and admits the whole group without native polling between copies. Startup is bounded to three frames, 1920 per-channel samples and 7680 live interleaved bytes; a single fallible construction-time allocation reserves three complete fixed-capacity AudioPcmFrame owners plus metadata. Every original expiry, source timestamp, generation and format survives preparation. Only exact-next real packets can extend it; no startup PLC, deadline renewal or output rebase. Any partial admission failure fences and clears the original source before another native callback. PCM is erased after each native copy, and the startup owner is permanently sealed. Native C interval, expiry, permission and steady-state underrun checks are unchanged.

Local evidence: exact pinned nightly; original fr-native linux-microphone-playout library and both real worker binaries built; all eight new actual production-helper tests and six existing device-free microphone policy/authority tests passed. Strict original-library Clippy and focused exact-source harness all-target Clippy passed. The harness references the original repository modules and exactly matching lockfile dependency versions, avoiding only the daemon dev-dependency graph. Full workspace compilation remains blocked by unchanged Asupersync at the 8 GiB memory limit; actual PipeWire execution is blocked because the environment rejects AF_UNIX socket creation with EPERM. This is not native-consumer or physical-microphone qualification, and this independently proven source interleaving is not asserted to be the exact cause of the old native CI child exit. The owner's comment 297 separately records repeated successful daemon microphone/session tests at eb7b4906. Keep native execution, visible public consent controls and live-tailnet qualification open.

title: Extension: optional true 4:4:4 precision mode (HEVC range extensions)
description:
WHY: 4:2:0 discards spatial chroma that high bitrate cannot restore; colored terminal text and thin diagram lines benefit from true 4:4:4 where BOTH endpoints genuinely support the range-extension profile. Optional, native-oriented, never a baseline prerequisite.

SCOPE: Capability negotiation treating encode, decode, GPU interop, and presentation support as four separate checks; hardware-path-only by default (no silent CPU fallback — enabling via CPU requires showing the user the performance envelope); operating-point integration with the controller; capability rows per GPU/driver.

CONSTRAINTS: bounded budget inside the contingency; independent off switch; never holds the baseline architecture hostage; disabled cleanly where any of the four checks fails.

ACCEPTANCE: side-by-side text-quality evidence at matched bitrate/latency; capability rows recorded; the mode ships only where all four checks pass. Provenance: plan sections 14.2, 23 extension lane.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Probe unit tests for all four capability checks (encode/decode/interop/present) with each failure combination producing its typed refusal

title: Extension: bounded HEVC-only chroma-carrier experiment
description:
WHY: A research extension carrying full-resolution chroma in the luma plane of an auxiliary ordinary HEVC stream — preserving the single-codec policy while changing the representation. A known technique family, not a claimed invention; plausibly the best text-color path where 4:4:4 hardware is absent.

SCOPE: Packed auxiliary-surface arrangement within encoder/decoder geometry limits; matching capture/configuration identities between base and auxiliary frames (never overlay stale chroma on newer luma); base view stays responsive while precision waits within a small bound or falls back explicitly; requires dependable access to decoded component samples with exact scaling/range semantics — endpoints exposing only color-converted RGB or opaque surfaces disable the extension; explicit coded-pixel and decoder-session cost accounting; not mathematically lossless and never claimed as such.

CONSTRAINTS: fixed portion of the contingency budget; ABANDON criteria binding — two-stream decode cost, color presentation, mobile thermals, or complexity outweighing the text benefit ends the experiment with a negative-evidence note.

ACCEPTANCE: working two-stream demo with correct reconstruction on at least one qualified pair, plus measured cost; or the documented abandonment. Provenance: plan sections 14.3, 23 extension lane.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Unit tests for chroma packing/unpacking arithmetic; reconstruction correctness verified by image hash against a reference transform

title: Extension: authorized FrankenTerm semantic observation adapter
description:
WHY: When the shared application is FrankenTerm and the user explicitly grants the capability, agents can read actual pane text/state through ft robot instead of OCRing pixels — dramatically better agent ergonomics at zero cost to the baseline daemon.

SCOPE: Read-only pane observation as the initial semantic extension: restricted to the explicitly selected pane/session with visibility/authorization revalidated (a mux can hold hidden unrelated panes); the same session authorization path — never a bypass, never scope beyond the selected panes, never a general remote command execution endpoint; the full ft robot write/execute namespace NOT exposed; terminal output treated as untrusted application content; integration optional and outside the baseline daemon's dependency graph (a separate opt-in component); envelope schema reuse independent of granting terminal access.

ACCEPTANCE: an agent reads pane text through the adapter under explicit grant; revocation/visibility tests; dependency-graph check proving frd carries nothing from it by default. Provenance: plan sections 18.3, 23 extension lane.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Every semantic read logged with pane identity and grant reference; audit log verified in tests

title: Extension: selective small-group RaptorQ FEC experiment
description:
WHY: Baseline repair is retransmission + reliable bootstrap (proven in Phase 1); RaptorQ over small fragment groups might beat it on lossy paths — but only measurement decides, and a failed recovery gate was never allowed to hide behind future FEC.

SCOPE: Existing asupersync RaptorQ machinery applied to small groups of media fragments on the datagram path; compare against the shipped repair under the impairment matrix on stall frequency, latency, repair bytes, and CPU; adoption only where it wins across the board on target hardware including mobile decode-side CPU.

CONSTRAINTS: bounded budget; independent off switch; never mandatory on every frame (explicitly rejected scope); loses cleanly if it complicates the recovery generations.

ACCEPTANCE: the comparison table with retained runs; adopt/abandon decision note either way. Provenance: plan sections 12.2, 23 extension lane, 25.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Unit tests for group-coding boundaries; comparison harness runs scripted with retained logs per impairment row

title: Encode at the viewer's pixel size: negotiated viewport-sized pictures (5K host -> 1080p viewer runs ~20 fps today)
description:
WHY: The host always encodes the whole display at native pixels (host_run.rs choose(): Codec width/height = display.pixel_width/height). The client requires the decoded crop to equal those pixels (display_selection.rs decoder_setup -> require_display). When the viewer's screen is smaller, the extra pixels are encoded, sent and decoded, then thrown away by the viewer's downscale. They also cap the frame rate.

Owner's setup, measured 2026-11-11: mac-studio's display is 5120x2880, and mac-mini-old's screen is 1920x1080 at 1x. VT low-latency HEVC encode takes about 26 ms at 5K and about 6 ms at 1080p (macos-host-findings, 11-08). frd's pacing settles the interval at 7/6 to 4/3 of the source work, about 40 ms at 5K, so a 5K stream to mac-mini-old runs about 20-21 pictures/s (11-11 A/B). At 1080p the source work would be about 15 ms, which the same pacing could turn into roughly 50-60 pictures/s. That is an estimate, to be measured. A 6K native display also does not fit the 16.78 MP protocol cap today; a scaled picture would.

WHAT EXISTS: ScreenCaptureKit scales in hardware. fr_cap_open already takes width/height separately from the display (SCStreamConfiguration width/height). The client's input layout (fr_client::input::viewport, configure_viewport(source = display bounds, area = picture)) aspect-fits the display into the picture area, so a smaller picture should keep input mapping correct. Verify this live.

SCOPE (phase 1):
- A negotiated capability. The viewer states the largest picture it can show 1:1 (its screen's or window's backing pixels) when it selects a display. Peers without the capability keep exact native pictures.
- One shared pure fit rule. Preserve the aspect ratio, use even dimensions, never upscale, and stay within the protocol cap. The host sizes the codec with it. The viewer accepts the resulting crop only if it equals fit(display, request), so dimension checks stay exact.
- Host: VideoToolbox scales via SCK. Backends that cannot scale (X11/PipeWire paths) keep native size, and the viewer must then accept native.
- A second viewer joining a shared publisher gets the existing picture. State the rule and test it.
- Live: mac-studio -> mac-mini-old, pictures/s and frame_intervals before and after, and a pointer-position check at the scaled picture.
LATER: resizing the window renegotiates (new codec configuration generation).

NOT CLAIMED: nothing implemented yet.

My earlier +30% estimate for viewport pictures was masked by the shared pool's 8-picture cap and the cadence rounding (see vif, d280b1bf). With those fixed, a 1080p picture for a 1080p viewer runs about twice the rate of the 5120x2880 picture (~50 vs ~26 /s), with half the frame interval.
