comments.author: ClaudeOpus55
comments.text:
2026-11-11 (Claude): implemented in 9751f5d6 (pushed to main). Not installed on mac-studio; installing needs the owner's OK.

Design: I dropped the draft's narrowing of max_dimension_pixels/max_coded_pixels. Display::validate checks catalog entries against the session limits, so narrowing would refuse a 5K display entry and also cap clipboard images. Instead there is a new optional capability `scaled-picture` v1. A viewer that selects it states its 1:1 box (8 bytes after the capabilities in SelectedConfiguration). A VideoToolbox host offers it and encodes the largest canonical picture that fits: an even width below native, height derived from the aspect ratio by one integer rule in fr_wire::display::picture. Without the capability the selection is byte-identical to before.

Live, mac-studio -> mac-mini-old (1920x1080), view-only, the same new client against both hosts, 25 s sessions, load 11-19:
- a21cbf5b host: 25.7-26.4 pictures/s, p50 36-37 ms, 69-113 gaps over 50 ms per session (7 full sessions)
- 9751f5d6 host: 49.2-51.2 pictures/s, p50 18-19 ms, 2-16 gaps over 50 ms per session (8 full sessions)
- The client's new completion fields (last_attempt_media.picture_width/height) reported 5120x2880 vs 1920x1080 (3 sessions each).
- An 11-10 client against the new host still gets native pictures (25.2/s).
- Not full: one a21cbf5b session decoded only 30 pictures, and one session on EACH host ended early with host_stopped while frd kept serving. So the early end is not caused by this change.

Gates: trj builder image: all workspace test targets build; workspace clippy (all targets, all features) clean; fr-wire, fr-client, fr CLI (443), frd lib (1542) and the frd shared/clock/input/microphone integration tests pass. macOS: fr-wire, fr-client and fr CLI (332) pass; frd/fr-native clippy clean.

Still open (why this bead stays open):
- Input under a scaled picture is not checked live (all sessions were view-only). The mapping uses display bounds and the drawn area, not the picture size, so I expect it to hold. Live control needs the owner's OK.
- v1 limit: a shared source keeps its first viewer's picture. A viewer without the capability (older client) cannot join a source that is already scaled.

comments.text:
2026-11-11 (Claude): 3b96affc, pushed and not installed. A resized Mac viewer window now asks for a picture it shows 1:1.

A resize already reopened viewing in a new window at the new size, but the reopened attempt stated the old box. frd's reconnect Application gains picture(attempt, original), which picks each attempt's box. The Mac Session states the window's part of the screen box (WindowBox::within(fit_window)), and a resize reopen sets fit_window to the new size first. A later viewer of the same host process gets a newly fitted picture: 1582x888 then 1584x890 in one run today, and in the 9751f5d6 A/B an old client got native pictures after scaled sessions. So the reopened viewer should get the new size (the commit message words this as "the host ends a share"; it is the shared source that is refitted, the frd share keeps running).

Verified: unit tests (frd offers, macos_sizing on macOS and Linux, a Session test that fails when the override is removed); trj clippy, fr CLI 443, frd lib 1543. Live, the first attempt is unchanged (1582x888 / 1584x890 at 49.3/s). The session between those two never reached the host in 20 s; the commit calls it unexplained, but it matches the known back-to-back-on-one-port stall (fr-w4yu class): my harness started it right after the previous session on the same port.

NOT verified live: no resize was driven. A helper started over ssh on mac-mini-old is not Accessibility-trusted. To check by hand: open a view-only session on mac-mini-old, drag the window smaller, and read last_attempt_media.picture_width/height and window_resizes in the completion JSON.

Input under a scaled picture (source read, not run): the Mac viewer maps the presented picture onto the display's native bounds (fr-client Viewport::configure), so pointer positions scale correctly. The mapping keeps the display's exact aspect, and a canonical picture is off by under one even step: 1582x888 for 5120x2880 maps the display to a centred 1578x888 rect. Pointer positions are therefore off by at most 2 viewer pixels at the far left/right edges (0 at the centre), and clicks in those 2-pixel edge columns are refused as letterbox. Small; it follows from the even-width rule.

The Linux client has no screen size before connecting (its X display is opened in the presenter worker), so only a --fit size could serve as its box.

Still open: full screen (whether it reopens and what box it states is untested), input under scaled pictures (needs the owner's OK), old viewers joining an already-scaled shared source, and the Linux client states no box.

title: fr-lab: deterministic scenario harness on the Asupersync lab
description:
WHY: The plan's correctness story rests on deterministic simulation of loss, reordering, delay, cancellation, and timer races against the PRODUCTION state machines — not generated traces that never touch production logic. This harness is the substrate for the Phase 1 property suite and for replaying controller decisions from sanitized traces later.

SCOPE: crates/fr-lab providing: deterministic transport adapters (drop/duplicate/reorder/delay by seed and schedule) that plug where real QUIC/WSS plug; virtual monotonic clocks including suspend/resume jumps and scheduler-stall injection; bounded-channel instrumentation that asserts byte budgets, not just queue length; a scenario builder that scripts host+client state machines through connect/view/control/fault/teardown sequences; failure output that logs the full event schedule and seed so any red run reproduces with one command.

CONSTRAINTS: Asupersync lab facilities only — no wall-clock sleeps, no real sockets in this crate. Real TLS/codec interop is explicitly out of scope here (native/browser lanes own it).

ACCEPTANCE: a demo scenario drives a toy state machine through loss+reorder deterministically twice with identical event logs; seed printed on every failure; harness API documented for the Phase 1 property-suite bead. Provenance: plan sections 4.1, 18.4, 24.1.
close_reason: Implemented at 2c83177747ae933bdfc784e5ddfdf9f0d26a5b4e; original acceptance freshly re-executed by author, independent review not returned. 70 workspace tests, strict remote check/clippy, fmt/docs/UBS passed on matching source bytes. Seeded replay runs compare complete schedules twice with real loss/duplication/reorder; authority-stall demo runs production expiry check. Full commands, terminal exits, limits, negative evidence and honesty inventory are in comments 6-7. No live transport/codec/OS/hardware qualification claim.

comments.author: AzureBasin
comments.text: Implementation boundary: fr-lab supplies a bounded datagram fault adapter using Asupersync LabRuntime virtual time and DetRng, with scripted local lifecycle boundaries and actual fr-core SessionAuthority scenarios. Consumer: Phase 1 property suite. No live QUIC, TLS, codec, OS-injection or cancellation-of-foreign-work claim. Existing upstream DeterministicNetwork has count limits but inbox/payload/trace bytes are not caller-bounded, so this thin test adapter owns explicit packet and metadata byte ceilings. Reuse the runtime and entropy; no second async runtime or production transport. First fixtures pin delayed ticket refusal, observation-expiry anti-resurrection, loss/reorder replay, and cancellation/restart fencing. The harness remains test-only infrastructure and is retired/reworked if production adapters cannot share its byte/event boundary.

title: Resample the original input deadline after authority lock waits before OS submission
description:
Plan sections 6.3, 7.3 and 15.1 and PROTOCOL input semantics require the original ticket/lease expiry to be checked immediately before OS submission. Attempt::one calls InputSession::check with a clock sampled before it acquires shared authority locks. Waiting for those locks can consume the remaining ticket lifetime without changing that supplied sample; an in-thread native sink then posts with expired authority.

After the complete authorization check returns its original exclusive deadline, resample the same original host clock outside authority locks and refuse expired, regressed or revoked work before tracking a possible native effect. Do not renew the deadline, retry authorization or replay the action. Preserve partial receipts, pessimistic held-state custody for actual unknown submissions, and release-only cleanup.

Acceptance: deterministic production InputSession regressions hold the actual authority mutex across an advanced clock to reproduce the old stale sample, then verify no submission, expired/clock refusal, no spurious held press, and no replay. Cover exact deadline, a still-valid wait, revocation and partial multi-operation effects. Run pinned fr-core tests, compiler/Clippy and attempt full repository verification separately from native qualification.
notes:

Refuse expired, regressing or revoked work before speculative held-state changes. Preserve partial effects, reliable duplicate receipts and release-only cleanup without reacquiring policy locks or renewing authority.

title: Queued native uploads ignore cancellation and expiry while the view is suspended
description: Sending::advance_intake checks source readiness before consuming an accepted pending request. A suspended view therefore prevents that queued selection from observing its own cancellation or original deadline, retaining selected descriptors and a WaitingForControl result. Retire only terminal pending selections before source admission, preserve the original immutable deadline and earlier receipts, and never start a source or replay the selection when readiness returns. Verify cancellation and exact expiry while the desktop stays alive. Plan sections 7, 11.3 and 15.6.
notes: 2026-11-06: Source fix included with this record. The intake can retire a queued cancellation, clock failure or original-deadline expiry before waiting for fresh-view/source admission. Retirement drops only that selection's descriptors and completes its exact handle; it does not cancel a separate direct source, inherit unrelated progress or replace an earlier selection's receipt. The common Sending owner also serves interactive host downloads. Added four deterministic queued_cancel/queued_deadline/queued_expiry regressions for suspended admission and concurrent direct-source ownership. Pinned formatting, documentation, whitespace checks and independent source review passed before the execution backend stopped responding; the separate fr-core suite passed 240 tests. The new frd regressions and broader workspace checks remain unverified and this issue stays open for that validation. No native filesystem or live-session qualification is claimed.

- mac-studio (load ~28-40 from builds and other agents): 6 runs by 13:55. Five ended `share ended: Cancelled` / `frd: stopped` / `Refusal (observation_indicator_evidence_lost): frd-indicator: Indicator(Expired)` (exit 1; launchd restarts after ThrottleInterval 10 s). The sixth ended cleanly at 13:30:19 (exit 0, no refusal line), so the failure-only KeepAlive left mac-studio not serving. On macOS, exit 0 means a local Stop (LocalRevoke) or a stop request, and the log does not say which; I have not restarted it.
- mac-mini-old (macOS 26.5, frd waiting for Screen Recording): 12 runs in ~60 min (about one every 5-6 min). Each ends `frd: stopped` / `Refusal (observation_indicator_unavailable): frd-indicator: Indicator(Unavailable)`: the helper's pipe reached EOF, or it sent IndicatorFailed (host_indicator/process/io.rs). screensharingd was running there.
What is known: frd checks the helper every CHECK_INTERVAL 50 ms and needs each answer within CHECK_BUDGET 250 ms (process.rs). The helper (macos_observation.m, fr_oi_pump) pumps AppKit with waits of up to 20 ms, takes no NSProcessInfo activity assertion, and lsappinfo lists it as type UIElement, so App Nap or timer coalescing could delay its replies. Expired fits that; Unavailable (the helper ending or reporting a failure) needs another cause, e.g. visible() failing across a display or Screen Sharing change. Both are hypotheses. frd.log has no timestamps, so ends cannot be matched to load or events. A second candidate for Expired, from the code: State::ready_at judges the lease at frd's READ time (check_at(now) against the previous until, then issued + 250 ms). So time frd's own I/O thread spends starved counts against the helper, the same class as the E17 drive-turn bound (fixed for transport in e328dbf5). Unlike the turn bound, this lease enforces the local-visibility guarantee, so I did not relax it: that is a policy call. A fail-closed option would have the helper stamp the visibility observation with the shared monotonic clock and judge freshness by that stamp, keeping a separate bound for a helper that stops answering. Corroboration: frd's host_indicator fixture tests on mac-studio pass at load ~30 and fail at load 33-69 (5 in parallel, 3 even with --test-threads=1). Next: log the helper's reply latency and exit reason, then A/B an activity assertion (NSActivityUserInitiated | NSActivityLatencyCritical) at the same load.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 2026-11-10 correction (Claude) to my note above: its "Corroboration" sentence was wrong. frd's host_indicator fixture failures on mac-studio are not caused by load, so they do not support the Expired hypothesis. This Mac's $TMPDIR (/var/folders/vt/.../T/) holds about 218k entries, mostly other projects' test leftovers; /bin/ls -f on it takes 11 s. Creating or running a file directly in that directory takes 1.2-4.2 s, against about 60 ms in a subdirectory of it or in a small directory elsewhere (same load). The fixtures write their Python scripts straight into temp_dir(), so the child's start can use up the 3 s OPEN_BUDGET. With TMPDIR set to a small directory, the suite passed 19/19 twice at load 56; with the default it failed 5/19 at load 32 (3 deadline asserts, and 2 tests that panicked on the CHILDREN mutex the first panic had poisoned). The clipboard suite passes either way, but takes 16.3 s instead of 1.5 s. The live helper is the installed fr-observation-indicator under ~/Library/Application Support/FrankenRemote/bin, not a file in $TMPDIR, so this does not explain the live ends either. The hypotheses in the note stand, but are now uncorroborated. Side finding: franken_remote's tests leak about 4.5k fr-* entries into $TMPDIR (fr-localapi-, fr-clipboard-fixture-, fr-ctl-, fr-trust-, fr-macsock-, fr-indicator-). GitHub's macOS runners start clean and are unaffected.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
2026-11-10 (Claude; a63edaec; self-checked, not independently verified). At the owner's request ("it needs to be much more inconspicuous ... like in the system tray in the upper right on mac"), the macOS indicator is now one menu bar status item instead of a "Screen sharing enabled — click to stop" banner on every display. Clicking the item opens a popover, "Screen sharing is on", with a Stop Sharing button.
Policy changes, made at the owner's direction:
(1) Visible now means installed in the menu bar, not on top of every display. Readiness needs the item on screen per AppKit. After readiness, an item the system has collapsed still counts: when another app is full screen the menu bar slides away, as the system's recording indicator does.
(2) Display changes no longer end the run; the per-display panels were the only reason they did.
(3) Hiding the item through System Settings or the notch's overflow is not detected.
Findings while building it:
- macOS 26.5 and 27 draw status items in a system process. The helper's status window number is 2^32 and WindowServer lists no status window for it, so a CGWindowList cross-check is impossible there; AppKit's occlusion state and screen are the evidence. A first build that kept the cross-check never reached Ready.
- A menu or NSButton would hold the main thread in a tracking loop past the 250 ms turn while the mouse is down, so both controls act on mouse-down in their own views. Real clicks posted from another process on mac-studio opened the popover; a Stop click carrying fr-input-agent's tag was ignored; an untagged one stopped (local Stop) with clean cleanup.
- Turn timing on mac-mini-old (M4, load 1.5). As a LaunchAgent with no ProcessType, from about 10 s in nearly every 20 ms event wait took about 167 ms (throttled to ~6 Hz), with a 385 ms maximum in 60 s. That is enough to end a host on the 250 ms bound. As an Interactive agent (frd's setting): 3326 turns in 90 s, max 36 ms. The helper now also holds a latency-critical activity assertion.
Deployed (on main as a63edaec + ba3824b5, which only renames the control in frd's startup line and --help): signed installs on mac-studio at 17:07 and mac-mini-old at 17:08, same CDHashes on both. mac-studio: frd listening on 8443, helper bound to it, the icon drawn in the menu bar (screenshot of the menu bar strip), and the helper owns no WindowServer window, so no banner. mac-mini-old (still waiting for Screen Recording): the old build had reached launchd runs = 112 by 16:58, with frd.log showing 108 Indicator(Unavailable) refusals (earlier measurement: 5-6 minutes apart). The new build stayed at runs = 1 with the same frd and helper PIDs from 17:08 to 18:00. Which of the two changes ended the cycle (the display-change rule or the activity assertion) is not isolated. frd.log has no timestamps and launchd keeps no exit records, so the old cadence could not be re-measured.
Not checked: macOS 11-25; System Settings' "Allow in the Menu Bar" turned off; VoiceOver; the control and clipboard panels (fr-input-agent), which are unchanged.

title: fr hosts reports every peer derp_relayed: Relay (home DERP) is checked before CurAddr
description:
PROBLEM: `fr hosts --json` reports EVERY peer as `"transport_path":{"kind":"derp_relayed","relay":"nyc"}` with warning `tailnet_direct_path_unavailable`, including thinkstation2 while `tailscale status --json` shows it Active with CurAddr 192.168.1.124:41641 (direct LAN).
ROOT CAUSE: crates/fr-tailnet/src/local/discovery.rs ~146-164 checks `peer.relay` before `peer.cur_addr`. In Tailscale's ipnstate.PeerStatus, `Relay` is the peer's HOME DERP region and is populated for essentially every peer; it does not mean traffic is relayed. Direct = non-empty CurAddr; relayed = Active with empty CurAddr (and, on newer Tailscale, PeerRelay); idle peers with neither are Unknown/idle.
WORK: reorder and add an explicit idle/unknown state; consumers: fr-native fr_cli output.rs (~74-104), robot.rs (~87-100), fr-client discovery prober is_derp_relayed. Tests with fixture statuses for direct, relayed-active, idle.
ACCEPTANCE: live `fr hosts` shows direct for LAN peers with CurAddr, and no warning for idle peers.

LIVE TEST CONTEXT (2026-10-12, HEAD 596da32, first-ever two-machine run): hosts ts1=thinkstation1 (Ubuntu 26.04, x86_64) and ts2=thinkstation2 (Ubuntu 25.10, GTX 1070, driver 580.159.03), client trj=threadripperje (Ubuntu 26.04); all same untagged tailnet user, HTTPS certs enabled (Let's Encrypt chain YE1 -> Root YE -> ISRG Root X2 -> X1 cross-sign, 3,418 bytes DER). Host: `sudo env DISPLAY=:71 XAUTHORITY=... frd run --software-explicit --display :71 --worker <abs>/fr-media-worker --json` on a cookie-authenticated Xvfb with xlogo/xclock/xeyes. Client: `fr connect <NODE_ID> --view-only|--control --experimental-native --display only --x-display :72 --worker <abs>/fr-media-worker --json` on a second Xvfb. Evidence level: LIVE (real tailnet, real Tailscale cert, real WhoIs), Xvfb displays (no compositor/HiDPI claim). The namespace e2e suite cannot see these defects: its fixture LocalAPI returns static status, its test CA chain is small, and loopback MTU is 64 KiB.
close_reason: Fixed in 4210bb5. Self-verified by the implementing session (no independent verifier) by re-running the acceptance checks; LIVE on trj: fr hosts shows thinkstation1/2, mac-studio, mac-mini-max as direct (CurAddr), idle peers with no path and no warning, sensedemobox derp_relayed only while Tailscale itself shows active; relay ord; 8-case table test with planted negative.

title: Idle frd uses ~2.2% of a core (target <0.1%): UDP busy-poll and per-renewal nft/ip process spawns
description:
PROBLEM: Plan objective for the idle broker is <25 MiB RSS and <0.1% of one core. Measured live on ts1 (release build, listening, no viewer, 30 s via /proc/PID/stat utime+stime): 2.17% of one core (~20x over); RSS 9.7 MB (meets target). Measurement scope: frd process only, Tailscale's cost excluded; build used scratch transport fixes (asupersync main + 1200-byte cap), which do not touch the idle loop.
OBSERVED CAUSES (strace on the debug host, 10 s window): ~3,100 `recvfrom(<udp fd>) = -1 EAGAIN` (~300/s busy polling of the listener socket) and ~20 child process pairs `/usr/bin/ip -j address show dev tailscale0` + `/usr/sbin/nft -j -n list table inet frd_...` (ingress renewal spawning processes every ~0.5 s).
WORK: make the listener readiness-driven (reactor wakeups, no timed spin), and make ingress verification event-driven or much less frequent (netlink monitoring or a long period) while still detecting rule removal; add an idle-CPU/RSS measurement script with a stated scope and a regression gate.
ACCEPTANCE: idle frd < 0.1% of one core over 60 s with the listener and ingress rule active, measured by the script.

LIVE TEST CONTEXT (2026-10-12, HEAD 596da32, first-ever two-machine run): hosts ts1=thinkstation1 (Ubuntu 26.04, x86_64) and ts2=thinkstation2 (Ubuntu 25.10, GTX 1070, driver 580.159.03), client trj=threadripperje (Ubuntu 26.04); all same untagged tailnet user, HTTPS certs enabled (Let's Encrypt chain YE1 -> Root YE -> ISRG Root X2 -> X1 cross-sign, 3,418 bytes DER). Host: `sudo env DISPLAY=:71 XAUTHORITY=... frd run --software-explicit --display :71 --worker <abs>/fr-media-worker --json` on a cookie-authenticated Xvfb with xlogo/xclock/xeyes. Client: `fr connect <NODE_ID> --view-only|--control --experimental-native --display only --x-display :72 --worker <abs>/fr-media-worker --json` on a second Xvfb. Evidence level: LIVE (real tailnet, real Tailscale cert, real WhoIs), Xvfb displays (no compositor/HiDPI claim). The namespace e2e suite cannot see these defects: its fixture LocalAPI returns static status, its test CA chain is small, and loopback MTU is 64 KiB.
notes: 2026-11-11: working on a bounded Linux observation-watchdog slice: replace the 5 ms watcher poll with an absolute CLOCK_BOOTTIME deadline wait plus explicit teardown wakeups. macOS keeps its existing polling until a suspend-inclusive native wait is qualified. This does not claim the broader idle-family CPU objective.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: LIVE observation 2026-10-12 (ts2, load 24-40): frd run ended twice with Listener(Err(Ingress(CommandUncertain))) -> ingress_unenforced (once as cleanup_failed stage ingress). fr-tailnet local/ingress.rs runs ip/nft with COMMAND_TIMEOUT 1 s every REFRESH_INTERVAL 500 ms; measured on ts2 both commands take ~10 ms, so a 1 s timeout firing suggests the command future was not polled (or its timer fired early) rather than a slow command — possibly the asupersync 0.6 scheduling issue in fr-asupersync06-drain-stall-3xan (asupersync 4d6ec8cfb: Sleep completes early under a cancelled ambient task). Fail-closed is correct; the trigger needs a timestamped reproduction.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
2026-10-13 MEASURED on the pinned asupersync (ts1, release frd run --software-explicit, idle listener + nft rule, 60 s of /proc utime+stime; children = reaped cutime+cstime):
- Baseline: frd 2.28% of a core, children (ip/nft) 1.10%, family 3.38%, RSS 9.2 MB.
- The idle task wakes every 10 ms. Each cycle is about 30 syscalls across 3 threads: 3 EAGAIN recvfrom, about 10 epoll_ctl, 3 epoll_pwait, timerfd_settime and sched_yield. That is ~300 recvfrom/s.
- The 10 ms comes from FOUR safety-net pulses in the same task, not from asupersync:
  - native_connection/host.rs Scoped (10 ms);
  - host/serial.rs Guard (10 ms re-arm);
  - session_agent/.../dispatch.rs first-peer wait (10 ms);
  - fr-tailnet certificate.rs SERVICE_PULSE (10 ms).
  Each re-checks state that has no waker: policy revision, ingress/identity status, route close, credential status.
- Slowing only the Scoped pulse while idle: 2.00% (another 10 ms pulse still drives the task).
- All four at 250 ms (experiment): frd 0.55%, children 1.12%, family 1.67%; ~64 wakes/s remain, dominated by the 500 ms ingress refresh (LocalAPI HTTP + ip + nft spawns, 38 execs per 10 s).
NEXT (in progress): idle-aware pulses, with 10 ms kept once a peer is accepted (Scoped re-polls the whole task). Reaching <0.1% for the family needs the ingress refresh changed: interval, or netlink instead of ip/nft spawns. That is a security-posture decision, since it sets how fast rule loss is detected and the node identity validity is 3 s.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 2026-10-15 measurement after the idle-aware pulses (ts2, release frd from ecce132's tree, frd run --encoder software, listening with ingress active, no peer, 60 s of /proc utime+stime): frd itself 0.58% of a core, reaped children (the ip/nft spawns of the 500 ms ingress refresh) 1.53%, family about 2.1%, RSS 9.9 MB. On 10-13 (ts1) the baseline was frd 2.28%, children 1.10%. The process is now 4x lower. The remaining cost is mostly the ingress refresh, which is still the owner's call on interval or netlink. Stopped with SIGTERM: share_ended Cancelled, then stopped.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 2026-10-16: the measurements here are frd with NO peer. With one idle view-only peer on a static desktop, frd's session thread used 84-97% of a core (debug, namespace): a QUIC ACK ping-pong at round-trip speed (~940 packets/s each way on loopback), see fr-r6qp. A prototype asupersync fix cut it to 20.7% and the packet rate from ~2000/s to 85/s. Release numbers are not measured yet.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
2026-11-08: four Ingress(CommandUncertain) ends on a swapping ts2. Two were under strace, with per-command timing; two were untraced, timed by /proc/pressure samples.

Setup: ts2 hosting ts1 with the live harness. frd was 7c40783d, run under `strace -f -tt -e trace=%process,read,write`, so the ip/nft children were traced too. ts2 was at load 69-146 (128 cores) and swapping.

In both runs, one `nft -j -n list table inet frd_...` child hung. Every other ip/nft child finished in 15-40 ms.
- Run 1794114285: 102 ip/nft children in about 15 s, revalidating two frd tables (frd_0cf4..., frd_dd43...). That is 48 ip, 46 `nft list table`, and 8 setup/teardown nft runs (`list tables`, `-f -`). The last two `nft -f -` commits took 0.30 and 0.33 s. One `nft list table` started at 00:05:03.832. By 03.850 it had loaded its libraries and read its config files. It made no further traced syscall and was SIGKILLed at 05.280 (1.449 s). The share ended Listener(Err(Ingress(CommandUncertain))).
- Run 1794113722: same shape. An `nft list table` started at 23:56:07.574, made no traced syscall after loading, and was killed 3.17 s later during teardown. Same share end.

What this shows:
- The command really was still running past the 1 s COMMAND_TIMEOUT. In these two cases, the 2026-10-13 guess that the future was not polled or the timer fired early does not fit.
- Nothing after its config reads was traced. The nft was most likely blocked in its netlink exchange with nf_tables (sendmsg/recvmsg are not in the trace filter), or stalled on a page fault.
- One stuck read-only check ends a live share. That is the fail-closed choice fr-ingress-revalidation-load-qelg names as the owner's call.

Why the stall may be an artifact: without --seccomp-bpf, strace -f stops every syscall of frd and of every child for one tracer process. CommandUncertain ended 2 of 8 traced runs and 0 of 12 untraced A/B runs on the same host the same evening.

Later the same night: two UNTRACED CommandUncertain ends, B7 and B9 of a 20-run A/B series with /proc/pressure sampled every 0.25 s. B7 ended at +35 s and B9 at +40 s. Both came during sustained memory stall: /proc/pressure/memory "full" ran 200-500 ms of every second, against at most 145 ms in any one second of the passing runs' first 20 s. ts2 was swapping (43 of 63 GB in use). The 13 runs that passed had at most 2.0 s of memory stall over the whole run, one of them at load 147. That points at host memory stalls, which delay a short ip/nft exec or its kernel reply past the 1 s COMMAND_TIMEOUT, rather than at frd failing to poll. No command-level timing exists for these two.

ts2's nftables state is small: 7 tables, 190 ruleset lines, `nft -j list tables inet` takes 34-40 ms. A large ruleset is not the cause.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
2026-11-08 02:35-03:00: 12 untraced live runs (C1-C12), ts2 host to ts1, AUDIO=0. Host frd eff459ed (share_ended now names a controlled viewer's ending), with the 7c40783d bundle's workers and the 3ad437d9 client. /proc/pressure was sampled every 0.25 s from C7 on; C1-C6 have no samples, so any stall there is unknown, not zero.

- Passed every row: C1-C4, C7, C8, C10 (7 of 12). Each logged viewer_end Some(Publication(Session(Renewal(PeerClosed)))): the controller closed its own session.
- C9: client Media(InvalidRoutes) after control_keys, control_wheel, clipboard and file_send had passed (7 of 11 rows). The host's viewer_end for the first time: Some(Publication(Session(ControlRenewal(Transport(Expired))))). No host memory stall around the end (0-5 ms/s). The client logged 4 input suspensions (832 ms).
- C5 and C12: start Desktop(Publication(Media(Worker(Deadline)))). C12 is the first PSI-timed one: 3.3 s of memory "full" stall in its first 20 s, up to 274 ms in one second. C5 is untimed, but the 5-minute memory "full" average read 23.8% just after C6.
- C11: frd never listened. Ingress setup ended Listener(Ingress(CommandUncertain)) during 100-540 ms/s of memory stall (the sampler itself missed seconds). The client got host_not_answering. C6: Ingress(CommandUncertain) mid-run, untimed.

Reading:
- Start Worker(Deadline) (fr-6zrg) and CommandUncertain (icui/qelg) now have timed cases during ts2 memory stalls: C12; B7, B9 and C11. Neither class has occurred in a timed calm period.
- InvalidRoutes (45mn) does not follow host memory stall: C9 was calm. Its host-side ending was a transport expiry in the host's control renewal. One run cannot order the two ends. If the host ended first, the client's InvalidRoutes is how it read the host's teardown, and that would fall under izv6's misleading codes. If the client stopped servicing first, the host's renewal records would expire the same way.

Leftovers (nothing deleted):
- ts2: ~/fr_work/live_6zrg updated in place to eff459ed (12 changed files; it was 7c40783d); target_6zrg rebuilt frd; new ~/fr_work/live_bin_vend (copied frd, hardlinked workers); ~/fr_work/vend_src (tar + results); psi.log grew (sampler PID 1091101 stopped); 12 more ~/fr_live run dirs with root-owned drop/.
- ts1: 12 more ~/fr_live run dirs.

comments.author: ClaudeOpus55
comments.text:
2026-11-10 (Claude; macOS measurements, no code changed). mac-studio, the LaunchAgent frd (a63edaec build), listening on [fd7a:...]:8443 with no viewer, load 21-29 on 36 cores. CPU time from ps over 1 h 45 min (19:06:19 to about 20:58):
- frd: 1.37% of one core. Per thread (ps -M, 20 s): main/async thread 0.5%; the rest is spread over five threads at 0.1-0.25% each.
- fr-observation-indicator (the menu bar helper): 0.71%.
- fr-session-monitor: 0.90%. It makes about 50 native reads per second (SessionGetInfo x2, CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary and display queries, each turn).
- Spawned children: the 500 ms ingress refresh runs `/sbin/ifconfig -v utunN` (4.1 ms CPU each) and `/usr/sbin/sysctl -n ...` (2.6 ms CPU each) via strong_host::qualified/enforced. Measured with getrusage over 50 runs. At two refreshes per second that is about 1.3% of a core. frd's own spawn work in the main thread comes on top.
- Family total: about 4.3% of a core, against the <0.1% target.
`sample` (10 s) shows nearly every frd thread waiting. Three threads sit in nanosleep loops: fr-session-monitor's supervisor (5 ms TURN between 50 ms queries), fr-observation-ui (5 ms TURN) and one unnamed thread. The main thread's active samples are mostly posix_spawn.
Options, largest first:
(1) The ingress refresh interval on macOS. The boundary is kernel state (check_interface/forwarding sysctls, utun flags and address). Changing it needs root, and nothing notifies. 2 s would cut the children to about 0.3%. A PF_ROUTE socket (nix already supports AddressFamily::Route on this target) could re-qualify the interface on RTM_* messages, with a slower poll kept for the sysctls. Owner's call, as noted on 10-13.
(2) Poll the helper pipes with rustix::event::poll instead of 5 ms sleep loops: roughly 0.5%.
(3) Slower helper cadences would also save about 1%. But they spend the stall margin that already runs out under overload (3 EvidenceExpired ends today, see fr-uvji), so I would not.

comments.author: ClaudeOpus55
comments.text:
2026-11-11 (Claude; measurements only, no code changed): bcfa50a8 on macOS.

Setup: mac-studio, load ~25 on 36 cores. Two idle hosts ran side by side, both listening with no viewer:
- the installed LaunchAgent frd (e8362992 build, before bcfa50a8) on 8443;
- a main build (fba24e2b, includes bcfa50a8) on 8444, same flags and helpers.
CPU time comes from ps. It counts each process itself, not its spawned ifconfig/sysctl children, which were about 1.3% of a core on 11-10.

What changed (sample, 5 s each):
- In the old frd, three threads loop on 5 ms nanosleep: fr-observation-ui, fr-session-monitor and one unnamed thread.
- In the new frd, fr-observation-ui and fr-session-monitor block in poll.
- The unnamed thread still loops in both. It is the liveness watcher in host_indicator.rs drive() (`thread::sleep(5 ms)` at line 198). It locks the indicator state and reads the clock about 200 times a second for the whole run. Per-thread ps puts it near 0.1% of a core.

CPU, percent of one core:
| window | build | frd | indicator | session monitor | total |
| 03:20:47-03:23:30 (163 s) | old | 1.39 | 0.70 | 1.04 | 3.13 |
| same window | new | 1.22 | 0.85 | 1.04 | 3.11 |
| 03:10:13-03:12:17 (124 s) | old | 1.52 | 0.73 | 0.97 | 3.22 |
| same window | new | 1.40 | 0.96 | 1.07 | 3.43 |
| 03:10:13-03:20:11 (598 s) | new | 1.25 | 0.88 | 1.02 | 3.15 |
top agreed: frd 1.4 old vs 1.2 new; both families about 3.0-3.1. The longer old window was cut short: the installed frd ended on EvidenceExpired at 03:18 and launchd restarted it (runs 84 -> 85).

Reading:
- bcfa50a8 does what it says. Two of the three sleep loops are gone, and frd's own CPU drops by about 0.15 points.
- The family total does not move measurably. My 11-10 estimate of "roughly 0.5%" for this option was too high.
- The helpers' own reads (SessionGetInfo, CGSession and display queries, the 50 ms cadence) are their cost. bcfa50a8 does not touch them.

What is left toward <0.1%, largest first:
1. The 500 ms ingress refresh: about 1.3% of a core in spawned children. Interval or PF_ROUTE is the owner's call (11-10 note).
2. The helpers' 50 ms query cadence: 1.7-1.9% across both helpers. It is tied to the evidence budget (VALID_NS 500 ms, CHECK_BUDGET 250 ms), which already lapses under overload (fr-uvji), so I would not slow it.
3. The drive() watcher: about 0.1%. Expiry can only happen at the recorded deadline, so it could park until then and be unparked at teardown, instead of polling every 5 ms. Not done: small gain on a liveness path.

Leftover: /Users/jemanuel/Library/Caches/FrankenRemoteLive/fba24e2b holds the main build used here. Nothing deleted. The 8444 instance was stopped with SIGINT (share ended: Cancelled, stopped), and its helpers exited.

comments.author: ClaudeOpus55
comments.text:
2026-11-11 (Claude), macOS numbers (mac-studio, release builds, idle: listening, no viewer). Measured with ps cputime over 30 s and 43 min.

- Installed frd: 0.44 s per 30 s (1.5% of a core); 36 s over 43 min (1.4%).
- Three idle test frds: about 1.0% each.
- The fr-session-monitor helper beside each: about 1.0% (25.7 s over 43 min).
So a Mac host idles at about 2.5% of a core with its helper. The target is 0.1%.

What wakes it, from one 5 s `sample` of an idle test host: the main thread was busy in 12 of 2,926 samples, 5 of them in posix_spawnp. On macOS the ingress refresh (fr-tailnet local/ingress/strong_host.rs) runs `/sbin/ifconfig -v utunN` and `/usr/sbin/sysctl -n` every 500 ms (REFRESH_INTERVAL), which is 4 process spawns a second. Their own CPU is not in frd's figure.

In-process reads would keep the same checks at the same interval: sysctlbyname for check_interface/forwarding, and getifaddrs plus SIOCGIFAFLAG_IN6 for the address flags. But fr-tailnet forbids unsafe code, and nix has no sysctl or IPv6 address-flag call. So this needs a decision on where that FFI lives. Not changed.

title: Image clipboard as a negotiated optional capability over the transfer channel
description:
WHY: v1.4 makes text clipboard sync default-on; image clipboard (screenshots, copied figures) is the natural next expectation. It is explicitly a NEGOTIATED optional capability carried over the bounded file-transfer channel — never smuggled through the 64 KiB control parser — so it must not be lost as a feature nor allowed to bloat the core clipboard path.

title: Under host load one slow ingress revalidation ends a live share, reported as Ingress(Closed)
description:
LIVE 2026-10-14 at 12b8a18 (ts2 frd run --encoder nvenc as host, ts1 fr connect --control). ts2 was at load 55-190 from unrelated jobs.
- Two controlled sessions ended ~20 s in. The client reported `transport_deadline_expired`; the host's share ended `Listener(Err(Ingress(Closed)))` (`ingress_unenforced`).
- A third run never admitted the client: the share ended `Listener(Err(Ingress(Identity(Timeout))))`.
- `tailscale status` on ts2 answered in 20-130 ms when measured just after.
- The same build passed the full live check with ts1 (load ~6) as host and trj as client: keys, wheel, clipboard both ways including a pre-session host copy, file sha256, `stopped`.

Mechanism (code reading, fr-tailnet local/ingress.rs):
- Every protection revalidation, and the LocalAPI identity lookup inside it, is bounded at 1 s (`TailnetPolicy::lookup_timeout`, ingress `COMMAND_TIMEOUT`).
- "Failure or dropped work retires the original lifetime": one slow revalidation on a loaded host retires the lease, and frd stops sharing (fail closed).
- After that, every `Lease::check` returns `Error::Closed` because `state.active` is false. The run reports `Ingress(Closed)`, not the cause that retired it (here most likely the same Identity(Timeout) or a slow nft/ip read-back).

Two separate defects:
1. Diagnosability: keep the first retiring error in the lease state and report it (Ingress(Identity(Timeout)), command timeout, ...), not Closed. No policy change.
2. Robustness (owner decision): a single transient revalidation failure under load ends a live share. Options: retry within the protection's remaining validity before retiring; a longer bound for the periodic revalidation than for admission; fewer process spawns per refresh (fr-idle-frd-cpu-icui, which would also reduce load sensitivity). Fail-closed on genuine identity or ingress change must stay.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Mechanism from the code (not yet confirmed by a run): fr-wire RecordStream starts a record's deadline (record_lifetime, 2 s) at its FIRST byte and never extends it. A stalled prefix or an unconsumed complete record expires the same way (stream.rs push/tick). fr-transport QuicRecords::check ticks every inbound stream's framing and closes the WHOLE connection on any error (quic.rs ~715-724). So a 64 KiB Bulk Files record that trickles in over more than 2 s ends the controlled session. Bulk is served after Critical and media, which happens when the client's sender is busy or the host's receive loop stalls. The diagnostic (buffered=0, blocked=false) fits a partially received record rather than one the host held back. Fix shape: an expired NON-critical inbound stream fails that stream and its transfer with a typed reason, leaving the connection up. Or the Files sender sizes records to the path rate so one record lands well inside the lifetime. Related: fr-xfvs (send starvation on lossy paths).

Why <= 1 looks sound to me (your call): publication is renameat only and never writes to the destination's inode. An
inode with no links cannot alias another file, so the refusal the check exists for, nlink >= 2, is unchanged.

title: fr completion reports audio_output_failed after reference recoveries although playback resumed
description:
WHAT: after reference recoveries in a controlled session with audio, fr's completion reports "audio_absence":"audio_output_failed" while "audio_active":true and playback demonstrably resumed after every recovery. Evidence (namespace e2e real_audio::controlled::every_lane_with_audio_recovers_from_repeated_capture_stalls, c6c0123, ts1, 3/3 runs): audio_output_resets 3, audio_frames_submitted 160, a NEW host tone detected at the client sink after each of three 400 ms capture stalls; still audio_absence "audio_output_failed". Sessions without a recovery report audio_absence null (e.g. 108 frames, resets 0).

WHERE: fr-native fr_cli linux/output/threaded.rs. Output::account() records `reason(fault)` whenever the current job's Shared.fault != 0; code 1 (Fault::Native) maps to "audio_output_failed". Candidate Native sites: native()'s `result.is_err() && !stopped` (configure or service failing for a NEW generation), Exit::drop with clean=false (cleanup not retired within CLEANUP 2 s), service()'s TryRecvError::Disconnected. A recovery calls reset() (resets += 1) and the next generation starts a new job; which one records Native is not yet known (needs a diagnostic build printing the fault site).

WHY IT MATTERS: the completion is the user-facing truth record; it must not name a failure that did not end playback (typed refusals, no misleading codes). Conversely, if one generation really failed and a later one recovered, the report should say so distinctly (e.g. a per-generation failure count), not as the session's absence reason.

ACCEPTANCE: the e2e above asserts audio_absence null (or a distinct recovered-failure field) with a planted negative; a unit test in output/threaded.rs for reset + new generation without a Native fault.
close_reason: Acceptance met at exact revision beaa5c71: namespace suite 109/109 (e2e asserts audio_absence null) + unit test with planted negative. Self-verified only; see comment.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 2026-10-16 diagnostic build on ts1 (prints only, not committed): every recovery logs 'native worker failed while live' (threaded.rs native(): result.is_err() && !stopped -> Fault::Native), and the failing step is the INNER playout Output::service (audio.rs ~237) returning Err while permission is still live (live=true, until-now ~100 ms). Not the packet validation, not the reply channel, not an unclean worker exit. Inner service can fail in Stage::Starting (device.poll, ProcessDecoder::new, PulsePlayout::with_decoder), Configuring (poll_ready, acknowledge) or Playing (playout.service). One per recovery (2-3 per run), right before the outer reset() stops the job, so the first fault recorded is Native and absent() keeps it for the whole session. Next step: a diagnostic that names the stage and the underlying DeviceError/decoder error; then either classify an error caused by the lane's own replacement as a reset (not a failure), or record it per generation.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 2026-10-16 root cause (second diagnostic, prints only): the failing call is the Playing stage's playout.service -> device_clock -> the Pulse output's validate_submission_clock (fr-native pulse/output.rs ~214-243), which fails closed with DeviceError::Expired when a submitted chunk would play at or after its valid_until (the freshness contract: stale audio is never played). During a capture stall plus reference recovery the client's queued audio goes stale, so each old generation's playout ends Device(Expired) (logged 3/3 per run). The worker turns that into Fault::Native (threaded.rs native(): result.is_err() && !stopped), reason(1) = audio_output_failed, and Report::absent keeps the first reason for the whole session, while the next generation plays normally. So the behaviour is right (no late audio) but the report misclassifies a recovered freshness expiry as an output failure. Fix shape for whoever takes it: carry the playout error kind out of native() (an Expired fault distinct from Native, e.g. audio_output_late), and decide whether audio_absence should name an end that a later generation recovered from (it is first-reason-wins today). Touches the audio freshness/reporting design, so not changed tonight.

title: Live NVENC host: cleanup_failed (source/launch/ingress) after a controlled share; an interrupted transfer leaves a .fr-part staging file
description:

In 2 of 4 controlled sessions, after the share ended frd reported {"event":"cleanup_failed","stage":"source"}, then "launch" and "ingress", and exited {"code":"cleanup_incomplete","detail":"frd-run: Cleanup(\"source\")"}. The other two runs stopped cleanly. Software-encoder runs on ts1 the same evening did not show it.

Consequence seen: after one such run a 100,000-byte, fully received file stayed in the drop directory as a private staging file (.fr-part-<hex>, root-owned, mode 600) instead of being published or removed. fr-files' PendingFile removes its staging file on drop, so the receiving owner was never dropped; nothing removes such leftovers later.

title: Clipboard lane ends for the grant on a view suspension instead of pausing (files fixed in a804f15)
description:
Known limit of fr-suspend-o37f (stale view suspends control input, plan 11.3).

The input lane now suspends on a view lapse. The clipboard bridge and file transfer lanes still check their authorization with the terminal semantics (live control or view readiness), so a transfer in flight during a lapse ends the session.

Wanted: those lanes pause while suspended, and resume or refuse with a typed reason, never silently.
- Clipboard content must not be applied to a host whose view is suspended.
- A file transfer's own deadlines still bound it.

Test: namespace e2e freezing capture during a clipboard sync and during a file send.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 2026-10-14 (47c0c60): the viewer's clipboard and file lanes now PAUSE for any turn in which the input view gate refuses (e.g. a submitted picture awaiting its visibility callback) instead of servicing the lane, whose refused transport authorization closed the connection; expect_clipboard registers with live control instead of requiring a picture visible at that instant. Found live (NVENC 1080p, ts2->ts1): Control(Clipboard(Transport(Unauthorized))) within seconds, or no clipboard all session. Two regression tests with planted negatives. Under a stale-view SUSPENSION the gate passes and the clipboard projection already ends for the grant (InputClient::suspend), so suspension no longer ends the session through these lanes. Still open per this bead: the namespace e2e freezing capture during a clipboard sync and a file send; live clipboard sync not yet re-verified.

Any clipboard admission failure first seen during session I/O no longer closes the connection, on the viewer (drive authorize) and on the host (InputServices::permitted includes Bridge::permits_io): its authority (including a host view lapse, InputMonitor ViewUnready), an item's deadline, a newer local copy, a switch, a stopped worker. The transport retires only the clipboard pair in that same checked operation (stream reset, queued bytes and retransmissions dropped), and the session continues. The completion now names it (clipboard_ended). Namespace e2e real_clipboard::a_copy_that_outlives_its_deadline_on_a_slow_path_ends_the_clipboard_not_control (120 ms netem) covers the drive-time fault path. comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 2026-10-14 analysis: the file side of this bead no longer ends sessions in production. Viewer: files::Slot::permits_io refuses during I/O only for (a) an unfinished attachment handshake past its deadline (check_pending), which must fence the parent because a half-acknowledged pair cannot be retired alone, or (b) a revoked fr_files::session::Permission. Production never revokes it: the only constructors are Permission::new(true) in frd native_files.rs:179 and streaming/files.rs:36, and nothing in fr-native, fr-client or frd calls revoke(). A sender failure during service already cancels only the file lane. Host: running/controlled/files.rs Slot::permitted refuses only a pending exchange's own error, for the same reason; HostReceiver failures retire only the pair. The view-lapse case this bead describes was the old terminal authorization path, which 47c0c60/145df7c replaced. Remaining: the namespace e2e that freezes capture (SIGSTOP the host media worker, as real_control's capture-stall test does) during a clipboard sync and during a file send.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
2026-10-16: the acceptance e2e (freeze capture during a file send and during clipboard use) written and run on ts1.

FILES - fixed in a804f15. real_files::a_capture_stall_mid_transfer_recovers_and_still_delivers_the_file (32 MiB; host capture SIGSTOPped 400 ms once the file is staging) failed before: files_refused host_permission after a 505 ms suspension, while control resumed on the same lease (recovered_streams 1). Cause: fr-files HostReceiver::check sampled InputMonitor::deadline, which refuses ControlStatus::Suspended with ViewUnready, and check() closes the receiver on any authority error. The disk worker calls service() on every timer turn, so a suspension also ended an IDLE file lane for the rest of the lease. The viewer already kept its file lane sending through a suspension (gate()), so the two ends disagreed. Fix: session.rs standing() = the control status deadline, Live or Suspended; revocation, lease/observation expiry and a suspension past MAX_VIEW_SUSPENSION stay terminal. Unit tests (planted negative = the old rule: Authority(ViewUnready)); e2e 3/3 after (suspensions 374/397/481 ms, sha256 match, durable). Deviation from this bead's 'pause' wording: file bytes CONTINUE through a suspension instead of pausing. Staging into and publishing in the drop directory is not an action on the view (plan 11.3 suspends input), and it matches the viewer's existing behavior.

CLIPBOARD - still ends for the grant on any suspension; confirmed. e2e (kept out of tree: copy works, 400 ms stall, control resumes, copy both ways): clipboard_ended clipboard_authority_ended after a 461 ms suspension; the post-stall copy never crossed. Live: 5 of 33 ts2->ts1 sessions on the 2026-10-15 evening (degraded hosts) ended the clipboard on a ~1 s suspension (input_suspended_ms 1019-1227); the other 28 had no suspension.
Why it is not a small fix: the client's clipboard projection proves the host lease only by tickets (host_until = ticket expires_at; 1 s ticket lifetime). The host issues no ticket while suspended, and the minimum suspension is ~1 s (fr-68qp), so the proof lapses in any suspension. PresentedInput::suspend therefore retires the projection deliberately ('never revived'), and the host's ClipboardSession::check treats ViewUnready as terminal too.
Design sketch for a pause: (1) a second lease proof that continues through a suspension: the host's authenticated control Challenge (scope Control(lease), deadline_micros) keeps flowing while suspended (ControlLease::deadline returns the suspension until), so the projection could take its deadline like a ticket's; no wire change. (2) The projection reports a suspended view as NotReady (non-terminal) instead of Expired. (3) A non-terminal 'suspended' refusal through fr-core ClipboardSession::check / image.rs, the fr-wire channel session and frd clipboard_quic, so both ends leave records waiting in their routes while suspended (the viewer's service_clipboard already pauses on a refusing gate). Item deadlines still bound an in-flight item. This changes the projection's security model (the other contributor's design), so it is left for that owner; raising to P2 for the live evidence.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 2026-10-16 correction to the comment above. (1) Attribution: the retire-on-suspend rule is this project's own deliberate interim choice from 70a53a8 (fr-suspend-o37f), not the other contributor's design, and this bead already asks for the pause/resume. (2) The design sketch's step 1 is wrong: a control Challenge proves only that the lease was live when it was issued. Its deadline_micros is issue time + authorization_lifetime (3 s), applied only if the response is accepted (fr-core issue_control_challenge/respond_control_challenge), so it cannot authorize clipboard work ahead of time. Viable shape instead: on the client a lapsed proof (view lapse or ticket expiry while suspended) PAUSES the projection (NotReady, non-terminal) and the next authenticated ticket of the SAME lease resumes it, while a different lease, revocation or the 10 s suspension limit stay terminal. On the host a Suspended status pauses the clipboard bridge and session (records wait in their routes, no terminal close), and a host copy made meanwhile is sent as the latest value after resume. Resume waits for the first post-lapse ticket (~1 s minimum, fr-68qp).

title: Client kills a healthy 1080p first decode after a fixed 200 ms native-request ceiling
description:
PROBLEM (LIVE 2026-10-12): every client session from trj (Ubuntu 26.04, 1920x1080 Xvfb) to a 1920x1080 host failed with `session ended without a named reason: Observation(Decoder(Media(Worker(Deadline))))` (native_session_failed), against both the software host (ts1) and the NVENC host (ts2), with old and new client builds alike.
CAUSE (strace): the parent sends the first 35 KB reliable IDR to `fr-media-worker --present`; the healthy worker decodes (~85 ms), converts to BGRA (~50 ms) and starts drawing, and the parent SIGKILLs it at +205 ms. crates/frd/src/media/presentation.rs bounded each native decode/present request by a fixed 200 ms (min'd with the picture's reference deadline); cursor.rs used the same 200 ms for the cursor re-present. For a reliable startup/recovery IDR the picture's own budget is the 2 s recovery window, so the fixed 200 ms made a slow-but-healthy first decode fatal (non-retryable).
FIX: NATIVE_REQUEST_CEILING = 2 s hung-worker ceiling (equal to the default recovery budget), still capped by each picture's reference deadline (datagram pictures stay <= 250 ms after first fragment); the cursor re-present uses the same ceiling.
close_reason: Fixed in ff14b5a: NATIVE_REQUEST_CEILING 2 s capped by the picture's reference deadline; unit test with planted negative on ts1; LIVE: decoder startup passes trj<-ts1 (software) and trj<-ts2 (NVENC), host pixels presented. Remaining streaming fragility is fr-live-client-present-cost-tqu7.

title: Client presenter costs 48-200 ms per 1080p frame (XPutImage, swscale, pipe busy-poll); late pictures end live sessions
description:
PROBLEM (LIVE 2026-10-12, after fr-live-client-present-ceiling-3m19): sessions from trj (busy 128-thread host, load 18-57 from other builds) to 1920x1080 hosts pass decoder startup and present (software ts1 and NVENC ts2 both shown on the client), then often end `Observation(Streaming(Media(Worker(Deadline))))`: a streamed picture's native decode+present outlives its reference deadline (<= 250 ms after first fragment), the worker is killed and the session ends (any decode error is fatal in viewer/streaming.rs).
MEASURED (strace of the worker pipe, one 28 s session at ~1 picture/s): 48-200 ms per present request (median ~125 ms) for 1080p; first IDR ~85 ms decode + ~50 ms BGRA conversion + X11 draw. Presentation uses XPutImage over the X socket (x11_image.c:236, ~8.3 MB per frame); MIT-SHM is used only for capture (X11_SHARED_MEMORY.md). perf: worker time in memmove/memset and libswscale; the parent `fr` busy-polls the worker pipe (non-blocking read every ~0.3 ms with 1 ms sleeps) and used more CPU than the worker.
WORK (measure first, each with a before/after number on the same host): (1) present via MIT-SHM (fd-based attach as capture does; extend the worker seccomp policy minimally) instead of XPutImage; (2) check whether sws_setColorspaceDetails forces a slow swscale path for same-size YUV420P->BGRA; avoid per-frame 8 MB memset; (3) replace the parent's pipe busy-poll with readiness; (4) decide whether a late streamed picture should be skipped with recovery instead of ending the session (design: PRESENTATION_FRESHNESS.md / RECOVERY_*.md).
ACCEPTANCE: 1080p view-only session trj<-ts1 runs 5 minutes without a Worker(Deadline) end at the same trj load; per-present p95 reported.
notes:
2026-10-30: measured and implemented a fixed four-slice HEVC decoder pool. The worker prepares only checked geometry before the existing TSYNC filter, then admits/configures remote hvcC after every thread is confined; no frame threading, added picture queue, deadline change or syscall permission. Final production bridge on FFmpeg 6.1.1, 65 actual 1080p software-encoded pictures and 60 paired warmed samples: moving desktop single/four p50 10.207/5.243 ms, p95 16.329/9.996 ms; noise p50 10.795/7.083 ms, p95 14.471/11.403 ms. Timings cover native decode+BGRA before confinement, not visible/transport latency. Each row also passed untimed confined decoding and all-four-thread file/socket/clone3 denials. Small/cropped rows, byte identity, reference history, allocation limits, malformed configuration and legacy constructor passed. Poisoned cropped buffers exposed and fixed an existing unwritten right-edge bug (1366-wide images); restoring the old converter flag fails the alpha regression. Actual same-source native library/worker compiled, all seven reference tests and strict Clippy passed. All three original Xvfb worker tests subsequently passed on e67bdfc: native/fitted pixel readback across reference-only history, cursor recomposition from the last displayed frame, and malformed decode-only refusal with worker termination and unchanged pixels. All ten reference_decode test bodies have now run successfully; the private-pipe test driver is not full frd supervisor or tailnet qualification. See scripts/test_native_decoder.sh, WORKER_SANDBOX.md and IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md. The broad bead remains open: five-minute loaded two-machine acceptance and the separate upstream idle QUIC loop have not been qualified/fixed by these native measurements.
2026-11-06 native buffer safety: the unchanged 95d010e production bridge reproducibly overwrote the trailing canary of an exact 1368x768 BGRA output with real FFmpeg 6.1.1 (expected 90, observed 35, SIGABRT). The fast SSSE3 converter writes sixteen-pixel groups, so the decoder now selects accurate general conversion whenever visible width is not divisible by sixteen. The existing scalar whole-frame path, exact Rust output capacity and four-slice HEVC decoder remain; no extra frame buffer or copy is added. The encoder also ends its swscale frame operation unconditionally before releasing the borrowed BGRA source, including partial setup failures.
The final production bridge and targeted regression tests passed scripts/test_native_decoder.sh: six small/cropped/uneven geometry cases and both 1080p workloads, exact pixels, opaque alpha, leading/trailing canaries, configuration/allocation refusals, reference-only and legacy decoding, and EPERM on all four slice-thread indices under the unchanged filter. Final bridge SHA256 500087d4100b49e76554c340bac6f5a2c2fb17e2a870fd8fa5ad9ab8444c70d1; test SHA256 0658cf4a46b29eb008758e0cca9c2623707135b9588cc3901031c9a267192621. Independent source review passed. The actual fr-media-worker built with the exact pinned toolchain and --locked --offline --no-default-features --features linux-media, then passed strict scoped Clippy (-D warnings), both exit 0 with unchanged source hashes. Pinned cargo fmt --all --check, docs and whitespace checks passed. This session did not complete full-workspace tests: earlier attempts were killed while compiling unchanged Asupersync within the shared 8 GiB limit; UBS is unavailable. No dependency pin, manifest or lockfile changed.
Parallel conversion experiments were rejected: a separate swscale pool increased desktop conversion cost; reusing HEVC workers improved conversion-only timing but did not establish lower complete decode-plus-conversion latency. The final experiment increased total p95 from 11.942 to 13.174 ms for desktop and 11.821 to 13.383 ms for noise. No experimental pool, band dispatcher or policy remains in the shipped source. IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md records the scoped measurements. Keep this bead in progress: the five-minute loaded two-machine acceptance is still outstanding; this change makes no latency or live-session qualification claim.

title: Live --control fails: client presenter worker exits 1 after launch, masked as Connection(Cancelled)/native_session_failed
description:
PROBLEM: `fr connect NODE --control --experimental-native --display only` fails live within ~3.5 s with stderr `fr: session ended without a named reason: Connection(Cancelled)` and code `native_session_failed`; host logs `peer_finished Err(Cancelled)` and `share_ended ... Report { source_renewals: 0, viewers: { admitted: 1, finished: 0, failed: 1 } }`. The SAME binaries/host succeed with `--view-only` (sessions run to the client timeout and end `cancelled` with cleanup completed). Happens with and without --clipboard; host was `frd run ... --input-agent <abs>/fr-input-agent [--clipboard --files DIR]` (startup probe passed, `"control":true`).

WHAT IS KNOWN: strace -f on the client shows its `fr-media-worker --present --parent-pid N` child writes a few FRW0 IPC records to stdout and then `exit_group(1)` with nothing on stderr; the parent then SIGKILLs the worker's process group and the connection scope is cancelled, which is all the client reports. No PacketTooLarge on either side (instrumented). Root cause NOT yet isolated (candidates: control-mode presenter configuration/geometry/fit, viewer-input window setup on the client display, or a host record the presenter rejects in a controlled share). Run used scratch transport fixes (asupersync main + 1200-byte host datagram cap) needed for any live session.

WORK: (1) make the presenter worker report a typed refusal record before exiting and propagate it to the client completion (no unnamed Cancelled); (2) find and fix the control-mode failure; (3) add the live control row (host pointer moves to the client's xdotool coordinates; key/button events observed) to the live lane.
ACCEPTANCE: live control session where an independent X client on the host observes the pointer at the client-driven position; the failure, if any, carries a specific typed reason.

LIVE TEST CONTEXT (2026-10-12, HEAD 596da32, first-ever two-machine run): hosts ts1=thinkstation1 (Ubuntu 26.04, x86_64) and ts2=thinkstation2 (Ubuntu 25.10, GTX 1070, driver 580.159.03), client trj=threadripperje (Ubuntu 26.04); all same untagged tailnet user, HTTPS certs enabled (Let's Encrypt chain YE1 -> Root YE -> ISRG Root X2 -> X1 cross-sign, 3,418 bytes DER). title: Host QUIC endpoint uses 1500-byte datagrams above tailscale0 MTU 1280 and the client's 1200-byte receive size
description:
PROBLEM: Even with asupersync's handshake split (companion bead), the host chunks its flight by its OWN endpoint limit: crates/fr-transport/src/quic/accept.rs `MAX_DATAGRAM = 1500` (line ~37) is used for the endpoint `max_packet_size: MAX_DATAGRAM + 1` (~202) and the advertised `max_udp_payload_size` (~113). Observed on tailscale0: host sends 1200 + 1438 + 1439 + 969-byte datagrams. tailscale0 MTU is 1280 (max IPv4 UDP payload 1252; IPv6 1232) and the CLIENT endpoint (crates/fr-tailnet/src/local/dial.rs endpoint_config, max_packet_size 1200) cannot receive datagrams over 1200 bytes, so the client never completes and times out (`tailnet_lookup_timeout`, host `HandshakeTimeout`).

EXPERIMENT: changing only the listener endpoint to `max_packet_size: 1200 + 1` made live catalog fetch and a 38-second view-only session work (pixel diff vs host: 0.14% of pixels at 10% fuzz, PSNR 39.4 dB; differences = cursor overlay, moving clock hand, codec edges).

WORK: define one transport datagram policy shared by host and client: never exceed the peer's advertised max_udp_payload_size, start at the QUIC 1200-byte floor, and only grow after path-MTU validation (or keep 1200 on tailnet, whose MTU is 1280). Keep the discovery sentinel/oversize detection separate from the send size. Verify that 1-RTT media/record packets also stay within the policy. Test on an MTU-1280 link.
ACCEPTANCE: live handshake + view session over tailscale0 with no datagram > 1252 bytes (IPv4) / 1232 (IPv6) in a tcpdump; namespace test on an MTU-1280 veth.

title: First dial to an idle peer fails IdentityChanged: PeerTarget::same_identity compares Tailscale path state (CurAddr/Relay)

title: Live controlled sessions end on the client with Media(InvalidRoutes) after the grant (8 of 50 runs on 11-08)
description:
LIVE 2026-11-08 (ts2 frd run --encoder software hosting ts1 fr connect --control, standard harness scripts/live/two_node.sh, AUDIO=0). The most frequent live end that night: 8 of 50 runs. The client printed:

  fr: session ended without a named reason: Observation(Streaming(Control(Media(InvalidRoutes)))); local: Some(Observer(Streaming(Control(Media(InvalidRoutes)))))

Each time the completion reported refused / native_session_failed, and the host reported peer_finished Err(Cancelled) with viewers failed 1.

Runs:
- 4 with the host's capture worker under a light strace wrapper: D4, D6, D7, D9, at 00:17-00:27 local.
- 4 of 32 untraced runs: B6 and B8 (frd 7c40783d), A7 and A8 (frd 3ad437d9), at 00:40-00:52. So both frd builds hit it.
- Every one ended after control_granted, 11-44 s into the session. B6, A7 and A8 had already lost the viewer window before the harness's colour sample.

Host context: ts2 has 128 cores and was swapping. All runs took the direct path. In the untraced series, runs 1-11 passed 11/11 rows (B4 aside: 10/11, keys). The next 7 all failed: B6, A7, A8 and B8 with this error; A9 host_control_revoked; B7 and B9 Ingress(CommandUncertain). The last two (A10, B10) passed again.

That time clustering is not explained by host memory pressure or load:
- Over each run's first 20 s, which contains every one of these ends (+11-13 s), /proc/pressure/memory "full" totalled 49, 10, 56 and 381 ms (B6, A7, A8, B8). Passing runs had 0-934 ms.
- Heavy stall (8-28 s per run) came after the ends, while the harness waited out its timeouts.
- Load at their starts was 56-72, at or below the low end of the passing calm hour's 64-116.
Cause of the clustering: unknown.

Which check: unknown. media_quic::Error::InvalidRoutes has about 20 sources. The likely one is NegotiatedMedia::check (media_quic/negotiated.rs:150). It requires every configuration, recovery and video stream route and the video datagram route to be live. ControlledViewer::check_inner (controlled.rs ~482) runs it on every turn while `self.media` is Some.

Hypothesis (code reading only; no host-side recovery has been seen in these runs). A host-initiated reference recovery resets the old media streams. If a client turn runs check_inner after the transport dropped those routes but before the client reads the host's failure notice, check() fails with InvalidRoutes. The notice is what leads to take_media_for_recovery (continuation.rs:698), which detaches the media first ("Recovery may already have retired the old media routes"). That would fit the D runs, where the strace-wrapped worker slows capture. It does not explain the untraced ones, which ended without a memory stall.

Against the hypothesis, from D6's light worker trace (execve/write only):
- Pictures came every 0.1-1.0 s with 2-19 KB bodies until +5.29 s after the worker's execve, the same pattern as the passing D3. There was no IDR-sized burst before the end.
- The worker was killed at epoch 1794115248.340, 76 ms before the client's completion timestamp (…248.416).
So it is not known which side ended first. Either the client hit InvalidRoutes and closed, and the host then reported its peer as Err(Cancelled). Or the host cancelled the viewer (Err(Cancelled) comes from several cx.checkpoint() points in native_connection/host), and its teardown reset the routes the client then tripped on.

To confirm or refute: a host-side record of why the peer was cancelled, and whether a reference recovery started, in a failing run. Or a fixture that applies the host's stream resets before the failure notice is read.

Related: fr-4vf5 (reference recovery for controlled sessions; its capture-stall e2e passes 10/10 in the namespace), fr-rc2-live-lane-a6ug (live lane), fr-live-misleading-client-codes-izv6 (this reaches the user as native_session_failed / "without a named reason").

Not shown: the cause; whether view-only sessions hit it; any rate on an unloaded host.
notes: 2026-11-08 source-identified recovery race, implementation in progress: streaming::network can queue/send the RecoveryRequest and receive authenticated host stream resets in one turn while ControlledViewer still owns old NegotiatedMedia. Its post-I/O check previously required live media before the outer loop could take_media_for_recovery, especially while native decode/presentation was still draining. Recovery service now enters the original input owner's recovery fence before that turn, and controlled checks validate only exact retiring old routes in that state. The ordinary strict route check remains outside recovery. Native-drain dispatch discards obsolete media/old progress and holds successor handshake/feedback records for the existing continuation; original session, grant, resource charge and recovery deadline remain mandatory. Added actual localhost TLS/UDP regressions retaining a ReceivedPicture in simulated native work across peer retirement plus a negative unsolicited-reset case. Native codec completion and authority fixtures are not hardware/live proof. Pinned formatting/docs pass; new runtime test execution is pending because local cargo check/test is killed compiling unchanged pinned Asupersync under the shared memory cap. Existing GitHub verification will provide capable-runner results. This is a concrete causal source fix, not proof that it explains every live InvalidRoutes occurrence. Keep the bead in progress until new regressions execute and the original two-machine control stress scenario is rerun.

comments.text:
2026-11-08, code reading plus one change (eff459ed).

Why the host log could not say how the viewer ended: controlled_outcome (session_agent/source/desktop/native/dispatch.rs) turned a controlled viewer's own ending into a bare count and dropped the error. B8's share_ended reads `viewers: Statistics { admitted: 1, finished: 0, failed: 1 }`. failed with finished 0 means the host saw a viewer-side ending that was not a peer departure (a departure would count finished 1, failed 0). eff459ed keeps that ending: share_ended now ends with `viewer_end: Some(...)`, as typed codes. A live frd at eff459ed is building on ts2 for the next runs.

Where the client's InvalidRoutes can come from, in controlled.rs:
- check_inner -> NegotiatedMedia::check, on every turn while media is attached. It fails InvalidRoutes once a media pair's route is retired. fr-transport retires a media pair locally when the peer resets it, sends STOP_SENDING, or FINs it (QuicRecords::service_optional_retirements). The host does that only in recovery (shared_publisher::advance_recovery -> begin_replacement -> retire_media_set). That recovery starts from the client's own request, and the client's serve loop detaches its media (take_media_for_recovery) as soon as that request is Requested, before any host reset can be read. So a host recovery reset racing check_inner is not shown by the code. My earlier hypothesis is weaker than I wrote.
- take_media_for_recovery -> retiring_viewer_routes returns InvalidRoutes when the connection is already closed. A host close that lands while the client starts a recovery would surface as InvalidRoutes rather than Closed or the host's named reason.
- install_recovered_media -> check on the replacement media.
- progress_route (in the turn's feedback path).
Which of these fired is not known. The client's error does not say, and the host's did not either until eff459ed.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
2026-11-08: what C9's host ending means (code reading, plus the ts1-ts2 RTT).

Host side: viewer_end ControlRenewal(Transport(Expired)). In fr-transport, a reliable record the host admits must be staged and acknowledged by max(send-by, admission + delivery_allowance_us), or QuicRecords::check returns Expired and closes the connection (quic.rs ~700, the senders' `until`). delivery_allowance_us = clamp(7 x (srtt + max(4 x rttvar, 1 ms) + 25 ms), 250 ms, 2 s). ts1 to ts2 measures 1.4 ms (mdev 0.4), so the allowance sits at its 250 ms floor. Unless a renewal record's own send-by is later, the session ends if the client's acknowledgement is 250 ms late.

So C9's host end most likely means the client, or the path, did not acknowledge a control-renewal record within about 250 ms. The client's own QUIC stack sends those ACKs when its loop services the socket, so a client stall that long would do it. The client logged 4 input suspensions (832 ms) in C9. But stalls of that size are common in runs that pass: A4 had 12 suspensions (1920 ms), B4 10 (2386 ms), C10 4 (867 ms). Not every lapse ends a session, and a view lapse can come from host capture rather than client stalls. So this ties nothing down yet.

Next evidence that would settle it:
- which record expired (stream role, admission age) in the host's Expired; or
- the client's loop latency around the end.
Changing the 250 ms floor is a liveness/fail-closed trade-off for the owner, not a quiet fix.

comments.text:
2026-11-08, correcting my note above. C9's host ending is better read as a result of the client's own end, not of a late host wake.

The viewer's error path closes with QuicRecords::close. That only drops the native connection: asupersync's UDP connection has no Drop that sends anything. So no CONNECTION_CLOSE reaches the host. This is fr-t4lj's remaining gap, for a role with no armed registration. The host learns only when its next control-renewal challenge (1 s cadence) goes unacknowledged, 250 ms after it is admitted: ControlRenewal(Transport(Expired)).

The reverse order cannot produce the client's error. After the host's Expired, its close sends nothing. A route retires on the client only on a peer RESET_STREAM, STOP_SENDING or FIN, or a local request, while the connection is open. Once the connection is closed, NegotiatedMedia::check returns Closed, not InvalidRoutes. So the client failed first. The cause is in the client, or in a retirement frame the host sent earlier. This also removes the "host ended first, and InvalidRoutes is the client's misleading reading of it" (izv6) option from the C-series note.

title: Live failures reach the client with misleading codes: busy host -> tailnet_lookup_timeout, host worker refusal -> host_not_heard, local presenter exit -> unnamed
description:

1. comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Investigation 2026-10-12 (code paths, no change yet):
(1) BUSY is blocked on the transport, not the refusal: while a share is active the one UDP socket belongs to NativeQuicUdpConnection, which silently drops datagrams from any other source (asupersync ee72b66 src/net/quic_native/udp_connection.rs:1065-1067: packets_dropped += 1; continue). A second Listener::bind fails (socket held) and QuicUdpEndpointConfig has no reuse-port/connect option; project code forbids unsafe. Options: (a) upstream reuse-port + connect() the established socket so a second unconnected socket receives new flows; (b) upstream bounded hand-off of foreign-source datagrams; (c) migrate to ManagedQuicEndpoint (large). Once packets arrive: one refusal attempt at a time via run_on_protected_listener_gated (TLS -> WhoIs/scope admission -> Host::from_admitted), then a new Host::refuse(reason) on opening::refusal::send; NOT Incoming::serve_host (a Warm view-only route would admit a late joiner). Only admitted peers may be told busy. fr_wire::refusal::Reason has no Busy (closest ResourceLimit=11 -> host_resource_limit). Note README row 26 'later viewers are refused Busy' is library-only behavior (dispatch::Error::Busy drops the Host without a record).
(2) HOST PREPARATION FAILURE: happens after SessionOpened/Detached, so Refused is not allowed (PROTOCOL_REFUSAL.md). Usable record: Closed{reason: HostFailure(7)} via the armed closing report (closure_reporting.rs:82-104). Three blockers: closure_reporting.rs:51-55 honours only reasons 1 and 6; fallback becomes HostStopping because the session Cx is cancelled; native_connection/host/desktop.rs Run::poll drops the listener after one poll so the report never sends. Client: refusal::session maps only Protocol(Refused); RemoteClosed(Closed) is unmapped (-> native_session_failed).
