title: Live QUIC handshake fails with real Tailscale certs: asupersync =0.5.0 sends each handshake CRYPTO segment as one oversized datagram (udp_send)
description:
PROBLEM: Every live connection fails during the QUIC/TLS handshake. Host logs `peer_finished ... Err(Accept(Handshake))`; client reports `tls_identity_refused` (then `tailnet_lookup_timeout` on retries). Instrumented host error: `Handshake(CryptoProviderFailure { provider: "rustls-quic-handshake", code: "udp_send" })`.

ROOT CAUSE: asupersync 0.5.0 `QuicHandshakeDriver::send_pending_flight` (src/net/quic_native/handshake_driver.rs ~1192-1222) assembles each pending TLS handshake segment into ONE long-header packet. The server's Handshake-level flight (EncryptedExtensions + 4-certificate Tailscale/Let's Encrypt chain + CertificateVerify + Finished) is ~3.6 KB, so `QuicUdpEndpoint::send_batch` returns `PacketTooLarge` (packet > max_packet_size 1501) and the handshake fails. tcpdump on tailscale0 shows the host answering each Initial with a single 1200-byte packet and never sending the rest of the flight.

UPSTREAM FIX EXISTS (unreleased): asupersync main 82b3e34b3 (2026-10-06) "a handshake whose certificate chain is larger than one datagram completes, its Handshake-level CRYPTO split into packet-sized datagrams (br-asupersync-5f1fcj)" plus 872e7c4e0 (anti-amplification). crates.io still has only 0.5.0. Scratch experiment: FrankenRemote HEAD builds unchanged against asupersync main (0.6.0, path dependency) and, together with the datagram cap in the companion bead, completes live handshakes (fr displays + fr connect --view-only worked ts1 -> trj).

WORK: publish asupersync 0.6.x (or another qualified revision) and adopt it in the workspace (see fr-rc-transport-adopt-pin-7bn; AGENTS forbids the mutable sibling checkout as the pin). Add a regression test whose server identity uses a >3 KB multi-certificate chain over a link with a 1280-byte MTU (e.g. a veth/TUN pair in the namespace suite with mtu 1280), so a single-datagram handshake can never pass again.
ACCEPTANCE: live `fr displays` from a second tailnet node succeeds against an unpatched-transport HEAD with a real Tailscale certificate; namespace regression test with large chain + MTU 1280 passes (and fails if the upstream split is reverted).

LIVE TEST CONTEXT (2026-10-12, HEAD 596da32, first-ever two-machine run): hosts ts1=thinkstation1 (Ubuntu 26.04, x86_64) and ts2=thinkstation2 (Ubuntu 25.10, GTX 1070, driver 580.159.03), client trj=threadripperje (Ubuntu 26.04); all same untagged tailnet user, HTTPS certs enabled (Let's Encrypt chain YE1 -> Root YE -> ISRG Root X2 -> X1 cross-sign, 3,418 bytes DER). Client: `fr connect <NODE_ID> --view-only|--control --experimental-native --display only --x-display :72 --worker <abs>/fr-media-worker --json` on a second Xvfb. Evidence level: LIVE (real tailnet, real Tailscale cert, real WhoIs), Xvfb displays (no compositor/HiDPI claim). title: Control sessions end on their own under heavy host load (namespace e2e, with and without the delivery allowance)
description:
Observed 2026-09-30 in the namespace e2e suite on a shared host at load 110-160. Five runs with the QUIC delivery allowance had 6 failures; four baseline runs without it had 1. Every failure is one class: a CONTROL session ended on its own before the harness expected any end.

Observed ends:
- Baseline: an unnamed native_session_failed just before a user window close (real_files::a_host_without_files...).
- Allowance build, as typed host reports:
  - host_control_revoked/local_revoke during setup (await_control), in a_stopped_controller... and the wheel test;
  - host_session_ended/session_ended just before a user close (control cursor test, twice);
  - view_stale before the host's lock revoke (real_session_lifetime lock test).

Why the labels differ: with the allowance the connection outlives a late ACK, so the host's typed report is delivered instead of dying with the connection.

The root cause is unknown. Candidates:
(a) The host view lapse. A presented report delayed past observed + 250 ms under CPU stalls makes fr-core end a held lease (terminal), giving AuthorityEnded and then SessionEnded.
(b) The executor's sharing indicator stops (MAP_TIMEOUT 2 s, Hidden, WindowLost or NativeFailure). fr-input-agent reports ANY indicator stop as a LocalRevoke datagram, so frd names it local_revoke. That is a MISLABEL: a mapping timeout is not a user's local revoke. The indicator's StopReason should travel in the signal and map to a specific typed reason.

Tools: scratchpad wt-diag + target-diag carry FRDIAG prints for the agent-loop and watchdog authority deadline error, non-Ready presented decisions, and transport expiry source. Run the full suite repeatedly until one failure shows its reason chain.
acceptance_criteria: The reason chain for each observed end class is identified from diagnostics. An indicator stop is reported with its own typed reason, never as local_revoke unless the user used it. Either the load-induced ends are fixed, or the suite's expectations are reworded to the real typed behavior with evidence. Five consecutive full-suite runs at load >100 have no unexplained control end.
notes:
2026-09-30 later: three full suites on the allowance build with both harness fixes (capture_workers scoped, close_viewer) and diagnostic prints were all 63/63. Part C final build: 63/63 as well. The earlier allowance-run failures clustered before the harness fixes. The hub reports a normal window close as viewer 'failed' (Session(Renewal(PeerClosed))), so share stats 'failed 1' are not by themselves an error.
2026-09-30 70a53a8: candidate (a) is addressed. A host view lapse under CPU stalls now suspends input instead of ending the lease. A capture stalled past the 250 ms reference horizon no longer ends the session when its result is unchanged (a late ENCODED result still does: new bead).

Candidate (b), extended: the streaming Fence in frd session_startup/running/streaming.rs stops native control with StopReason::LocalRevoke whenever the host's media/network loop ends with an error, so a media failure reaches the client as host_control_revoked/local_revoke. Seen twice at 40 ms + 5% loss in the matrix. The fence should carry the real cause.

title: Keep native session lifetime deadlines enforceable during stalled launch and evidence races
description:
The existing read-only session monitor can block indefinitely opening a FIFO before checking its file type. The host's startup waiter relies entirely on child wakeups, so a stuck launch cannot trigger the documented original opening deadline. Shared evidence acceptance also checks and updates its lifetime in separate critical sections, leaving a clock-regression/terminal-publication race.

Implement nonblocking image validation, an independent bounded startup wakeup, and atomic original-evidence validation/terminal publication. Preserve Linux wire behavior, single-child custody and explicit cleanup reporting. Regressions must cover a real FIFO, a startup without child wakeups, clock rollback, expiry, terminal replies and no resurrection. Plan sections 7, 19 and 24; AGENTS authority/freshness rules.
notes: Implemented serialized original-evidence state, terminal publication before returning, nonblocking image validation and independently timed host startup wait. Focused exact-source verification passed 18 evidence/process tests; two Asupersync/host-run tests remain blocked locally because rustc compiling the unchanged pinned runtime is killed by SIGKILL (peak RSS about 2.2 GiB). Full workspace and native qualification are not claimed; tracking remains in progress pending those gates.

title: Bound initial negotiation framing before payload allocation
description: Source review at 02cabc95: RecordStream::negotiation accepts ordinary caller maxima up to 65536 through new_inner, while PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION.md and negotiation::MAX_RECORD cap initial records at 4096. A header announcing 4097 bytes can allocate before later codec refusal. Keep the initial framer at the normative limit regardless of caller maximum; verify header-only overlimit refusal has zero payload allocation and preserves poisoning/bounds behavior. Add constructor and boundary regressions without weakening ordinary attached-record limits. Owning contract: plan sections17.2/19.3, PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION, fr-wire stream framing. This report is source-inferred until reproduced.

title: macOS workspace does not compile (fr-tailnet trust, frd service_install, fr closure); no macOS lane; frd install writes an always-refusing LaunchAgent
description:
PROBLEM: `cargo build --workspace` fails on macOS (verified on mac-studio, M5 Ultra, macOS 27.0.1, pinned nightly):
1. crates/fr-tailnet/src/trust.rs:4 `use asupersync::tls` but fr-tailnet declares asupersync only for target_os = "linux" (Cargo.toml) while `pub mod trust` is ungated.
2. crates/frd/src/service_install/options.rs:120 `use crate::host_policy::options::RunOptions` — host_policy is Linux-only.
3. crates/fr-native/src/bin/fr_cli/closure.rs:4 `use frd::session_startup::ViewerCloseOutcome` — Linux-only.
A 3-part fix verified in a scratch copy (both fr and frd then build on macOS): (a) fr-tailnet asupersync{tls} dependency for cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32")) (the trust reader is platform-neutral); (b) split validate_run_args so non-Linux returns UnsupportedPlatform before parsing run options; (c) cfg(target_os = "linux") on the ViewerCloseOutcome import, its From impl and closure tests.
After the fix every macOS command is an honest typed refusal: `fr hosts|doctor|connect` -> platform_unavailable (exit 2), `frd run` -> "frd host runtime is currently supported on Linux" (exit 2), `frd status --json` -> refusal platform_unavailable (exit 1; inconsistent exit code). Verified identically on mac-mini-max (macOS 26.2) and mac-mini-old (26.5). BUT `frd install --user` on macOS writes a LaunchAgent plist that runs `frd run`, which always refuses — installer should refuse instead.
WORK: land the 3-part fix; add a macOS `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` CI/local lane (all 39 workflows are Ubuntu-only; no RCH Darwin worker) so macOS compile breaks are caught; make frd install refuse on platforms whose host runtime is unavailable; align refusal exit codes.

title: macOS host control: fr-input-agent CGEvent executor, local indicator and revoke; frd run --input-agent on macOS
description:
WHY: The owner's goal is native Macs and Windows machines that control each other. A Mac host can be viewed (fr-p1-host-macos-vif) but not controlled: `frd run --input-agent` is refused on macOS ("remote control of a Mac is not implemented yet"). fr-5a4w covers the other direction (a Mac controlling a remote).

SCOPE: a macOS role for the existing per-lease `fr-input-agent` process, behind the same frd InputSession owner and the unchanged `fr_core::input_submission::process` protocol (Hello/Prepare/Submit/Release/Cancel/Cleanup/Stop/Probe; Fence/LocalRevoke/IndicatorFailed).
- Injection: CoreGraphics events on the session tap from a private event source, every one tagged in kCGEventSourceUserData.
  - Keys: HID usage page 0x07 mapped to kVK through the inverse of fr-native macos_keys, with tracked modifier flags.
  - Pointer: absolute in the catalog's encoded-pixel desktop space, mapped to CG global points; drags while a button is held; click state for double clicks.
  - Scroll: pixel and line.
  - Text: CGEventKeyboardSetUnicodeString.
- Refused before Ready unless AXIsProcessTrusted() is true (events would otherwise be dropped silently). The executor must also find the CG display whose encoded bounds equal Hello's bounds.
- Indicator: an always-on-top AppKit panel shown for the whole lease. Ready is sent only after it is on screen. A click on Stop counts as LocalRevoke only when the event is not one of ours (no tag). If the panel closes without the local user, that is IndicatorFailed.
- Lifetime:
  - The parent-exit watch and a panic or exit path both post releases for every held key and button.
  - Stop releases everything before replying Stopped.
  - The deadline, fence and revoke are re-checked immediately before every post.
- frd: launch the agent on macOS (no DISPLAY), probe its capabilities, take InputBounds from the catalog entry of the selected display, and lift the macOS `--input-agent` refusal.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Unit tests on macOS:
  - the key-map inverse is total and unique over macos_keys;
  - pixel-to-point mapping at 5120x2880 over 3072x1728 and at 1:1;
  - held-state bookkeeping, including emergency release;
  - click-state sequencing;
  - the protocol executor's refusals (no Accessibility, mismatched bounds, fenced or expired Submit).
- A real event test that posts tagged events to the test's own pid only and reads them back, so the owner's cursor never moves.
- Live, with the owner's explicit go-ahead, since it injects into their Mac: a Linux or Mac viewer with --control moves, clicks, scrolls and types into a test window. A real local click on Stop ends control as LocalRevoke. Killing frd releases held input.
- CI: Linux all-features builds still pass; the macOS lane still compiles.
notes:
2026-11-09 precise-scroll extension: added optional native-input-pixel-scroll v1 negotiation, offered by the host only after the real executor probe and by the Mac controller only when requested. Legacy peers keep the rest of the control profile. GrantBroker freezes the original selected marker and rejects unselected precise requests through the real wire decoder before approval or seat admission. Precise AppKit distances preserve both axes and signed16.16 logical units through Quartz pixel scrolling; no Retina scaling or guessed pixel-to-line conversion. Whole-line wheel input remains separate. Bounded sub-unit carry keeps the oldest capture timestamp and resets on other actions, mode changes, expiry/refusal or producer retirement. A fixed native/client clock correlation preserves original capture time for all queued Mac input. Unsupported, expired and invalid scrolls are counted without sending remote input; completion retains those counts alongside file and close evidence.
Validation: actual fr-wire suite311pass plus strict all-target Clippy; actual fr-client native_profile20pass; exact production Mac input/key/display/scroll policy20pass plus strict Clippy; exact production broker selection decoder3pass with real fr-core/fr-wire plus strict Clippy. Native tests now read back continuous mode, fractional fields, point fields, flags and position and check final-authority refusal/cancellation via process-local Quartz events. Those native tests, the new Objective-C SDK build and target-application smoothness are NOT executed in this Linux environment. Full frd/native integration remains blocked by the unchanged pinned Asup build resource limit. Keep in_progress; portable verification does not extend live Mac qualification.

title: A controller's deliberate close sometimes ends revoked/host_control_failure instead of stopped
description:
FOUND 2026-10-13 (ts1 namespace e2e under the tailnet-path emulation, FR_NS_SUDO=1, TMPDIR=/tmp).

real_control_cursor::fr_connect_control_draws_the_host_cursor_once_as_the_local_pointer_or_the_overlay passes every behavioural stage (local owner, host-moved overlay, follow, pointer left). Then, after the test closes the viewer window, fr's completion is sometimes
{outcome: revoked, error.code: host_control_failure, revocation: {reason: host_failure, cleanup_stage: fenced, effect_stage: unknown}}
instead of outcome stopped (assert at real_control_cursor.rs:231). That is an authenticated LeaseRevoked(HostFailure) received after a NORMAL user close: a misleading code.

The host's ShareEnded reports viewers {admitted: 1, finished: 0, failed: 1}. A second, rarer mode fails earlier: the test's WM close gets BadWindow (real_media.rs:152), i.e. the viewer window was already gone.

NOT a regression from this week's host changes: alternating runs of the same test give
- ff3099a (before a496ec9): 2/6
- HEAD 7722316: 2/6
- HEAD + idle pulses b47a271: 1/6 and 3/6
Same failure text everywhere.

LIKELY MECHANISM (to confirm with host-side cause logging):
- session_startup/running/streaming.rs fail() -> failure_reason(): a serve that fails while authority is live is StopReason::NativeFailure, which revocation.rs maps to Reason::HostFailure.
- The first stop reason wins (input_watchdog Control::stop compare_exchange).
- The host only names ClientDisconnected when the ACTIONS route ends (input_quic.rs receive_ended).
- So if the controller's orderly close ends another route first (media feedback, renewal, view readiness), and the host's serve fails on that before the actions FIN is processed, the lease is revoked as HostFailure and the still-connected client hears it.
- Other first-writer candidates: input_agent.rs native_failed() (the fr-input-agent child lost during teardown) and the native thread's exit stop(NativeFailure) at input_agent.rs:179.

WORK:
- Log the serve error and the first StopReason at the host; reproduce with the e2e (fails ~50%).
- Make a peer-initiated teardown map to ClientDisconnected/SessionEnded (never HostFailure) without masking real host failures.
- Planted negative: the e2e passes 10/10, and a real host media failure still reports host_failure.
Related: fr-live-misleading-client-codes-izv6 (other misleading codes), fr-t4lj (typed close codes).
close_reason: Fixed in 5d25287. The ROOT CAUSE differs from the mechanism hypothesised when this bead was filed. It was not the serve failing on a route end: on Ubuntu 26.04 Xvfb, XFixesGetCursorImage returns NULL (no X error) at teardown as the cursor's owning client disconnects, measured 9 of 10 runs at that branch. cursor::snapshot mapped NULL to NativeError::Allocation, so the capture worker refused ReadCursor. The host's capture producer then failed, Fence::fail recorded NativeFailure first (live authority), and the client got LeaseRevoked(HostFailure) when it lost the race with its own stop. A NULL image is now transient NeedInput. ts1 e2e real_control_cursor: 10/10 with the instrumented equivalent; 9/10 with the final worker, whose one failure was a startup native_session_failed, not the teardown. Before: about 4 in 6 runs failed at teardown at HEAD and at ff3099a. ts2 (25.10) never showed it (6/6). Remaining design question, not done here: any ReadCursor refusal still ends the whole share as a host failure; the cursor is advisory.

title: verify-* workflows cannot finish: verify.sh fast at -j1 exceeds their 25-30 min timeouts (15 nightly); the 11 unscheduled ones lack libxcb-render0-dev
description:
OWNER DECISION NEEDED. The nightly verify-* workflows cannot finish inside their timeouts, even after 4df6c0a9.

What 4df6c0a9 fixed: cargo's fetch of Asupersync's git history took 18-24 min in every CI job. With `[unstable] git.shallow_deps` it takes 15-16 s on GitHub runners: 22:57:37->22:57:53 in run 42308451213 and 22:58:27->22:58:42 in 42308517114. It also added `apt-get update` to four workflows that installed without it. Two of them (held-state, control-renewal) failed with apt 404s on 11-06; clock-sync and ticket-renewal had the same gap. In 42308517114 the install step succeeded where 42239588357 had exited 100.

What it did not fix:

1. TIME BUDGET. 26 workflows run `./scripts/verify.sh fast` before their own check: 15 scheduled nightly, and 11 that run only on a push to their own file or on dispatch. That is fmt, check, clippy, test and examples over the whole workspace with --all-features, the same work rust-verification does on every push to main. They set CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 and timeout-minutes 25 or 30. Measured in dispatched verify-held-state run 42308517114 at 4df6c0a9:
   - fetch 15 s;
   - check finished 4m16s;
   - clippy 1m38s;
   - the test build began at 23:04:38 and was still compiling at 23:22:56, when the 25-minute timeout cancelled the job.

   For comparison, rust-verification at CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 takes 19.5 min for its Tests step alone (459a94b9: 21:00:57->21:20:27). Before 4df6c0a9, 17 of the 19 scheduled runs on 11-06 were cancelled at their timeout (the 19 are these 15 plus four nightlies that skip verify.sh fast), and verify-reconciled-capture had not passed in 12 nights. They will keep timing out, now in the test build instead of the fetch.
   Options:
   - (A) Raise timeout-minutes to about 60. That is up to about 15 runner-hours a night.
   - (B) Drop `verify.sh fast` from the nightlies and keep each one's targeted check. Rust-verification already gates the workspace on every push.
   - (C) Fold the nightlies into fewer jobs that share one build.
   - Even with time, `verify.sh fast` exits nonzero on the known receiver_load probe flake (fr-rc-media-wire-controller-qej; 3 of the last 4 rust-verification test lanes).

2. MISSING BUILD PACKAGE. The 11 unscheduled workflows do not install libxcb-render0-dev (all 15 scheduled ones do), so no nightly breaks on it; a dispatch or a push to one of those files does:
   - broker-control, capture-discovery, clock-sync, controlled-host, input-attachment, media-delivery,
   - negotiated-input-join, relative-input, session-clock, session-startup, streaming-host.

   fr-native's linux-viewer-input feature compiles src/viewer_cursor.c, which includes <xcb/render.h>, so an all-features build panics in build.rs. Seen in verify-clock-sync 42308451213 at 4df6c0a9 ("install XCB RENDER development headers (libxcb-render0-dev)"). The fix is one package name per file. It is NOT pushed yet: each of those 11 workflows runs on a push to its own file, so the push would start 11 runs of about 25 min that would then time out under item 1. Apply it together with the item 1 decision.

The package lists have drifted. Next to rust-verification's list, the nightly lists also lack pipewire, pipewire-bin, nftables, iproute2 and xfonts-base, which are runtime tools for specific lanes. libxcb1-dev arrives through libx11-dev. One shared list, a composite action like .github/actions/build-swap or the scripts/builder image, would end this class of break.

Evidence: run IDs above; trj fetch timings in 4df6c0a9's message.

title: frd --encoder nvenc fails on real NVIDIA hardware: refs=1 rejected by hevc_nvenc, then NVENC pic_timing SEI rejected by HEVC admission
description:
PROBLEM: `frd run --encoder nvenc` has never worked on real hardware. Live on ts2 (GTX 1070 Pascal, driver 580.159.03, Ubuntu FFmpeg 7.1 / libavcodec 61.19.101): the capture worker loads libcuda/libnvidia-encode/libnvcuvid and opens /dev/nvidia0, then the share ends `Preparation(Media(Worker(WorkerRefused(Unsupported))))`; the client only sees `host_not_heard`.

ROOT CAUSE 1: crates/fr-native/src/bridge.c fr_encoder_new sets `c->refs=1` for every backend. hevc_nvenc treats an explicit refs as a multiple-reference-frame request: ffmpeg CLI with the bridge's exact options prints "Multiple reference frames are not supported by the device" / "No capable devices found". Same options without -refs encode valid HEVC Main 1920x1080 yuv420p that decodes cleanly.
ROOT CAUSE 2 (after a scratch fix that skips refs for NVENC): the share then ends `WorkerRefused(NativeFailure)`. NVENC emits a prefix SEI (NAL 39) with payloadType 1 (pic_timing) on every frame (60/60 frames), but crates/fr-media/src/hevc/mod.rs `user_data_sei` (~272-292) admits only payloadType 5 (user_data_unregistered), so the host's own encoder output fails HEVC admission. (VAAPI was not tested; no VAAPI device in the loop.)

WORK: do not set refs for hevc_nvenc (use the NVENC-specific option set; verify max_num_ref_frames stays 1 via the produced SPS); strip or suppress non-baseline SEI on the HOST before admission (e.g. NVENC config or a bounded NAL filter in the worker) rather than widening admission; then run a live NVENC session and record GPU encoder stats (nvidia-smi encoder.stats) and pixel readback. Add a capability probe that does a real encode+admission at `frd run` startup so this fails at startup with a typed reason instead of per viewer.
ACCEPTANCE: live NVENC session ts2 -> trj with pixels verified and nvidia-smi showing an active encoder session; startup probe refuses with a specific reason on unsupported hardware.

LIVE TEST CONTEXT (2026-10-12, HEAD 596da32, first-ever two-machine run): hosts ts1=thinkstation1 (Ubuntu 26.04, x86_64) and ts2=thinkstation2 (Ubuntu 25.10, GTX 1070, driver 580.159.03), client trj=threadripperje (Ubuntu 26.04); all same untagged tailnet user, HTTPS certs enabled (Let's Encrypt chain YE1 -> Root YE -> ISRG Root X2 -> X1 cross-sign, 3,418 bytes DER). Host: `sudo env DISPLAY=:71 XAUTHORITY=... frd run --software-explicit --display :71 --worker <abs>/fr-media-worker --json` on a cookie-authenticated Xvfb with xlogo/xclock/xeyes. Client: `fr connect <NODE_ID> --view-only|--control --experimental-native --display only --x-display :72 --worker <abs>/fr-media-worker --json` on a second Xvfb. Evidence level: LIVE (real tailnet, real Tailscale cert, real WhoIs), Xvfb displays (no compositor/HiDPI claim). The namespace e2e suite cannot see these defects: its fixture LocalAPI returns static status, its test CA chain is small, and loopback MTU is 64 KiB.
close_reason: Acceptance met. LIVE NVENC session ts2 (GTX 1070) -> ts1 (same client build as trj): 5 minutes, encoder.stats.sessionCount 1 throughout, host/client pixels within 0.13-0.19% (10% fuzz) at each minute. Fixes: c87b578 (refs, encoder SEI, SPS RPS/VUI HRD admission). Startup probe 15d4c21: --encoder nvenc admits a real IDR on ts2 and refuses encoder_unavailable/Unsupported on ts1 (no NVIDIA) in 43 ms; --encoder vaapi refused on ts2. VAAPI on real VAAPI hardware remains unqualified.

comments.author: Codex
comments.text:
Fleet pre-publication source review (2026-10-13 UTC), captured draft based on 5afabc5: strip_encoder_sei in crates/fr-media/src/hevc/mod.rs says output is at most input size and reserves input.len()+4. AnnexB in hevc/nal.rs accepts three-byte start codes, but the filter emits four-byte start codes for every retained NAL. With N retained three-byte-delimited units and no other removed bytes, output is input length + N. For more than four such units, the requested fallible reservation does not establish output capacity; extend_from_slice can then allocate infallibly. MAX_NALS=256 makes the expansion finite, so this is a bounded framing expansion and allocation-contract defect, not an unbounded stream or a measured OOM.

Keep the draft and strict receiver admission, but correct the declared length bound and fallibly reserve the actual maximum normalized output, or preserve delimiter widths. Add a regression with more than four retained three-byte-delimited NALs. Source arithmetic review only; no new GPU/live-session proof and no code edit. The fleet pass is withholding the HEVC group while this remains unresolved.

title: Lossy control: one input record that cannot be sent before its deadline ends control, labelled transport_deadline_expired
description:
FOUND 2026-10-13 (fr-xfvs instrumentation; scratch client printing the final typed failure; ts1 namespace, tailnet-path emulation, controlled impairment matrix with 19e46cc's allowance).

WHAT: in the lossy 40/120 ms RTT control rows the most common end is ControlledViewerError::Expired: the controlled viewer holds one input record that the transport refused with Backpressure (the input stream is stop-and-wait per epoch, so one lost packet holds later records), and check_inner ends the session when that record's until passes (controlled.rs, `self.pending ... t.0 >= p.until`). until = PresentedInput::send_deadline = min(view deadline, ticket deadline, now + receipt timeout). The CLI maps C::Expired to transport_deadline_expired (reconnect::lapse), which tells the user the transport failed when the viewer's own unsent action timed out.

Sample (one matrix run): Control(Expired) 2, Control(View(Input(Stopped(InvalidControl)))) 2, Startup(Expired) 2, Control(Session(Transport(Expired))) 1.

SAFETY CONSTRAINT: never send the action late. title: Phase 0 gate: Chrome and Safari HEVC WebCodecs decode-and-present probe at real geometry
description:
WHY: WebCodecs does not mandate HEVC; support is per browser/OS/hardware combination. The v1.3 decision makes current Chrome and Safari (on combinations where their HEVC path passes) the browser qualification bar — this spike determines what that bar actually covers, before the browser client is built.

SCOPE: In real Chrome and Safari on their supported OS/hardware: generate the complete HEVC codec identifier from actual stream configuration (hvc1/hev1 parameter-set rules consistent with the bytes, 4-byte-length-prefixed NALs in complete access units, exact hvcC); VideoDecoder.isConfigSupported followed by REAL decode-and-present of a representative sequence at real display geometry. Test specifically: a single IDR; one P picture after long idle; the final frame of a burst (some paths retain output when no more frames arrive); recovery after loss; low-cadence presentation. Never call flush() per frame (the flush algorithm requires the next chunk to be a key chunk). Close VideoFrame objects promptly; bound decodeQueueSize AND renderer retention; prefer worker-based decoding where supported. Record hardware-vs-software decode evidence per combination.

ACCEPTANCE: a written support matrix (browser x OS x hardware -> passed/failed/blocked/not tested) with capture of the probe outputs; the emitted-bitstream requirements this imposes on host encoders. Failure meaning: narrow the matrix honestly; no second codec, no per-frame flush hacks. Provenance: plan sections 8.1, 16.3, 23 Phase 0, v1.3 note in section 1.

title: Decision notes: FFmpeg binding family, desktop windowing/shell, mobile FFI mechanism
description:
WHY: The plan bounds three implementation choices as short evidence-based decisions, explicitly forbidding open-ended adapter competitions: the exact FFmpeg wrapper revision, the native GUI/windowing binding, and (per v1.4) the Swift/Kotlin binding mechanism for the shared core.

SCOPE: Three short decision notes, each citing spike evidence: (1) FFmpeg binding — default expectation is a pinned ffmpeg-sys-next-family binding under the project-owned interface, with ffmpeg-next and ffmpeg-the-third evaluated during the build spike; one family chosen, one FFmpeg ABI qualified; no competing wrapper maintained. (2) Desktop windowing/shell — one minimal maintained integration preserving hardware-surface presentation per OS (AppKit/Metal, Win32/D3D, a Linux layer), chosen for surface interop, with accessibility/DPI/input/lifecycle costs counted in the client budget; no Electron/Chromium. (3) Mobile FFI — hand-written C ABI plus maintained Swift package / Kotlin JNI wrapper, or a qualified binding generator; chosen for auditability of the narrow boundary, keeping all logic in Rust.

ACCEPTANCE: each note states the decision, the evidence rows it rests on, the rejected alternatives with one-line reasons, and the revisit condition. Committed under docs/. Provenance: plan sections 9.1, 16.1, 16.2, 25.

title: Phase 0 spike: Linux PipeWire portal -> VAAPI/NVENC HEVC -> decode -> present
description:
WHY: Wayland capture is portal-mediated and DMA-BUF-based; sharing a file descriptor is not synchronization. Buffer ownership, modifiers, plane layout, fences, and cache sync must be handled explicitly, and compositors differ enough that GNOME, KDE, and wlroots-family are separate qualification rows.

SCOPE: Spike: ScreenCast portal session -> PipeWire stream (resolve stream by the strongest identifier offered — recent portal versions expose a PipeWire serial because node IDs are reused) -> GPU-local copy into an owned surface where the compositor buffer cannot be held -> FFmpeg VAAPI (and NVENC where present) HEVC encode -> hardware decode -> native presentation. Clear padding/cropped borders in newly allocated surfaces so stale GPU contents can never become encoded pixels. Run on at least GNOME and KDE; record wlroots-family status even if only as blocked/not-tested.

MEASURE: the standard set (first packet, steady delay, copies, IDR verification, config readback) per compositor row, plus DMA-BUF import/export paths actually used and fence behavior.

ACCEPTANCE: reproducible command + exact compositor/portal/driver versions per row + results + retained failure reasons. Failure narrows the Linux support matrix honestly rather than adding a hidden CPU path. Provenance: plan sections 8.3, 10.1, 11.1, 23 Phase 0.

title: Phase 0 spike: macOS ScreenCaptureKit -> VideoToolbox HEVC -> decode -> present
description:
WHY: The entire product premise on Apple hardware — capture surface to hardware HEVC to hardware decode to GPU presentation with pixels staying on the GPU — must be proven as a small real vertical experiment before any architecture is built around it. Apple's documented low-latency VideoToolbox rate-control mode is H.264-specific; HEVC needs its OWN real-time, hardware-required, no-reordering configuration and measurement.

SCOPE: A standalone spike (spikes/, not crates/) on Apple Silicon: ScreenCaptureKit full-display capture -> (GPU color conversion only if needed) -> VideoToolbox HEVC encode (Main 8-bit 4:2:0, low-delay I/P, no reordering, no lookahead, one previous reference where allowed) -> VideoToolbox decode -> Metal/native-layer presentation. Drive it with a representative desktop-sized moving/text workload, never only a tiny synthetic frame.

MEASURE AND RECORD: time-to-first-packet, steady-state encode delay, decode delay, copy count along the path (zero-copy is a measured property, not a claim), reconfiguration latency, verified independently-decodable IDR on start/reconfigure (observe the emitted bitstream, including effective reorder/reference requirements — an API accepting a request proves nothing), effective configuration readback, behavior at low cadence and after long idle.

title: Phase 0 spike: Windows Desktop Duplication -> FFmpeg hardware HEVC -> decode -> D3D present
description:
WHY: The Windows path runs through a trimmed FFmpeg libavcodec/libavutil boundary to NVENC/AMF/QSV; GPU-surface interop, capture formats, and hybrid-GPU laptops (capture on one adapter, encode on another) are exactly where hardware advantages die. Prove the pipeline before committing to it.

Exercise access-lost, device-removed, resize, and duplication-session exhaustion. Note DuplicateOutput1 format behavior for HDR-to-SDR handling. Wrapper code must implement FFmpeg's real send/receive state machine: drain output for progress, retain reference-counted inputs until ownership permits reuse, distinguish EAGAIN/EOF/device-loss/fatal — never one-packet-per-frame assumptions or sleep-retry.

MEASURE: same set as the macOS spike (first packet, steady delay, copies, IDR verification, config readback), plus capture-device-vs-display-adapter mismatch behavior.

title: Phase 0 gate: OS permission and lifecycle spikes (Wayland tokens, macOS TCC attribution, Windows session/loopback, lock/suspend)
description:
WHY: A daemon cannot erase OS consent boundaries, and permission attribution is packaging-dependent. Discovering these rules after the product is built is how remote-desktop projects die; the plan requires exact capability rows per OS before the architecture hardens.

SCOPE: Wayland: full portal sequence (create RemoteDesktop session, select devices/sources, request clipboard integration BEFORE Start, complete response, obtain restricted PipeWire remote and input connection); restore-token single-use rotation with atomic persistence; returned grants (not requested flags) determine authorization; session agent retains the portal session while delegating only the stream capability to a worker — a worker must never inherit input authority. macOS: signed launchd process family; Screen Recording + Accessibility permission attribution stable across updates and helper layout; protected-content reporting; sleep/wake and fast user switching. Windows: service vs interactive-agent split; Session 0 never treated as the user's desktop; lock/secure-desktop transitions as capability changes; SendInput integrity limits; WASAPI render-endpoint loopback scope (cross-session audio — must be disclosed, never misrepresented as per-user isolation). All platforms: lock/logout/user-switch ends observation and control; suspend/resume as an authority generation boundary.

ACCEPTANCE: a capability row table per OS (capture, pointer, keyboard, restore, clipboard, playback audio) with exact versions and passed/failed/blocked/not-tested; retained scripts; failure reasons. Provenance: plan sections 5.3, 10.1-10.3, 23 Phase 0.

title: Phase 0 gate: qualify one live Asupersync QUIC endpoint composition end to end
description:
WHY: The inspected Asupersync tree exposes a native QUIC alias, but NativeQuicConnection performs no socket I/O, endpoint_api.rs explicitly declines to claim external interoperability, and adapter queues are not a deployable transport. Treating a type alias as a transport is the single largest architectural risk in the plan. This gate decides the native profile.

SCOPE: Choose ONE documented live endpoint composition and qualify its complete packet path: real UDP sockets suspending through the runtime's OS reactor (verify actual suspension per target, not async-looking signatures); TLS 1.3 certificate/hostname verification; negotiated project ALPN; packet protection; stream + DATAGRAM behavior including negotiated DATAGRAM size limits (QUIC's 1200-byte minimum Initial is NOT 1200 bytes of datagram payload; Tailscale's MTU is 1280); retransmission, congestion accounting, pacing; multi-client routing; cancellation; bounded allocations. Interoperate against an INDEPENDENT QUIC/H3 peer in the test harness (test-only dependency, never shipped). Test direct and forced-DERP-relay paths. Loopback tests that manually advance handshake states are not security evidence.

FAILURE MEANING: keep the unqualified path disabled; count bounded upstream Asupersync work against the 15k transport allowance; qualify and label the WSS profile instead. NEVER implement a second QUIC stack or import another runtime.

ACCEPTANCE: reproducible commands, captured interop transcripts, measured behavior under loss, and a written go/no-go with evidence. Provenance: plan sections 4.1, 12.1, 12.4, 23 Phase 0.
close_reason: Gate executed with live-wire evidence: NO-GO for external QUIC interop (3 independent RFC breaks measured: unpadded Initials 288B, pre-HP header parsing, no coalescing), CONDITIONAL for native profile (datagram admission connection-kill at 1180B, busy-poll receive 99% core, ~71% spurious loss at 29ms RTT). Full report spikes/quic-native/RESULTS.md; upstream work filed as fr-5nb, requalification as fr-7yd; fr-p0-webtransport-b9u now depends on fr-5nb.

title: Phase 0 gate: fragmented HEVC loss recovery and authority-expiry spike
description:
WHY: With 1100-byte payloads, a 50 KiB access unit spans 47 datagrams (37.6% chance of losing at least one at 1% independent loss) and a 1 MiB IDR spans 954 (loss near-certain), and 1 MiB takes about 1.68 s to serialize at 5 Mbps. "Drop and send another IDR" is not viable; the recovery design must be proven against real fragmented HEVC before any low-latency claim exists.

SCOPE: A spike combining the wire fragmentation format, deterministic loss/reorder injection, and real encoded HEVC: sender fragment cache bounded by bytes and time; receiver coalesced missing-range requests after a small reordering allowance, clamped in range/retries/frequency/bytes; separate DISPLAY deadline vs REFERENCE-retention deadline (repair a too-old-to-display picture only while it unlocks dependents within the horizon, initial estimate ceil(fps x horizon)+2 pictures, horizon <= 250 ms, clamped to the negotiated 2-12 window and byte budget); dedicated bounded reliable stream for startup/recovery IDRs; only one outstanding recovery per pipeline; the non-circular startup handshake (DecoderConfiguration -> DecoderConfigured [API configured, not first frame] -> RecoveryAccessUnit -> FirstFrameDecoded/PresentedState). Also: queue input through a long stall and prove expired actions do NOT execute afterward, and local revoke fences immediately.

ACCEPTANCE: bounded bytes/metadata asserted (not just queue lengths); stall/recovery behavior measured across loss patterns including a lost final fragment before idle; retained numbers. Failure meaning: no low-latency or safe-control operating point may be claimed. Provenance: plan sections 12.2-12.4, 15.1, 23 Phase 0.
close_reason: Phase 0 fragmented HEVC loss recovery and authority-expiry spike executed and verified with evidence retained in PRESENTATION_FRESHNESS.md. Reproducible command (cargo test -p fr-native --features linux-media,linux-input-agent --test presentation_input) passes all 10 tests. Verified final fragment loss repair (28.0ms elapsed, 114 wire bytes, 29.8KB peak sender cache), entire picture loss repair (29.3ms elapsed, 28.9KB wire bytes), and every-fifth fragment loss with late reference decode (105.7ms elapsed, 5.86KB repair bytes). Verified input authority expiry during stall (1.1s stall triggers TicketExpired, admitted-stage receipt, zero OS submissions, button release cleanup) and explicit local revoke (715us to cleanup readback without network round trip). Feeds the adaptive controller and downstream production loss recovery (fr-p1-loss-recovery-20s).

title: Phase 0 gate: Tailscale identity, membership, scope, and ingress qualification with real fixtures
description:
WHY: The entire authentication story is tailnet admission — FrankenRemote deliberately has no second credential. Same-tailnet membership, user identity for the v1.2 own-user default scope, and actual tunnel ingress must be POSITIVELY provable from the installed Tailscale's authenticated local metadata on tested versions, or admission must refuse.

SCOPE: Qualify LocalAPI/status/WhoIs access per platform installation variant (Linux socket, Windows local transport, macOS Standalone/App Store/CLI). Build real fixtures: two local members with different owners; a tagged member; a shared-in host; an external sharee; a user present in more than one tailnet; a TAGGED HOST (which has no owning user and therefore cannot use the own-user default — must force explicit scope selection). Verify: source address must be one of the node's own addresses (not behind a subnet route); ShareeNode/AltSharerUserID/Sharer interpretation; InNetworkMap alone proves nothing; DNS suffixes/zero-valued sharer fields/email-domain equality are NOT authorization; IPv4+IPv6 ingress binding to tailnet addresses with platform firewall/interface enforcement; behavior on local identity change, key expiry, and policy removal. Missing/ambiguous evidence -> typed refusal tailnet_membership_unverifiable; the app-capability-grant profile is the configured alternative, never an ad hoc allowlist.

title: Phase 0 spike: host virtual-microphone endpoint per OS (PipeWire source, CoreAudio plugin, Windows driver)
description:
WHY: v1.4 makes audio bidirectional. Client-to-host microphone requires a host-side virtual input device that real applications can select; this is trivial on Linux, signed user-space plugin work on macOS, and genuine driver-class work on Windows. The risk must be retired before mic forwarding is promised per OS.

SCOPE: Per OS, create a selectable input device and route a test Opus uplink into a real host application (e.g., a recorder or meeting app): Linux — PipeWire virtual source; macOS — signed user-space CoreAudio server plugin (BlackHole-style architecture; validate the signing/packaging path and TCC interaction); Windows — signed virtual audio endpoint driver (evaluate: own driver vs a vetted existing open component with recorded provenance; either way, it is native non-Rust code counted like other native artifacts, with its own signing chain). Measure added latency per endpoint and device-change behavior.

CONSTRAINTS: no undisclosed third-party driver downloads; where an endpoint cannot be qualified, microphone forwarding ships as a TYPED UNSUPPORTED capability on that host OS — never a fake device.

ACCEPTANCE: per-OS row (created device, app-visible, audio flowed, latency measured, signing path validated) with passed/failed/blocked status and retained evidence; a recommendation for the Windows approach with licensing/provenance notes. Provenance: plan sections 15.4, 23 Phase 0 (v1.4 row).

title: Phase 0 gate: real HTTP/3 WebTransport interop with Chrome (and Safari where available) plus WSS fallback shape
description:
WHY: A queued adapter or self-loopback is not interoperability. The browser profile requires an actual browser completing the HTTP/3/WebTransport handshake against the production-intended listener, and the WSS fallback needs its bounded-credit shape proven early because browser WebSocket has no application receive backpressure.

SCOPE: Against the qualified (or candidate) Asupersync H3 endpoint: real negotiated SETTINGS, extended CONNECT session establishment, HTTP Datagram association, stream prefixes, required capsule handling; pin the exact WebTransport draft/implementation compatibility tested. Datagram size budget computed from inner MTU 1280 minus IP/UDP/QUIC/WebTransport overheads — measure the actual usable payload. Exercise session binding, cancellation, reconnect, and origin-checked establishment. Chrome is the primary target; record Safari WebTransport status (expected gap: Safari may need the WSS profile — that is an accepted, labeled outcome under the v1.3 Chrome+Safari qualification bar). For WSS: prove separately-bound channels, receiver-granted outstanding-byte credit (bufferedAmount reports outbound buffering only), and stale-generation fencing on channel replacement.

ACCEPTANCE: transcript of a real browser handshake + datagram exchange with the tested draft/version pinned; measured payload budget; WSS credit protocol demonstrated; go/no-go with evidence. Failure meaning: label WSS as the browser profile and publish the tested H3 status honestly. Provenance: plan sections 12.1, 12.4, 12.5, 16.4, 23 Phase 0.
close_reason: Passed live Chrome 153 HTTP/3 WebTransport and WSS fallback qualification with 100% verified scenarios (datagrams up to 1150B echoed, uni/bidi streams, 403 origin rejection, WSS credit backpressure and generation fencing). Evidence documented in spikes/webtransport/RESULTS.md.

title: Adaptive quality controller v0: deterministic, hysteretic, pressure-aware
description:
WHY: Phase 1 needs basic rate control that never oscillates and never mistakes encoder stalls for network pressure; the sophisticated tuning is Phase 4, but the deterministic skeleton and measurement honesty land here.

SCOPE: A deterministic controller with hysteresis, bounded step sizes, and minimum dwell times; separate pressure attribution (network vs encoder vs decoder vs presentation) before any setting changes; reduce offered load fast on persistent queue growth, increase slowly after sustained headroom; budget includes keyframes, retransmissions, auxiliary data, audio, and per-viewer shares with a per-host/per-path aggregate ceiling; provisional operating points near 75-85% of a measured sustainable delivery estimate, never from momentary spikes; application-limited samples marked (idle screens are not low link capacity); unknown metrics recorded as unknown, never derived certainty; conservative restart after idle/route-change/reconnect; bounded probe bursts only when queues are healthy; reconfiguration via announced new generation at a clean recovery point unless the backend has a qualified low-stall in-place path; path-change resets estimates.

ACCEPTANCE: controller decisions are a pure function of its logged inputs (replayable — this is the hook Phase 4 diagnostics builds on); lab scenarios for step response, oscillation damping, and pressure misattribution; every decision logged with its input snapshot. Provenance: plan sections 13.1-13.4.
acceptance_criteria: - [x] Unit tests for step/hysteresis/dwell functions; every decision log entry carries its full input snapshot for replay
close_reason: Implemented deterministic, hysteretic, pressure-aware adaptive quality controller v0 with full input snapshot replayability, step/dwell enforcement, and complete unit tests (Plan §13).

title: First desktop client shell: window, hardware-surface presentation, input capture, minimal toolbar
description:
WHY: Phase 1 ends with a human actually using a remote desktop; that requires one real native shell over fr-client, built on the windowing decision note, presenting decoded frames without GPU-to-CPU readback.

SCOPE: For the chosen first client OS: window/session lifecycle, hardware decode output to a native presentation surface (VideoToolbox layer / D3D swapchain per the decision), keyboard and pointer capture including modifier and focus-loss semantics feeding fr-client's sequencing, minimal UI (machine picker fed by discovery-lite or manual FQDN, connect/disconnect, display choice, connection-state indicator, revoke-visible state), local cursor rendering with the single-owner rule, DPI/scale correctness (native pixels when practical, one explicit scaling step), clean teardown releasing held input state.

ACCEPTANCE: a human drives a real remote session end to end; focus loss releases input state (verified in logs); resize and display-scale changes reject stale coordinates until the new geometry generation is acknowledged; e2e script exercising connect/control/revoke/reconnect with screenshots and full logs. title: fr-e2e: scripted end-to-end session harness with structured logging and artifact capture
description:
WHY: Every feature bead's acceptance names e2e scenarios; without one shared harness those become ad-hoc shell scripts with inconsistent logging and no artifact retention. This harness is the runnable spine for all of them — the consumer is every feature bead from Phase 1 on, and the phase gates' fault suites execute through it.

SCOPE: A harness (under fr-lab or a sibling test crate plus scripts/e2e/) that: launches a real frd process family and a real client core (headless client driver first; desktop-shell driving where the platform permits) against a loopback or real tailnet endpoint; scripts scenarios as data (connect, authorize, view, control, inject faults, tear down); captures STRUCTURED logs from every process (host authority transitions, queue depths, per-action input dispositions, recovery events) into a per-run artifact directory with the exact commit, config, and seed; standard fault injectors (kill/stall worker, drop transport, expire tickets, resize display) reusable across scenarios; assertion helpers over the captured logs (e.g. "no input executed after revoke", "queue high-water under N bytes"); every red run reproducible from its artifact bundle with one command.

CONSTRAINTS: real processes and real transports — no mocks presented as live proof; deterministic-lab scenarios stay in fr-lab (this harness is the real-process complement); scenario registration convention documented so each feature bead lands at least one scenario with itself.

ACCEPTANCE: the harness runs a connect/control/revoke/reconnect scenario against the Phase 1 pair with full artifacts; a planted violation (deliberately delayed revoke fence in a test build) is caught by the assertion layer, proving the harness can fail; CI lane wiring documented. Provenance: plan sections 23 Phase 1 gate, 24.2; AGENTS section 7 (evidence discipline).
notes: REALITY-CHECK REMEDIATION (2026-09-23): This bead is THE live lane every other bead's acceptance uses. Build it for real: scripts/live/ drives a real `frd run` on host A and a real `fr` on host B across the tailnet from the same pinned commit (rch exec --job on two tailnet workers, or ssh over the tailnet to lab machines per fr-rc-media-lab-decision-3b5), with Xvfb -auth on both ends for the automatable variant; the client verifies by reading back its own presented window; the host verifies XTest effects via X11 state queries; per-run artifact bundle (commit, both binaries' sha256, tailscale versions, path kind direct/DERP from LocalAPI, structured logs from every process, sanitized screenshots) recorded in the evidence ledger. Fault injectors act on real processes (kill -9 / SIGSTOP the media worker, drop the transport with nftables or tailscale down, expire tickets by stalling the client, resize the Xvfb screen). The existing crates/fr-e2e simulation must be relabeled synthetic (fr-rc-truth-relabel-synthetic-9dz) and is not evidence for this bead. title: Single FFmpeg hardware codec wrapper (the fr-native bridge) behind the media contracts: device-qualified VAAPI/NVENC probe + real send/receive state machine (Linux/Windows)
description:
WHY: Windows and Linux hardware HEVC run through a trimmed FFmpeg libavcodec/libavutil boundary (NVENC/AMF/QSV/VAAPI). This is the project's largest unsafe/foreign surface; it lives in one audited crate behind the fr-media contracts so nothing FFmpeg-shaped ever leaks upward, and so the macOS path never waits on it.

SCOPE: crates/fr-ffi implementing the fr-media Encoder/Decoder contracts over the pinned binding family from the Phase 0 decision note, against the curated FFmpeg build: the REAL send/receive state machine — drain available output to make progress, never assume one packet per submitted frame, never sleep-retry EAGAIN; retain reference-counted inputs until ownership permits reuse; distinguish temporary backpressure, EOF, device loss, and fatal corruption as typed results; end-of-stream draining kept off the per-frame path; compressed input buffers with the alignment/padding the native API requires, allocated via the library's packet/buffer facilities with checked lengths and initialized padding — never a raw unpadded network slice; timestamps, duration, output status, color information, and configuration changes preserved through the wrapper; configure/encode/decode calls off the authority/event-loop thread; all callback contexts and GPU resources alive until completion or contained worker termination; GPU surfaces opaque, hardware-context handling audited; documented pointer provenance, callback threading, buffer ownership, and shutdown order per AGENTS section 3.2.

CONSTRAINTS: one binding family only (no competing wrapper); FFmpeg types never appear in fr-media/session/wire signatures; libraries load from protected package paths only.

ACCEPTANCE: integration tests against the curated build exercising backpressure, drain, device-loss, and hostile-input paths with full state-transition logging; sanitizer lanes (ASan/UBSan where the target permits) green; fuzz the compressed-input boundary with the padded-allocation contract asserted; a leak test across 10k encode/decode cycles. Provenance: plan sections 9.1, 9.2, 19.1.
notes:
REALITY-CHECK REMEDIATION (2026-09-23): RETARGET. There must be ONE FFmpeg wrapper (AGENTS section 8). The working one is crates/fr-native/src/bridge.c + its Rust side (used by fr-media-worker); crates/fr-ffi is an orphan duplicate with silent mock/stub modes and weaker checks (no decoded-frame size/format check before sws_scale, ffmpeg_bridge.c:494-505) and is on the proposed deletion list (fr-rc-budget-owner-decision-56k). Implement the hardware backends (VAAPI/NVENC; QSV/AMF on Windows later) in the fr-native bridge with the real send/receive state machine, device-qualified probe (probe + representative encode/decode, plan 8.2), GPU-surface input where capture allows (DMA-BUF import on Linux after XShm interim), typed EAGAIN/EOF/device-loss/fatal results, and no silent CPU fallback (hardware-required means fail or explicitly select the software profile). Hardware evidence comes only from the lab (fr-rc-media-lab-decision-3b5).

title: fr-client: shared client session core (connect, decode scheduling, freshness, input sequencing, reconnect)
description:
WHY: One Rust core drives desktop, mobile, and browser clients; platform shells stay logic-thin. This crate is that core, and everything the v1.4 mobile apps and the WASM build reuse.

SCOPE: crates/fr-client: connection establishment against fr-transport with certificate/destination verification; session state machine mirroring host authority (never assuming control from media arrival); decoder scheduling honoring reference dependencies with bounded queues; presentation policy — newest ready frame wins, obsolete presentation work discarded, decoded-vs-presented progress reported separately (background/occluded rendering never counts as presentation); view-freshness tracking that suspends input readiness on sustained unknown/stale presentation while read-only diagnostics continue; client-side input capture semantics (ordered actions vs replaceable pointer states, separate sequence spaces, click coordinate barriers, relative checkpoints); reconnect flow — media reconnect may preserve viewing but NEVER silently restores a revoked input lease; a fresh lease and recovery point on resume; viewport/mapping model distinguishing local zoom (client transform only) from host crop (negotiated mapping generation, acknowledged before coordinate input uses it); diagnostics surface.

ACCEPTANCE: unit tests plus lab-driven integration covering reconnect-without-lease-resurrection, stale-view input suspension, and mapping-generation rejection of stale coordinates, with full state-trace logging. Provenance: plan sections 7.1-7.3, 11.3, 14.4, 16.1.

title: fr-media: safe media contracts, capability probing, and the baseline bitstream rules
description:
WHY: FrankenRemote owns the interface, not the codec. A small ownership-aware contract keeps every backend replaceable and keeps codec library types out of session and wire layers forever. This bead is deliberately CONTRACTS-ONLY and depends on nothing platform-specific: the macOS VideoToolbox path consumes these contracts directly, so the Phase 1 Apple vertical is never blocked behind the Windows/Linux FFmpeg binding decision (that wrapper is its own bead, fr-ffi).

SCOPE: crates/fr-media (safe, #![forbid(unsafe_code)]): Encoder, Decoder, GpuSurface (opaque), EncodedAccessUnit, CodecConfiguration, MediaCapabilities; capability probing that encodes/decodes a real representative workload and reads back effective configuration (an API accepting a request proves nothing); probe caching keyed by OS/driver/device identity, invalidated on device loss; live-session admission against current capacity; observable copy counting per path; the baseline bitstream contract every backend must satisfy: HEVC Main 8-bit 4:2:0, no frame reordering, low-delay I/P with one previous reference where allowed, bounded decoded-picture buffering, verified independently-decodable IDR on startup/reconfigure/recovery, provisional max GOP 2 s during ACTIVE encoding only (never waking a static screen), coded dimensions advertised separately from visible crop with initialized padding, SDR default with explicit color primaries/transfer/matrix/range, qualified HDR-to-SDR tone-map or typed refusal (clipped HDR is never labeled SDR support); hardware-required means fail or explicitly select a software profile — never a silent library-internal fallback.

ACCEPTANCE: contract unit tests with a scriptable fake backend (including probe-cache invalidation and admission refusal paths); compile-time/API-review test that no foreign codec type appears in any public fr-media signature; detailed probe logging (device identity, effective config, copy counts). Provenance: plan sections 8.1, 8.2, 9.1.
close_reason: Bounded ProbeCache and device identity metadata, added ProbeReport, verified no foreign codec types in public API, validated EncodedAccessUnit debug privacy, and passed all contract tests and clippy across the workspace.

title: fr-tailnet: LocalAPI identity adapter, admission policy, scope enforcement, ingress binding
description:
WHY: Implements the qualified identity evidence from the Phase 0 gate as the production admission path. The admission policy IS the authentication story.

SCOPE: crates/fr-tailnet: narrow Rust client for the installed Tailscale LocalAPI (or the qualified platform bridge — bounded CLI invocation at setup/admission where that is the supported path; never a shell with peer-supplied arguments, never per-packet subprocesses); internally consistent status/WhoIs snapshots with retry on local identity change; the full admission conjunction — verified current same-tailnet node AND within the locally selected sharing scope (default: nodes of the host's own tailnet user; explicit option: all members/tags) AND allowed by Tailscale policy AND locally enabled sharing AND capability supported AND controller slot AND approval when configured; typed refusals for every failure including tailnet_membership_unverifiable; binding each connection's transport peer address to node identity (own addresses only, not subnet-routed); listeners bound only to current tailnet node addresses with platform ingress enforcement; revalidation on path change; disabled replayable early data; subscription to local Tailscale changes — when identity authority is unavailable, admit nothing new, stop renewing, terminate at recorded deadlines; tagged-host handling (no owning user -> explicit scope selection required); the app-capability grant profile as configured alternative.

title: fr-transport: qualified native QUIC integration with channel semantics and packet budgets
description:
WHY: Turns the Phase 0 transport qualification into the production native profile with the plan's traffic partition, so input can never queue behind bulk bytes and datagrams carry only replaceable media.

SCOPE: crates/fr-transport over the ONE qualified Asupersync endpoint composition: reliable ordered channels for critical input and small session operations; separate bounded channels for clipboard, configuration, cursor shapes, and the bootstrap/recovery stream; datagrams for video access-unit fragments, audio, replaceable pointer state; the file-transfer channel as its own bounded stream class (budgeted, never ahead of input on a shared resource); connection-level flow-control credit reserved for control so bulk cannot starve key-up; payload budget computed from inner MTU 1280 minus IP/UDP/QUIC-protection/DATAGRAM-frame/application-header overheads, qualified on IPv4 and IPv6; no IP fragmentation reliance; compact negotiated stream bindings (session/display/codec-config/recovery/viewport) so datagrams reject stale work cheaply; per-turn poll work limits so codec feedback cannot starve the reactor; 0-RTT application operations disabled.

ACCEPTANCE: integration tests over the lab adapters plus real-socket loopback; budget arithmetic unit-tested against both IP versions; a saturation test proving input latency stays bounded while bulk channels are full, with logged per-channel queue depths. Provenance: plan sections 12.1, 12.4, 15.6.

title: Frame pipeline and freshness contract: bounded queues, two ages, cursor/damage, idle
description:
WHY: This is differentiator number one — optimize the age of useful state, not throughput. Every stage gets a bounded queue and a defined rule for obsolete work that respects codec references.

SCOPE: Host and client pipeline policy per the plan's queue table: one replaceable latest pending capture; one-or-two in-flight encoder surfaces where the backend allows (admitting a driver's real requirement only after memory+latency accounting); byte+deadline-limited compressed outbound; negotiated reassembly window (2-12 units by count AND bytes); bounded decoder queue respecting references; newest-frame presentation; small strict audio jitter ceiling. Hidden stages count: codec-internal surfaces, packet caches, QUIC send buffers, renderer-held frames, shared-viewer retention — physical allocations accounted once, each subscriber charged for work it can force; a stalled viewer cannot pin unbounded shared history. "Skip presentation" separated from "discard reference state"; never free driver-owned surfaces to satisfy a metric. Two ages tracked distinctly: last pixel update vs last trustworthy source observation (serviced capture op, OS-qualified damage/unchanged evidence, or unknown — with bounded verification capture at a declared cadence where cheap evidence is impossible, cost reported); stale marking while heartbeats stay healthy. Cursor: shape reliable, position replaceable, single rendering owner via capability bit, unknown-shape fallback, no double cursor in pointer-lock/touch modes. Damage: full valid surface reconstruction before full-frame encode (dirty rects are not permission to encode uninitialized pixels); surface clearing after resize/device loss. Idle: stationary screens stop transmission except refresh/refinement, first damage exits idle promptly, source-verification distinguishes idle from hung capture.

ACCEPTANCE: lab property tests for every bound (bytes and counts) with planted violations; an e2e soak on the real macOS path logging queue high-water marks and both ages; static-screen test proving near-zero encode work while freshness evidence continues. Provenance: plan sections 3.1, 11.1-11.4, 13.4.
close_reason: Implemented frame pipeline and freshness contracts: CursorShape/CursorPosition wire codecs in fr-wire, 12-stage bounded queue accounting ledger, damage surface reconstruction with clear on resize/device loss, cursor tracking with single rendering owner and fallback, two-ages ledger, and static-screen idle controller with settle-to-sharp refinement.

title: frd broker: idle daemon, listeners, session registry, role-capability IPC, process family
description:
WHY: The always-running piece must be small, idle-cheap, and incapable of media work by construction — the proposed idle envelope is under 25 MiB RSS and under 0.1% of one core with NO capture, encoder, or GPU surfaces resident.

SCOPE: crates/frd: tailnet listeners (from fr-tailnet/fr-transport/fr-certs), small local configuration (sharing scope own-user/tailnet, approval mode, selected session/displays, audio/file settings), current peer-identity cache, session registry, browser-asset serving stub, local control socket; the internal process-role family (broker / interactive-session agent / media worker) as modes of a signed process family; local IPC with parent-created or protected endpoints, OS peer credentials where available, ROLE-SPECIFIC capabilities and process/session generations — credentials alone identify a user, not a trusted helper; workers receive no Tailscale control socket, no certificate keys, no approval endpoint, no input-lease capability; privileged platform broker kept minimal (service registration, user-session launch, protected Tailscale metadata/cert ops) with no arbitrary privileged RPC; startup before login where the OS supports it, honestly reporting when no shareable desktop exists.

ACCEPTANCE: idle measurement harness (process-family RSS/CPU over a defined quiet interval) with results recorded against the envelope; IPC forgery unit tests (wrong role, wrong generation, unauthorized user) all refused with typed errors and logs. Provenance: plan sections 5.1, 5.2, 19.2, 21.1.
notes: REALITY-CHECK REMEDIATION (2026-09-23): The broker's real behavior arrives through fr-0il (frd run wiring) and the process split (fr-p1-session-agent-iq3). Unused broker modules (ipc, browser_assets, peer_cache, process_role, idle_harness, session_registry) are on the proposed deletion list unless they gain a production consumer in that work. Idle envelope must be measured on a real idle frd run (no polling loop) with process-family RSS/CPU over a defined interval.

title: First host adapter: macOS ScreenCaptureKit capture + VideoToolbox encode in the media worker role
description:
WHY: Phase 1 needs one complete real host. Apple Silicon is the preferred first path (spike-proven), keeping capture and encode co-located in an on-demand worker so GPU surfaces never cross processes and a hung codec cannot touch authority.

SCOPE: Productionize the macOS spike inside the media-worker process role: SCK full-display capture with borrowed-buffer discipline (owned GPU copy at the documented release point), cursor capture mode and damage metadata where granted, VideoToolbox HEVC session with the qualified real-time no-reordering configuration, encoded access units + bounded metadata to the broker over bounded IPC; worker lifecycle — spawn on demand, generation-fenced teardown, kill-on-stall with authority fencing FIRST, restart with bounded rate/backoff, repeated GPU failure ends the media profile rather than spawning unlimited workers; explicit thread affinity for SCK callbacks and VT completions; permission loss / display removal / display-color changes as typed capability events; protected-content reported as such, never as a stalled network.

ACCEPTANCE: runs as the real process family on Apple Silicon; kill -9 of the worker mid-encode leaves broker+agent healthy and the next session admits cleanly; e2e script capturing a moving desktop for minutes with logged queue depths, copy counts, and zero unbounded growth. Provenance: plan sections 5.4, 10.2, 11.1.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Unit tests for worker lifecycle state machine; the fr-media fake-backend contract-conformance suite runs against this adapter
notes:
REALITY-CHECK REMEDIATION (2026-09-23): The existing macos.rs 'encoder' synthesizes bytes and must not ship (fr-rc-truth-neutralize-fakes-ny0). Real work: ScreenCaptureKit + VideoToolbox via a narrow Objective-C/Swift or objc FFI boundary in a macOS-only platform crate, signed helper for TCC attribution, run on mac-mini-max/mac-mini-old per fr-rc-media-lab-decision-3b5; the honest spike evidence (spikes/media-macos: ffmpeg VT CLI only, SCK blocked by TCC over SSH) is the starting point.

2026-11-09 capture freshness correction (plan 10.2 and source-observation invariants): stream silence and cached pixels can no longer produce fresh Unchanged evidence or a newly stamped cached IDR. Require post-request Complete/Idle display-time evidence; after 50 ms without it, macOS 14+ performs one real screenshot with the original filter/configuration and encodes only that returned buffer. Keep the original broker timestamp and total deadline, isolate late one-shot callbacks, and fence every retained result with a checked invalidation generation through final publication. Native NAL growth is checked before allocation/copy; fragmented CMBlockBuffer data and invalid output lengths are handled safely. Count verification requests/encodes explicitly; up to 20 genuine verification captures per second is an unqualified idle cost, not zero-idle work. Eleven production C policy tests pass with GCC 14.2.0 and strict warnings, including in-flight invalidation/repair, late completion and output bounds. Pinned Rust formatting, docs links and diff checks pass. Objective-C build, real screenshot/VideoToolbox behavior, performance and the existing 2 s host preparation timeout remain unqualified; no full Mac host or bead closure claimed.

2026-11-09 canonical native capture output: VideoToolbox four-byte NAL lengths now stay length-prefixed across the native boundary. The worker uses one bounded host-only SEI/padding normalization allocation followed by the unchanged strict canonical HevcGuard; independent broker/viewer admission remains. This removes the Annex-B round trip and one complete access-unit allocation/copy while preserving parameter/reference state transactionality, exact output capacity, and original capture/preparation deadlines. Real retained VideoToolbox IDR/P fixtures and malformed-length/escaping/parameter/reference/count/byte-bound regressions pass in the complete fr-media test suite (156 library tests plus integration/doc targets); the 11 strict C capture-policy tests also pass. Native SDK/hardware behavior and elapsed startup/energy benefit remain unverified; this does not establish the cause or resolution of the owner's unpublished macOS host preparation timeout.

2026-11-09 native capture setup extension: one 2000 ms monotonic opening deadline now spans mandatory cross-process setup-lock acquisition, shareable-content discovery, stream construction/start, encoder configuration, and final capture publication. Stream start and caller-owned VideoToolbox preparation overlap within that same original budget; the earlier broker preparation deadline still wins. Expired or failed lock acquisition refuses setup. An explicit original opening owner retains capture and the setup lease through late start completion, acknowledged stream stop/output removal/sample-queue retirement, and encoder invalidation. Expiry closes admission but never invents native cleanup. Final publication requires a timely successful start plus live source state; delayed callbacks cannot publish a replacement capture. Strong Objective-C output ownership avoids autorelease-delayed setup-lock handoff. The existing worker exits after failed ConfigureMonitor; the process supervisor remains the hard bound for synchronous framework hangs or unconfirmed cleanup. Validation: 20 exact production capture-policy tests pass under strict GCC, including nine new deadline/late-start/retirement cases. Independent source reviews checked publication races, lock ordering, and codec/capture ownership. macOS SDK compilation, hardware timing and end-to-end native qualification remain unverified here; no measured startup speedup or resolution of the separately reported private host timeout is claimed. This broad host qualification bead remains open.

comments.author: ClaudeOpus55
comments.text:
2026-11-10 (Claude): 23e355b8. The capture worker's per-picture Screen Recording and display checks were the largest fixable host cost.

Evidence: I sampled the installed worker (`sample`, 5 s) during a live 5K view session. Its main thread spent:
- ~45% blocked in VTCompressionSessionEncodeFrame (synchronous XPC to the encoder service);
- ~20% in CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess (a synchronous tccd round trip);
- ~15% in SLSDisplayStatusQuery (the display mode/placement check).
capture_live() ran both native checks three times per picture: on entry, after selecting the picture, and before publishing.

Change: the stream's own stop flag is still read on every call. A positive native check younger than 100 ms (FR_CAP_LIVE_REUSE_NS) now stands for the next checks. It is stamped before the calls, on CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW, so system sleep counts. A refusal is never kept, so revocation or a mode change is refused within 100 ms.
Tests: the C policy test gained the reuse bounds (22 pass); the real-display macos_capture_worker tests pass 4/4, twice.

Measured at 5120x2880 on the M5 Ultra:
- Worker per-request time (scratch harness, 150 back-to-back requests, 5 interleaved A/B rounds): 71-82 ms mean before, 43-47 ms after.
- Live view-only sessions from mac-mini-old, swapping only the installed worker between sessions (3 interleaved rounds): 11.3-12.1 pictures/s before, 18.2-18.8 after; p50 at most 83-85 ms before, 51-53 ms after.

The installed worker was restored to a63edaec afterwards; the backup is in ~/Library/Application Support/FrankenRemote/backup-a63edaec/. The installed host does not have 23e355b8 until the next install-host.sh run.

Unexplained: in an earlier noisy window, both variants averaged 200-336 ms per request, and 2 runs of the new worker died at EOF with no reply. Their stderr was not captured. Since then, 0 of 11 new-worker runs have failed.

Remaining ceiling at 5K: synchronous low-latency VT encode of ~27.5 ms (spike, today's load), plus the post-request source wait, with one encode in flight. In the spike, PrioritizeEncodingSpeedOverQuality is refused (-12900) in low-latency mode, and MaximizePowerEfficiency=false changed nothing.

Next levers (an owner trade-off):
(a) Pipeline two encodes in flight. This changes the worker's request/credit model.
(b) Encode 3840x2160 (15.4 ms; ~35+ fps at one in flight). This downscales from the 6K panel.
(c) Accept ~19-26 fps at 5K.

comments.author: ClaudeOpus55
comments.text:
2026-11-11 (Claude): 23e355b8 is installed on mac-studio (install-host.sh from e8362992, 00:33). A live view-only session from mac-mini-old measured 20.0 pictures/s, p50 at most 49 ms and a max gap of 165 ms at load 17. Before the fix it was 11-17 pictures/s.

Where the 5K ceiling comes from. I benchmarked VideoToolbox on synthetic 5120x2880 NV12 frames: scrolled text, the worker's session properties, M5 Ultra, macOS 27. The harness is scratchpad ms_probe/vt_depth.m.

| Mode | Latency per frame | Throughput |
|---|---|---|
| Low-latency RC (the worker's mode), 1 in flight | 25.4-26.0 ms; EncodeFrame blocks for all of it | 38.3 fps |
| Low-latency, 2 or 3 frames queued from one thread | same | 38.3 fps (no gain: EncodeFrame is synchronous) |
| Low-latency, 2 / 3 separate sessions on their own threads | same | 77 / 115 fps aggregate (the hardware is not saturated) |
| Low-latency with a fixed per-frame BaseFrameQP (22/28/34) | 25.9 ms | 38.5 fps, and no dropped frames (8 drops per 125 frames under its own RC) |
| Low-latency at 3840x2160 | 15.2 ms | 65.6 fps |
| Normal mode (RealTime, no reordering), 1 in flight | 12.1 ms; EncodeFrame returns in 0.4 ms | 82.7 fps |
| Normal mode, 3 in flight | 21 ms | 141.6 fps |

Normal mode is twice as fast at 5K, but it still refuses ReferenceBufferCount=1 (-12900) and MaxFrameDelayCount=0. It therefore keeps 4 references, and HevcGuard's subset (DPB budget, "P pictures reference exactly the preceding POC") refuses it. Low-latency time scales linearly with pixel count (about 1.8 us per 1000 pixels), which looks like one engine and no split.

So at 5K under the current protocol the encode alone caps a one-in-flight worker at about 38 fps. The live 20 fps also includes:
- the post-request source wait: the reply carries the request time as the freshness lower bound, so the worker waits for a frame captured after the request, about 9 ms on average at the display's 56 Hz;
- per-picture overhead in the worker and frd.

Possible levers, each a design change:
(a) Two requests in flight, so the next picture's source wait overlaps the current 26 ms encode. That changes frd's one-capture-in-flight stream model and worker concurrency. Estimated 33-38 fps.
(b) Let the reply carry the selected picture's own display time, so a frame newer than the last encoded one can be used without a post-request wait. This is a freshness-evidence change. About 9 ms back per picture.
(c) Capture at the viewer's backing size when it is smaller (owner priority: native-or-viewport capture). 4K encodes in 15 ms.
(d) Allow multi-reference low-delay P streams in HevcGuard, so normal mode can be used. This is a protocol and recovery-semantics change across every decoder.
