What held the rate down, found by live measurement (60 Hz change source, view-only viewer on mac-mini-old):
1. SharedFramePool admitted 8 pictures (host_run.rs; the 8 came from a test fixture). Each sent picture stays cached until its 250 ms reference horizon, so any source was capped near 8 / (0.25 s + capture time): 27.5 pictures/s at 1080p. It is now 32 (each viewer's own send-cache limit; covers 120 fps).
2. Cadence::after_turn rounded the next start up to a whole slot: 37 ms of work at 60 fps got a 50 ms period. The next capture now starts at max(started + interval, completed); missed slots are still not owed.
3. A turn without capture credit waited a whole interval. Viewers' connection tasks now advance a credit epoch when they hand records to the transport; the source wakes on it and starts the capture early (never less than one interval after the previous capture started).
Multi-viewer: until a picture has been shared for one interval, a capture waits for every viewer and refuses none. After that, a viewer still holding the picture is refused as slow, as before.

Live, d280b1bf's host binary against main 61939487, interleaved 25 s sessions. Picture: mac-studio's display is 6144x3456, which macos_display.rs encodes at 5120x2880 (5/6):

  d280b1bf: 26.5 26.1 25.8 26.3 25.2 25.3 /s, p50 36-37 ms, p95 55-66 ms
At 5120x2880 the capture itself (~37 ms) now sets the rate. At 1080p (prototype tree, same pool size, 1 ms retry poll): 49.3-51.7 /s, p50 18-19 ms, against 27.5 with the old pool. The production binary at 1080p is not measured.

Found along the way:

A busy VideoToolbox probe is reported as Unsupported. That label is misleading, and it is likely what my earlier "frd refuses at 6K" observation was: 6K hosts start fine today.
- Viewer sessions started back to back on the same host port spend about 24 s in two Accept(HandshakeTimeout) before a short session. Alternating ports avoids it. Not investigated.

title: Tailscale HTTPS certificates: provisioning, renewal, atomic replacement, endpoint configuration
description:
WHY: TLS 1.3 underlies QUIC and browser trust; Tailscale-provisioned certificates for the host's tailnet FQDN are the only identity material — no second CA, no TOFU, no accept-any-certificate path ever, including under expiry pressure.

SCOPE: Certificate acquisition through the qualified Tailscale metadata/cert bridge (helper restricted to approved hostnames and protected key storage — not a general Tailscale admin proxy); renewal with backoff, pre-expiry alerts, continued use of a still-valid cert during renewal outages; ATOMIC install of chain+key; device rename / tailnet switch revalidates endpoint names before new sessions; one configurable unprivileged service port (8443 provisional default) for TCP and UDP with collision detection and honest endpoint reporting — never silently overwriting another listener or Tailscale Serve config; ALPN separation (project-native ALPN vs h3); setup reports tailnet-HTTPS enablement as an explicit prerequisite including certificate-transparency visibility of the machine name.

ACCEPTANCE: unit tests for rotation/atomicity/rename paths; a renewal-outage simulation proving still-valid certs keep serving and expiry never enables skip-verification; setup/doctor output naming the real endpoint. Provenance: plan sections 6.5, 20.3.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Renewal, rotation, and failure events logged with typed reasons and surfaced in fr doctor with expiry countdown
close_reason: Implemented zero-dependency ASN.1 DER not_after parser, typed CertificateEventKind and CertificateEvent recording in NativeServerIdentity lifecycle, expiry countdown calculation, port collision detection for service ports, honest HTTPS and QUIC endpoint formatting, certificate transparency notice, and fr doctor in fr-native with full JSON and human output. Tested with unit tests in fr-tailnet and fr-native, and CLI integration tests in tests/fr_cli.rs.

title: Input pipeline: ordered actions, tickets at submission, held-state cleanup, no replay
description:
WHY: Reliability is not permission to execute stale actions. This bead implements the complete input discipline that makes FrankenRemote safe for humans and mandatory for agents.

SCOPE: End to end across client core, wire, broker, session agent: one ordered bounded action sequence per lease (key/button transitions, scroll, committed text, mode changes); replaceable absolute pointer states on datagrams with their own sequence space (pointer gaps never create action-sequence gaps); click carries its coordinate and a pointer-sequence barrier — late pre-click motion cannot move the pointer backward after the click; relative movement as cumulative/checkpointed representation; drag and touch-emulation transitions obey the same ordering. Tickets: host-issued, tied to lease + view/recovery readiness + geometry + mapping generations, verified against host-clock expiry IMMEDIATELY before OS submission; delayed traffic gets no new lifetime at receipt; timed-out actions reported refused/expired, never silently retried; ordered-sequence gaps are protocol errors or bounded resync, never skipped clicks; duplicates return the retained bounded result within the live epoch; monotonic consumed-sequence floor independent of the result cache (evicted receipts return no-replay/unknown-history, never re-admission); expired press fences queued dependents; release-only cleanup always allowed; periodic held-state reconciliation releases inconsistencies but never synthesizes presses. Text vs keys separated: physical positions/modifiers/repeat ownership distinct from bounded committed Unicode with a qualified injection path — no layout-guess translation, no clipboard smuggling; unavailable text injection surfaced as a limitation with physical keys retained. Focus/geometry/mode/lifecycle checked per batch; cleanup distinguishes requested / OS-submitted / uncertain.

ACCEPTANCE: lab properties (duplicate no-readmit, expiry-before-injection, no resurrection after stall, barrier ordering) against production code; e2e on the real host: type/click/drag through induced stalls and reconnects with per-action disposition logs proving zero stale executions. Provenance: plan sections 7.3, 15.1, 15.2.
acceptance_criteria: - [x] Unit tests for sequence spaces, ticket lifetime/floor logic, and dedupe-cache eviction, independent of the e2e lanes

title: Deterministic property suite: authority, input, recovery, and bounds against production state machines
description:
WHY: The plan's section 24.1 property list is the correctness contract; encoding it as a permanent deterministic suite (not one-off tests) is what lets every later change prove it broke nothing.

SCOPE: On fr-lab, against PRODUCTION state machines: duplicate input identifier cannot admit another click within its live epoch; an old lease never controls a new session; geometry changes reject old coordinate input; obsolete codec configuration never reaches the new decoder; missing references trigger repair or recovery, never indefinite corrupted output; host-clock challenge expiry; ticket expiry immediately before injection; no action resurrection after a stalled reactor; read-only approval enforcement (approval gates thumbnails/audio/clipboard/semantic reads, not just control); controller-handoff serialization; shared-pipeline lifetime (closing one viewer never cancels another's encoder; last unsubscribe stops it); late viewer join waits for a fresh recovery point; old pointer datagrams after a click; client-freshness vs unchanged-screen distinction; committed-vs-uncommitted work in channel cancellation; admitted-vs-irreversibly-submitted OS injection in teardown results. Recovery model rows per the P1_RECOVERY bead. Every failure emits the seed and full event schedule; every bound asserted in BYTES as well as counts.

ACCEPTANCE: suite runs in CI lanes deterministically (two runs, identical logs); a deliberately-broken guard for each property class demonstrates the suite catches it (planted-negative validation); suite documented as the permanent regression gate. Provenance: plan section 24.1.

title: Instrumented input-to-photon latency harness
description:
WHY: The Phase 1 exit gate requires an instrumented latency result, and every future performance claim inherits this harness's honesty rules: distributions and worst useful tails, stages separated, never packet-to-decoder-submission mislabeled as input-to-photon.

SCOPE: An instrumented host application whose input handler changes a known visual target; client-side timestamping of submission and presentation; stage decomposition (input transit, OS/app response, capture wait, conversion, encode, return transit, reassembly/jitter, decode, display wait); local monotonic clocks for stage durations; cross-host offsets only with estimated uncertainty bounds (never raw subtraction of unsynchronized clocks); an optical/high-speed-camera lane documented for later use where practical; output as distributions (p50/p95 and tails) with the measurement scope recorded (process family, direct/relay, cold/warm, refresh rate, capture path). Proposed objectives to measure against, not to claim: direct 2-5 ms RTT p50 <= 45 ms / p95 <= 70 ms; ~40 ms WAN p95 <= 130 ms; warm first useful frame <= 500 ms.

ACCEPTANCE: harness produces reproducible reports on the Phase 1 pair; results recorded with full scope; explicitly labeled as instrumented-workload measurements. Provenance: plan sections 21.1, 21.3.
acceptance_criteria: - [x] Harness self-calibration test: a synthetic known-delay loopback must be measured within stated uncertainty before any real numbers are reported
notes: REALITY-CHECK REMEDIATION (2026-09-23): Method (replaces the hard-coded constants): a tiny test-only instrumented X11 host application paints a marker region encoding a sequence number when it receives an injected key/click and logs (seq, host_monotonic_us) at receipt and at draw; the client reads back its own presented window (XGetImage on the viewer window) and logs (seq, client_monotonic_us) at first presentation; ClockProbe/ClockReply samples give per-probe offset intervals (NTP 4-timestamp bounds) intersected with Marzullo's algorithm; each sample is reported as [lower, upper] input-to-presented latency; distributions p50/p95/p99 of both bounds; scope label 'instrumented workload, client presentation readback, excludes display scanout and panel response'; path kind (direct/DERP) recorded; optional optical lane later. Self-calibration: a known injected delay on loopback must be recovered within the stated uncertainty before any real number is reported. Refuse to emit without real samples.

title: Production loss recovery: fragmentation, repair, recovery generations, startup handshake
description:
WHY: Productionizes the Phase 0 recovery spike. Correctness-critical recovery belongs to Phase 1 — it is explicitly NOT postponable polish, because the Phase 1 exit gate requires surviving real loss.

SCOPE: In fr-transport/fr-media/fr-client: access-unit fragmentation with explicit total length/offset/index/count/stream binding/generations, all arithmetic checked, overlap rejected, duplicates deduplicated without allocation, reassembly bounded in time/metadata/bytes even for hostile tiny fragments; sender cache bounded by bytes and time; receiver missing-range coalescing with clamped ranges/retries/frequency/bytes; separate display vs reference-retention deadlines with the negotiated dependency window (initial ceil(fps x horizon)+2 clamped to 2-12 and byte budget, horizon <= 250 ms provisional); abandon-and-recover when a needed reference exceeds horizon/budget — never feed incomplete pictures to a decoder; startup/reconfiguration handshake exactly as specified (config ack is API-configured, not first-frame; bounded bootstrap IDR retained or refreshed; each milestone with timeout and cleanup; dependent pictures buffered within admitted bounds until IDR decodes; unknown-generation media discarded or held in a tiny pre-config allowance); recovery generations PER SUBSCRIPTION so one viewer's recovery never resets another's decoder; shared-pipeline IDR request coalescing/rate-limiting; chronically failing viewers get an independent operating point or refusal; reliable recovery stream with reset semantics advancing the recovery generation; no per-frame acks in steady state.

ACCEPTANCE: the full lab recovery model (missing first/middle/final fragments, loss before idle, reference repair past display deadline, lost recovery config/ack, exhausted budget, 120 ms repair horizon case, large IDRs, receiver-credit starvation) green against PRODUCTION parsers/state machines with byte-bound assertions and seed-logged failures; real-HEVC e2e under injected loss sustaining useful video. Provenance: plan sections 12.2-12.4, 24.1.
acceptance_criteria: - [x] Unit tests for fragmentation arithmetic (offset/count/overlap/overflow) and sender-cache byte/time eviction

title: Interactive-session agent: consent, indicator, revoke, input lease ownership, watchdog
description:
WHY: The agent runs in the selected user's interactive context and owns everything consent- and input-shaped. Its control path must stay responsive when the encoder is dead, and revoke must never wait on anything slow.

SCOPE: The interactive-session agent role: local approval UI (when enabled, gating any new observation before pixels/thumbnails/audio/clipboard/semantic data), always-visible sharing indicator with immediate revoke (revoke is synchronous at the authority decision point; OS cleanup completion reported separately), input lease ownership with expiry re-checked immediately before EVERY OS submission, key/button held-state tracking for remote injections only, platform permission state surfacing; independent watchdog path so a blocked OS call never holds the lease timer or revoke decision (no authority lock across blocking calls); on OS session change/logout/lock/permission loss, old authority revoked and never inherited; local-input-priority option that suspends the remote lease only where injected-vs-local events are distinguishable (present the limitation honestly where not); approval records device, role, displays, audio scope, session identity; approval expiry on requesting-session end; approval-mode transitions revoke existing grants.

ACCEPTANCE: fault tests — agent alive with dead worker, revoke latency measured and logged, expired lease refuses injection at the submission checkpoint, uncertain release states reported honestly after an input-process crash; UI states screenshot-tested where the platform allows. Provenance: plan sections 5.3, 7.3, 15.2.

ADDED SCOPE (polish round 1): (a) The first platform input-injection adapter lands here: macOS keyboard/pointer injection (CGEvent posting under the Accessibility permission, with the qualified committed-text path distinct from physical-key events), since the session agent owns the submission checkpoint; Windows SendInput and Linux EIS injection land inside their Phase 2 host-adapter beads under the same submission-time checks. (b) The optional OS-supported active-session sleep inhibitor: while a session is actively shared, hold the platform idle-sleep inhibitor (IOKit assertion on macOS, SetThreadExecutionState on Windows, systemd/logind inhibitor on Linux); it prevents idle sleep only — it never defeats lid-close policy or a deliberate local lock, and it releases immediately when the last session ends. Tests: injection refused without Accessibility permission (typed); inhibitor held/released verified in logs across session start/end and crash.
notes:
REALITY-CHECK REMEDIATION (2026-09-23): Target process model (plan 5): `frd agent` is a separate process spawned by the broker into the interactive session over an inherited socketpair with role capabilities and generations; it owns SessionAuthority, the approval UI and sharing indicator (existing X11 code), the input owner with an independently progressing watchdog thread, clipboard and audio endpoints; it spawns fr-media-worker. Today SessionAgent is an in-process struct, the input agent is a thread in the same process, broker/ipc.rs is unused, SleepInhibitor defaults to a simulated platform, and macOS injection is a RecordingPoster. Also fix fr-rc-sec-approval-synthetic-input-t2r and fr-rc-sec-panic-abort-cleanup-4m7 here or before.
2026-09-27 reality check #2: Session-agent duties split into concrete beads: fr-rc2-lock-logout-revokes-wmrt (plan violation: lock/logout does not revoke), fr-rc2-indicator-for-every-observation-qdn5, fr-rc2-approval-local-in-frd-run-x153. title: fr-core session authority: state machine, leases, challenges, tickets, generations
description:
WHY: This is the heart of "input authority that ends cleanly." Observation permission, media readiness, and input authority are three separate state variables; conflating them is how remote-desktop tools replay stale clicks and leak observation.

SCOPE: In fr-core: the session state machine (Identified -> CapabilitiesChecked -> WaitingApproval? -> ViewOpening -> Viewing -> ControlGranted -> Suspended/Revoke -> Draining -> Closed); a SERIALIZED authority owner (handoff is never a check-then-set race across broker tasks); challenge/renewal on the host's monotonic clock — one-second cadence, three-second provisional renewable deadlines; a response renews only an outstanding unexpired challenge for the current lease (a buffered heartbeat arriving late extends nothing); expired leases are terminal, reacquisition is a new grant re-running approval policy; input-validity tickets as bounded host-side records addressed by opaque random handles (no PKI/custom crypto), lifetime 0.5-1.5 s path-aware, always bounded by the lease, renewed at a cadence comfortably shorter than lifetime without per-action round trips; typed generations (from the F_WORKSPACE bead) fencing every stale artifact; suspend/resume and scheduler-stall as generation boundaries (deadline checked before processing queued work); local approval gating ANY new observation (pixels, thumbnails, audio, clipboard, semantic data) as well as control; the fixed teardown order (revoke input -> release held keys -> invalidate generations -> stop capture admission -> cancel cooperative tasks -> drain bounded sends -> kill stuck worker -> publish closure); pending approvals/reservations with short bounded lifetimes.

ACCEPTANCE: exhaustive unit tests for every transition and every anti-resurrection rule; acknowledgement stages typed as admitted/submitted/observed (never "exactly once"); all tests logged with state-transition traces. Provenance: plan sections 6.3, 7.1-7.3, 15.1.
close_reason: Implemented at f1d89fc: SessionAuthority serialized-owner state machine with observation/readiness/control as separate variables; clock-injected (HostInstant as data, no runtime dep). Covers grant/revoke/handoff serialization, ControllerBusy slot, host-clock challenge renewal with anti-resurrection, ticket lifetimes clamped to lease, authorize_submission pre-OS-submission check, and apply_resume_boundary generation boundary. Design finding fixed: observation drop demotes phase to CapabilitiesChecked so reacquisition is a legal new grant. Gates via rch at this revision: fmt clean, clippy -D warnings clean, 26 unit + 2 doc-tests pass. Note: this is the pure-logic core; wiring into the asupersync-owned broker region lands with fr-p1-frd-broker.

title: Client microphone to host: explicit-enable uplink into the qualified virtual-mic endpoint
description:
WHY: v1.4 makes audio bidirectional — talking into a meeting running on the remote workstation is the defining use case. The uplink reuses the downlink's Opus discipline with roles reversed and terminates in the per-OS endpoint proven by the Phase 0 spike.

SCOPE: Client capture (desktop APIs; mobile/browser capture lands with their clients) behind an explicit per-session talk toggle backed by the client OS microphone permission — NEVER activated by connecting, with a visible indicator on both ends; Opus encode at the client; the same sequence/timeline/jitter/generation rules as the downlink; host-side delivery into the qualified virtual-microphone endpoint (PipeWire source on Linux; signed CoreAudio server plugin on macOS; the Windows endpoint per the spike's recommendation — a native non-Rust component with recorded provenance). Where the endpoint is not qualified on a host OS, microphone forwarding is a TYPED UNSUPPORTED capability there — no fake device, no undisclosed driver install. Mic capability is separately advertised and separately approved in approval mode; a viewer never gets it; revoke/lease expiry silences the uplink at the host boundary immediately.

ACCEPTANCE: end-to-end talk test into a real host application per qualified OS with measured added latency; hot-mic security test (activation without explicit enable must fail, logged); lease-expiry silencing verified; endpoint absence produces the typed capability refusal in fr doctor and the client UI. Provenance: plan section 15.4 (v1.4), Phase 0 virtual-mic spike.

title: Host playback audio to client: Opus pipeline, per-OS capture, jitter discipline
description:
WHY: Hearing the remote machine is v1 scope. Audio must never force stale video to display for fake sync, and Windows loopback's cross-session scope must be disclosed, not hidden.

SCOPE: Opus-only downlink: 48 kHz mono/stereo, 10 ms packets nominal; one controlled resample/format boundary from the real device rate; negotiated channels and max packet duration/decoded samples validated before allocation; sequence numbers plus a monotonic sample timeline; explicit capture gaps, silence suppression, device changes, configuration resets. Per-OS sources: ScreenCaptureKit audio on macOS (audio permission/scope distinct from Screen Recording); a selected output monitor via qualified Linux audio APIs; WASAPI render-endpoint loopback on Windows with its endpoint-wide, cross-session scope explicitly disclosed at local setup — authorized as such or left unavailable, never misrepresented as per-app isolation. Client playback: small bounded adaptive jitter buffer with a strict ceiling, packet-loss concealment, slow drift correction anchored to sample timestamps and the client audio clock; bounded A/V offset — fresh video is never held hostage to delayed audio; late packets discarded; device change/reconnect resets the audio generation so stale buffered sound never plays after resume. Playback capture disabled until locally enabled; active only for admitted sessions that request it; approval mode gates it as observation.

ACCEPTANCE: e2e latency/continuity test with induced loss and device switches, logged buffer depths and concealment events; scope-disclosure text verified in setup; lab tests for generation reset and A/V offset bounds. Provenance: plan sections 15.4, 23 Phase 2.

title: Remaining desktop client shells with qualified hardware decode and presentation
description:
WHY: v1 ships native desktop clients on Linux, macOS, and Windows; the first shell exists from Phase 1, and the remaining two reuse fr-client with per-OS decode/presentation qualification.

SCOPE: The two remaining desktop shells per the windowing decision note: window lifecycle, hardware decode to native presentation (D3D swapchain on Windows; the qualified Linux GPU decode + presentation path), full input capture semantics, the standard UI set (machine picker, recent hosts, display selection, toolbar, connection-quality panel, settings, permission explanations), DPI/scale correctness, single-cursor ownership, clean teardown. CONSTRAINTS: no GPU-to-CPU readback to fit a UI abstraction; text quality per plan section 14.1 (native pixels when practical, one explicit scaling step, correct color metadata, no accidental limited/full-range mismatch).

title: Discovery: local tailnet peers, bounded capability probes, saved hosts, optional directory
description:
WHY: Native clients should find hosts from local Tailscale state without scans; mobile and web cannot read another app's local API, so their baseline is saved hosts and links — and any served directory must be information, never delegated permission.

SCOPE: Desktop: peers from local Tailscale state, then bounded concurrent capability probes ONLY against those node addresses (timeouts/backoff), cached by stable node identity with expiry, invalidated on tailnet change; discovery states distinguished (offline, no interactive session, permission required, ready) where evidence allows; live encode/decode admission revalidated after OS/driver changes. Mobile/web baseline: saved hosts and explicit host links (no bearer tokens in links, ever). Optional authenticated directory served by a known frd: opt-in, restricted by local policy, discovery information only — it must not proxy connections around the viewer's own Tailscale policy or expose inventory contrary to a restricted directory policy; no screenshots, application titles, clipboard previews, or audio in discovery responses; every client device needs its own working tailnet connectivity.

ACCEPTANCE: probe behavior verified bounded (connection counts, backoff) under a flaky-host simulation; directory policy tests (restricted inventory stays restricted); saved-host flow e2e on desktop shells. Provenance: plan section 6.4.

title: Display selection and multi-display: stable catalogs, geometry generations, hotplug
description:
WHY: Multi-monitor desktops are the workstation norm; coordinate-dependent input must be provably bound to the geometry it was aimed at, and display identity is only as stable as the OS actually guarantees.

SCOPE: Display catalog per host: stable local identity within the OS's real guarantees (connector/ID reuse after hotplug handled), pixel bounds, logical bounds, scale, rotation, geometry generation; hotplug/reconfiguration creates a new geometry generation BEFORE coordinate input is accepted; missing/ambiguous mappings refuse rather than guess; only selected displays transmitted, each visible display an independently identified stream under the shared session budget (never one giant bounding-box framebuffer); unobserved displays suspended; the single controller's pointer/keyboard target explicit when viewing several displays; per-display selection UI in the shells; catalog bound to the OS-session/geometry generation.

ACCEPTANCE: lab tests for stale-geometry input rejection; e2e hotplug tests (remove display during a drag, change scale during a click — from the plan's fault list) on each host OS with logs proving refusal rather than misdelivery; multi-display selection round-trips in every desktop shell. title: Denial-of-service bounds: rate limits, global resource limits, flood fairness
description:
WHY: Plan section 19.3 is an implementation requirement, not only a test list: an admitted peer, a pre-admission stranger, or a flood of metadata must never exhaust the host. The security campaign (Phase 5) attacks these bounds; this bead builds them.

SCOPE: Rate-limit pre-admission connections, expensive codec probes, control requests, cursor-shape uploads, recovery requests, and diagnostic exports; admission accounting for encoder sessions, GPU surfaces, CPU fallback, decoder limits, bandwidth, and per-viewer memory; bounds on message counts AND bytes everywhere (a queue of two access units is still unbounded if access-unit size is); resource limits applied BEFORE a malicious stream can allocate its declared decoded dimensions; global limits for handshake concurrency and duration, pending approvals, half-attached WSS channels, retained request receipts, decoder reconfigurations, and worker restarts; idle-session timeouts that unauthenticated garbage or stale challenges cannot extend; codec probes cancelled when their requesting session disappears (no hardware reservation by mere negotiation); metadata allocations counted (thousands of zero-byte fragments or stream IDs exhaust memory without crossing payload limits); unknown generations, large cursor shapes, long Unicode names, and invalid parameter-set requests rejected before expensive work; revoke/expiry serviced FAIRLY during floods — no high-priority queue is unbounded.

ACCEPTANCE: unit tests per limit with planted violations; a lab flood scenario proving revoke latency stays bounded while a peer floods recovery requests, with logged queue/limit counters; limits integrated into the one fr-core limits structure with safe administrator overrides constrained by absolute bounds. Provenance: plan sections 17.2, 19.3.

title: File send/receive over ATP: bounded channel, path safety, atomic publication
description:
WHY: v1.4 promotes file transfer into core scope, reusing asupersync's ATP object-transfer machinery (resumable, integrity-verified) instead of inventing a protocol — the accretive move that turns the remote workstation into a complete workflow.

SCOPE: Explicit file send/receive between the admitted controlling client and the host on its own bounded channel class within the session: ATP-backed transfer with resumption across reconnects; drag-and-drop initiation where the desktop shells support it plus explicit pick-and-send everywhere; sends land in a locally configured host drop directory; receives come from explicit host-side selection or a configured share directory — the client can never browse or address arbitrary host paths; every received path validated against traversal and symlink escape BEFORE any write; nothing auto-opened or auto-executed; partials written to temporary names and published atomically (cancel/crash never leaves a half-visible file); per-session byte/rate/concurrency budgets admitted separately, transfer traffic sharing congestion capacity without ever sitting ahead of input or starving the freshness contract; progress metadata observable, contents never logged; capability separately advertised and approval-gated; viewers get nothing.

ACCEPTANCE: e2e send/receive of small and multi-GB files with mid-transfer disconnect/resume, logged progress and budgets; path-traversal and symlink-escape attack tests refused with typed errors; a saturation test proving input latency stays bounded during a full-rate transfer. Provenance: plan sections 12.2, 15.6 (v1.4).
notes:
2026-09-27 reality check #2: Viewer->host file send WORKING at namespace scope (fr connect --control --send; e2e real_files, hash-checked, atomic publication in the drop dir). Gaps: host->viewer receive, resumption across reconnect, drag-and-drop; CLI refuses --send with --clipboard (fr-rc2-cli-clipboard-with-files-i9uk).
2026-10-26: Added repeated explicit uploads on the original completed lane (core commit 7b58020), with a one-slot SendIntake, immutable submission deadline and sender policy, independent per-batch controls/receipts, increasing transfer IDs and unchanged cumulative host limits. Native Linux X11 copy-only XDND selection now reaches that intake after a successful initial --send batch: up to 8 local file/directory URIs per drop and 8 further batches, metadata preparation on one retained worker, fresh progress-window controls, preserved content-free results including accepted drops retired before preparation, and no replay after reconnect. Host download and duplex support are already separately implemented. Exact pinned compiler execution passed all 7 production URI/inbox tests; production viewer_window.c including viewer_drop.c passed strict C syntax validation. New original-owner UDP/TLS/ATP two-batch, native-panel, worker-history and CLI regressions are authored but full runtime-dependent Rust/native-X11 execution is still unverified in this workspace. Keep open for runtime qualification, resumption, general pick-and-send and remaining acceptance; no multi-GB, throughput or live-tailnet claim.

title: Linux host adapter: Wayland portal/PipeWire with agent-owned sessions, EIS input, X11 adapter
description:
WHY: Linux hosting spans compositors with genuinely different capability sets; the plan requires per-environment qualification rows and an ownership rule that keeps input authority in the session agent even when capture is delegated.

SCOPE: Wayland: the session agent creates and RETAINS the RemoteDesktop portal session and input connection, passing only the selected PipeWire remote/stream capability to the media worker (a worker must never hold a combined capture+input session); portal sequence with clipboard requested before Start; returned grants, not requested flags, define authorization; restore tokens persisted atomically and rotated (single-use); streams resolved by the strongest identifier (PipeWire serial where available; node IDs are reused) and re-verified after reconnect; compositor-space coordinates vs stream pixels vs crop/scale vs EIS region mapping kept distinct; cursor metadata only when granted; EIS-preferred input path, libei/PipeWire FFI in the platform exception list. X11: explicit adapter using established capture/damage and input mechanisms, its different security assumptions surfaced in diagnostics. systemd user service attaches to the correct graphical session and its D-Bus environment. Qualification rows: GNOME, KDE, and Hyprland/wlroots-family separately (capture, pointer, keyboard, restore, clipboard, playback audio) with exact versions; unsupported rows are actionable refusals or explicit view-only capability — never a privileged input fallback after a portal refusal.

ACCEPTANCE: fault suite green per qualified compositor row with versions recorded; restore-token rotation and node-ID-reuse tests pass; the qualification table published in-repo. Provenance: plan sections 10.1, 23 Phase 2, 24.2.
notes: REALITY-CHECK REMEDIATION (2026-09-23): Wayland work has not started (the prior closure rested on models and a fabricated qualification table, withdrawn by fr-rc-truth-withdraw-qualification-mdh). Dependency route: reuse the sd-bus FFI already used for logind (crates/fr-native/src/logind/bus.rs) for the xdg-desktop-portal RemoteDesktop/ScreenCast calls rather than adding zbus (whose executors would bring a second runtime unless audited); libpipewire and libei via narrow FFI in the platform crate (exception list). Session agent owns the portal session; only the PipeWire remote fd goes to the worker. Qualification rows GNOME/KDE/Hyprland need real sessions on lab machines (fr-rc-media-lab-decision-3b5); unsupported rows are typed refusals.

title: Windows host adapter: Desktop Duplication capture, FFmpeg hardware encode, session-aware service split
description:
WHY: Windows hosting is a v1 requirement; the spike proved the path, this bead productionizes it inside the process-role family with Windows' session model handled honestly.

SCOPE: Desktop Duplication full-display capture with cursor and dirty-region info; prompt frame release with copy-to-owned-GPU-surface when retention would block capture; recreation on documented desktop/display transitions; access-lost / device-removed / resize / rotation / duplication-exhaustion handled explicitly; capture device qualified against the actual display adapter (hybrid GPUs); qualified SDR conversion/tone-mapping without changing user display settings (DuplicateOutput1 format behavior); FFmpeg hardware encode (NVENC/AMF/QSV per probe) in the media worker. Service split: the service never captures Session 0 as the user's desktop; the interactive agent binds to the intended session with its executable, launch permissions, and named-pipe endpoints session-bound; lock screens, user changes, and secure-desktop transitions are typed capability changes; SendInput integrity-level limits surfaced as capability rows (no promise of elevated-window or secure-desktop control); protected-content blackouts and integrity-restricted input reported separately from transport failure; mixed-DPI monitors with negative virtual-desktop coordinates and rotation mapped correctly.

ACCEPTANCE: the common Phase 2 session/input fault suite green on real Windows hardware with device evidence; capture-transition tests (lock/unlock, resolution change, GPU reset) logged; input refusal on elevated windows verified and reported as the typed limitation. Provenance: plan sections 8.3, 10.3, 23 Phase 2.

title: Service lifecycle and installers: idempotent registration, permission setup, honest uninstall
description:
WHY: Installation is where consent is established and where trust is most often burned. The installer must detect reality (Tailscale variant, permissions, certificates, conflicts, hardware) before advertising a working host, and uninstall must remove FrankenRemote without touching the user's Tailscale.

SCOPE: Per-OS installers/service registration (launchd family on macOS with signing/notarization; Windows service + interactive agent; systemd user/system units on Linux attached to the right graphical session): idempotent registration; setup flow that verifies tailnet connectivity, obtains OS permissions through signed user-visible paths (a headless service cannot complete consent), checks hardware encode support, provisions certificates, records sharing-scope and audio/file consent locally; only narrowly required firewall rules for the tailnet service; never enabling a public/LAN listener after failure; repair preserves consent without broadening it; uninstall removes services and files, leaves Tailscale and tailnet policy untouched; offline installation of packaged assets supported (cert issuance and Tailscale enrollment still need their own connectivity).

ACCEPTANCE: install/repair/uninstall cycles tested per OS with permission-state assertions before and after; packaging smoke tests (the Phase 2 exit requirement) green; failure-mode tests (no Tailscale, permission denied, port conflict) produce the typed setup guidance. Provenance: plan sections 20.3, 23 Phase 2.
notes:
REALITY-CHECK REMEDIATION (2026-09-23): Units must exec a working frd run (fr-0il). System unit: User=/Group= of the service account, NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=read-only, PrivateTmp=yes, RestrictAddressFamilies, CapabilityBoundingSet empty for the broker (the ingress helper gets only CAP_NET_ADMIN, fr-rc-transport-ingress-helper-6lx). No logs in /tmp (macOS plist logs to /tmp/frd.log today - symlink risk). Windows/macOS: refuse with a typed platform_unavailable until real services exist (today Windows writes JSON and tells the user to run 'sc start frd' without registering; launchd KeepAlive restarts a binary that refuses). service-status must check the unit is active, not just that the file exists.
2026-09-27 reality check #2: Audit gaps: the service units cannot carry --input-agent/--display/--headless; the system unit would restart-loop without DISPLAY; uninstall does not stop/disable the running service; no ingress-helper unit.
2026-09-28 PROGRESS 514af9b: frd install [flags] -- <frd run options> (systemd only) carries control/clipboard/files/audio/display/--logind-session into ExecStart, validated by frd run's RunOptions parser at install time with typed refusals (clipboard/files without --input-agent, system unit without --headless) and refusals for installer-owned flags/--once/relative paths; user units WantedBy=graphical-session.target (not default.target: no SSH-login restart loop); Restart=on-failure + RestartPreventExitStatus=2 (configuration refusals don't loop); uninstall prints stop/disable steps; uninstall JSON serde-built. Tests + planted negative (validation bypassed -> refusal test fails). STILL OPEN: ingress-helper unit activation needs root (rendered, not written - by design); macOS/Windows service paths remain refusals/unsupported; no live systemd run yet.

title: Shared clipboard: default-on bidirectional text sync with bounded transfers and echo prevention
description:
WHY: v1.4 declares the shared clipboard table stakes: copy on either side, paste on the other, automatically — while keeping the privacy and bounds discipline that stops it becoming a covert channel or a parser exploit.

SCOPE: Automatic bidirectional text clipboard synchronization between the controlling client and the host, DEFAULT-ON for the controlling session, visible off switch on both ends; one MiB validated UTF-8 per item (configurable), carried on its own bounded chunked channel with declared total length and chunk sequence — never smuggled through the 64 KiB control parser; sequence identifiers and source labels preventing echo loops; controller-only (read-only viewers get nothing); approval mode covers clipboard as observation; Linux portal clipboard requested before session Start and honored only per the returned grant; clipboard can be absent even where input works — typed capability row; reject invalid encodings and cancellation-sensitive partial transfers before publishing to the OS; session buffers cleared on closure (without promising to erase OS clipboard-manager history or overwrite newer local values); clipboard content NEVER in logs, error messages, URLs, or traces; image clipboard as a negotiated optional capability over the file-transfer channel (deferred follow-on, not this bead's blocker).

ACCEPTANCE: e2e copy/paste both directions on all three host OSes; echo-loop lab test; oversized/invalid-encoding refusal tests; a log-scrubbing test proving clipboard bytes never appear in diagnostics. Provenance: plan section 15.3 (v1.4), 10.1.
notes:
2026-09-27 reality check #2: Text clipboard WORKING for the controller at namespace scope (fr-input-agent --clipboard child; e2e real_clipboard both directions). Gaps vs scope: opt-in (--clipboard), not default-on; CLI refuses it with --send (fr-rc2-cli-clipboard-with-files-i9uk); image clipboard not started; live lane.

2026-11-09 implementation extension (plan 15.3; native qualification still open): Added the Mac CLIENT's default-on controlling UTF-8 clipboard on the original bounded clipboard lane, composable with upload/download commands and precise-scroll negotiation. A thread-confined NSPasteboard adapter observes throttled revision/type metadata, validates bounded complete UTF-8, suppresses only exact own-publication echoes, preserves local supersession, and clears private buffers without clearing the OS pasteboard. Original worker authority, switch generations and immutable item deadline are rechecked at each multi-call publication boundary; post-mutation failures retain UnknownEffect and fence further adapter work. The original viewer now has a visible immediate Turn Off control and bounded privacy heartbeat; reconnect, focus/control loss and display replacement do not revive used clipboard consent. CLI completion retains separate setup, submitted/unknown/refused publication, local Off and real cleanup evidence through later failures. Validation: actual native_profile target 20 passed with clipboard/plain/upload/download/duplex combinations; exact production backend Rust cargo check against real fr-core/fr-wire traits passed; portable revision/privacy policy tests 9 passed. Native private-board tests and six original NativeAccess runtime tests authored but not executed. Full frd/fr-native compilation remains blocked by the observed pinned Asupersync compiler OOM, and no macOS SDK/runtime is available. Mac HOST clipboard, all-three-host-OS live acceptance, and hardware/tailnet qualification remain incomplete; this is not a closure claim.

2026-11-09 host clipboard preparation: factored the existing bounded native process dispatcher for shared Linux/macOS use without changing X11 backend checks, and fixed a source-identified receipt race. A validated Published reply for the original Publish now survives a later privacy stop as its exact submitted/refused/unknown result while the worker is poisoned first; text reads and other responses remain fenced, and no later operation is sent. Six private-socket dispatcher tests and four deterministic parent IPC receipt regressions were authored and independently source-reviewed. The execution workspace became unavailable before validation; no runtime/native pass is claimed. Mac host integration follows separately; keep this bead in progress.

2026-11-10 Mac host clipboard implementation: wired default-on controlling shares through the existing isolated fr-input-agent --clipboard protocol to the shared native NSPasteboard backend. Separate main-thread local Off panel, bounded terminal UI heartbeat and independent parent-loss watchdog fence the original lane while native work may block; read-side shutdown preserves the write side only for a completed publication receipt. Prepared native bytes are consumed once with original revision/origin/deadline checks; raw nanosecond deadline projection only shortens the cap. Explicit --no-clipboard is preserved through real LaunchAgent installation/parser tests. Added private-pasteboard, command/parent-loss, deadline and installed-default regressions; Mac CI explicitly selects executor and broker suites. Independent source review completed; workspace execution became unavailable before validation, so no native/runtime pass is claimed. Corrected the nested test module path identified by first-batch source-format CI. Native Mac-host copy/paste, physical Off/provider-stall qualification, Windows and all-three-host-OS acceptance remain open.

2026-11-10 privacy timing correction: source review found that Mac readers sampled Instant before the heartbeat mutex; a preempted reader could then misclassify a newer UI pulse as rollback and permanently stop a healthy lane. Production now samples under the mutex in both client and host. Verified pinned Rust Apple Instant uses CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW (excludes sleep), whereas existing Darwin CLOCK_MONOTONIC includes it; the heartbeat retains both ages and expires at the original 250 ms cap in either domain. Clock failure/regression and a late UI turn after sleep are terminal. Original clipboard item deadlines and raw child-clock translation are unchanged. Deterministic injected-clock regression coverage added; runtime/native qualification remains separate, and this does not close the Mac host lock/logout gap.

title: Bounded viewer admission and controller handoff over shared pipelines
description:
WHY: The initial viewer limit is deliberately small — one controller plus two read-only viewers subject to resource admission — and shared-pipeline ownership is where multi-viewer systems usually corrupt authority or leak resources. Added only after single-controller behavior is correct.

SCOPE: Viewer admission against encoder sessions, GPU surfaces, bandwidth, and per-viewer memory; shared encoded streams only where codec configuration, viewport, and operating point match, extra encoder sessions through admission otherwise; shared pipelines owned by the OS share session region — closing one viewer never cancels another's encoder, last unsubscribe stops the pipeline, a failed shared pipeline suspends affected control/readiness while unrelated display pipelines continue; slow read-only viewers degraded or disconnected independently, never backpressuring the controller; controller handoff serialized in the authority owner — second requests observe, wait, or request handoff; handoff invalidates the old lease and releases its held state before admitting the new controller; a new controller is denied or explicitly handed off, never auto-substituted by arrival order; read-only viewers cannot move the host cursor, change the controller's viewport, use the clipboard, or force global quality changes; per-viewer counters (pipelines, encoder sessions, surfaces, cached bytes, queued repair).

ACCEPTANCE: lab properties for shared-pipeline lifetime and handoff serialization (kill first viewer of a shared encoder, disconnect a slow secondary, join a third during recovery — the plan's fault list); e2e three-viewer session with per-viewer budget logs. Provenance: plan sections 2.2, 7.1, 15.5, 24.2.

- [ ] Host-side connected-sessions list in the session agent UI: device name, role, capabilities in use (view/control/audio/clipboard/files), with per-session revoke — not just the aggregate indicator

title: Media-worker OS sandboxing and privilege reduction per platform
description:
WHY: A separate worker process gives crash/hang isolation by itself — NOT a security sandbox. Client decoders and host encoders both run foreign code on untrusted input, so the plan requires OS-supported containment compatible with GPU/capture access, and explicit documentation of residual trust where real enforcement is impossible. Claiming isolation that is not enforced is forbidden.

SCOPE: Per platform, apply and TEST the strongest sandbox compatible with the worker's GPU/capture needs: Windows — restricted tokens, job objects, reduced integrity, restricted inherited handles; macOS — sandbox profiles/entitlement minimization for the signed worker; Linux — namespaces, seccomp filters, and landlock where GPU access permits. Document the actual enforced restrictions on filesystem, IPC, network, process creation, and input APIs per OS, and record residual trust explicitly where an adapter cannot be meaningfully sandboxed (a compromised same-user unsandboxed worker is never claimed harmless). Workers continue to receive no Tailscale control socket, certificate keys, approval endpoint, or input-lease capability (enforced by the broker's role-capability IPC). Client decode workers get the same treatment: host-supplied HEVC is untrusted input to foreign code even on a trusted tailnet.

ACCEPTANCE: per-OS sandbox capability table (enforced / partial / not enforceable, with reasons) committed; escape-attempt tests for each enforced restriction (open a network socket, read outside allowed paths, reach the approval IPC — all must fail with logs); the shipped boundary tested as shipped, not as designed; residual-trust statements mirrored into SECURITY.md. Provenance: plan sections 5.4, 19.1, 19.2.
notes:
REFINEMENT 4 (2026-09-23): The capture/encode worker role runs with no seccomp filter (only the decoder/presenter role is filtered, crates/fr-native/src/bin/media_worker.rs:87); add a qualified filter for the capture/encode role (X11 + FFmpeg/x265 syscalls) or record the residual trust explicitly; worker executable path should get the ownership/permission checks fr-tailnet's protected_executable applies (crates/frd/src/worker.rs:117 checks only absoluteness).
2026-09-27 reality check #2: The client Opus decode child fr-opus-worker is contained (no_new_privs, TSYNC seccomp, RLIMIT_AS, close_range; 20c49ef/7e15e31) alongside the HEVC decoder worker. title: Android app: native Kotlin/Jetpack Compose application over the shared core
description:
WHY: The Android counterpart to the iOS bead: first-class Kotlin/Jetpack Compose UI in mobile/android, same shared core, same authority discipline, with Android's own media and lifecycle rules respected.

SCOPE: Compose app: machine picker/saved hosts/links, session viewer decoding to a Surface via MediaCodec (never copying decoded pixels through Rust memory), trackpad and direct-touch modes, keyboard including hardware keyboards and IME committed-text semantics (composition local until committed; cancelled on session replacement), pan/zoom with the defined transforms, talk toggle with Android mic permission, file send/receive via SAF within scoped-storage limits, settings/quality panel/permission explanations; lifecycle: background releases control, resume = fresh lease + recovery point, rotation requires current mapping, network transitions re-evaluate the route and never carry stale authority; predictive back, edge-to-edge, dark theme, TalkBack labels; signing per platform mechanism. Media APIs remain foreign trust boundaries even behind safe-looking wrappers — decode admission against negotiated limits before configuration.

ACCEPTANCE: real-device session against each host OS; background/resume and rotation authority tests green; thermal steady-state decode measured; e2e scripts with logcat capture; UI review against platform conventions. Provenance: plan sections 14.4, 16.2 (v1.4), 23 Phase 3.

title: Browser audio: Opus playback path and getUserMedia microphone uplink
description:
WHY: Browser clients need both directions too: play the host's audio, and speak into the host's virtual mic — within the browser's gesture, permission, and worklet constraints.

SCOPE: Downlink: probe an actual supported Opus decode/output path; the fallback is a small WASM Opus decoder feeding an AudioWorklet with bounded preallocated work, no network fetches or blocking calls in the worklet; bounded ring/credit protocol with transferable buffers as baseline (SharedArrayBuffer only as an optional optimization with its cross-origin-isolation requirements stated, never an unmentioned prerequisite); audio starts on a browser-permitted user gesture and stops on lifecycle transitions; measure worklet/buffer overhead on phones before claiming low added latency. Uplink: getUserMedia capture behind the same explicit talk toggle, browser permission prompt respected, Opus encode within the bounded WASM budget, the standard uplink sequence/generation rules, indicator visible.

ACCEPTANCE: Chrome and Safari playback + talk e2e against a real host; hidden-tab and gesture-requirement behavior verified; buffer-depth and added-latency measurements recorded per browser. Provenance: plan sections 15.4, 16.3.

title: Browser qualification matrix: Chrome and Safari rows with decode-path evidence
description:
WHY: The v1.3 bar makes current Chrome and Safari the qualification target; this bead produces the evidence-backed matrix that says exactly which browser/OS/hardware combinations are supported, degraded (WSS), or unsupported — 'WebCodecs exists' is not an acceptance test.

SCOPE: For each combination (Chrome on Windows/macOS/Linux-with-hw-caveats; Safari on macOS/iOS-adjacent): exact browser version, OS build, codec probe output, transport mode achieved (WebTransport vs WSS), decode-path evidence (hardware vs software), presentation behavior including the idle/first-frame/last-frame/low-cadence cases, input capability rows (keyboard lock, pointer lock, clipboard, fullscreen), audio both ways, file-transfer capability; each row passed/failed/blocked/not tested; the published matrix distinguishes supported, degraded, and unsupported and feeds fr doctor and the README known-restrictions list.

ACCEPTANCE: the matrix committed with retained probe outputs per row; unsupported combinations produce the typed in-product explanation; matrix wired into the release-evidence flow. Provenance: plan sections 16.3, 24.4, v1.3 note.

title: Browser origin security: exact-Origin checks, nonce bootstrap, ticket attachment, CSP
description:
WHY: Tailscale authenticates the connecting NODE, not the web origin running on it. A hostile page on an admitted machine must gain nothing. This is release-blocking security, not browser polish.

SCOPE: Serve the UI only from the configured host HTTPS origin; validate configured Host/authority (and SNI where exposed); require the EXACT expected Origin for all state-changing requests and WebSocket/WebTransport establishment; deny wildcard CORS, null origins, cross-origin fetches, and state changes via GET (a navigation GET serves only static content — never a ticket, lease, or capture start); Fetch Metadata as defense in depth, never the sole test; short-lived one-use nonce via origin-checked same-origin HTTPS POST, bound to verified peer + requested session/role, required before any sensitive operation; non-executable JSON with no-store/nosniff (no JSONP, no nonce-bearing scripts); since browser sockets cannot carry custom handshake headers, authenticate the application session in a bounded FIRST reliable message after the origin-checked transport opens — until then no pixels, audio, input, codec work, or directory expansion; every auxiliary channel attaches with a role-specific one-use ticket (a bare session ID attaches nothing); nonces/tickets never in query strings, links, logs, or referrers; unauthenticated handshakes rate-limited, unused tickets expired; restrictive CSP, frame-ancestors 'none', safe referrer policy, no-store on sensitive responses; browser state invalidated on session closure; native WSS clients follow the same origin/nonce contract — missing Origin is not an alternate authentication mode.

ACCEPTANCE: attack tests from the plan's list — malicious iframes, DNS rebinding/Host tricks, cross-origin WebSockets, stale/replayed tickets, bfcache restoration, request smuggling/header ambiguity in the selected HTTP stack — all refused with typed logs; CSP verified by automated header assertions. Provenance: plan sections 16.4, 24.3.
notes: REALITY-CHECK REMEDIATION (2026-09-23): Before wiring anything, fix fr-rc-sec-csprng-nonces-go6 (predictable SHA-256 nonces/tickets). The origin checks are sound as a library but no HTTP/H3/WSS server exists in frd; acceptance requires attack tests over real sockets against the real listener (malicious iframe, cross-origin WebSocket/WebTransport, DNS rebinding/Host tricks, replayed tickets, bfcache restore, request smuggling in the chosen HTTP stack). CSP should drop style-src 'unsafe-inline'.

title: File transfer on mobile and browser within platform file-access limits
description:
WHY: File send/receive is core scope; mobile and browser platforms constrain file access (document pickers, SAF, browser download/upload sandboxes), so the capability ships within those limits with honest capability rows rather than pretending desktop semantics.

SCOPE: iOS: send via share sheet/document picker, receive into the app's Documents with export via share sheet. Android: SAF-based pick/send and receive with scoped storage. Browser: upload via file input/drag-drop; receive as browser-mediated download (the viewer sandbox rules mean downloads are user-gesture-bound; label what is and is not possible per browser). All platforms reuse the ATP channel, budgets, atomic publication, and path-safety rules from the desktop bead; capability rows per platform recorded (e.g., folder sync explicitly desktop-only in v1); progress UI in each client.

ACCEPTANCE: e2e send/receive per platform with disconnect/resume where the platform permits; capability rows in the matrix; refusal paths (unsupported direction on a platform) typed and user-legible. Provenance: plan section 15.6 (v1.4), 16.2, 16.3.

title: iOS app: native SwiftUI application over the shared core
description:
WHY: v1.4 makes the iOS client a first-class native SwiftUI application — platform-conventional, polished, in this monorepo under mobile/ios — not a thin wrapper around a Rust view.

SCOPE: SwiftUI app: machine picker (saved hosts + host links; no bearer tokens in links), session viewer with VideoToolbox decode output to native display layers/Metal (never the UI toolkit's image path), trackpad mode and direct-touch mode with visibly different semantics, long press/secondary click/scroll/modifier keys/explicit text entry discoverable, software+hardware keyboard support with IME composition as local state committed explicitly (cancelled on view/session replacement, never replayed into a different desktop), pan/zoom with the defined coordinate transform (local zoom = client transform; host crop = acknowledged mapping generation), the talk toggle with iOS mic permission, file send/receive within iOS file-access limits (share sheet / document picker), settings, connection-quality panel, permission explanations; lifecycle: backgrounding releases control, resume obtains a fresh lease and recovery frame (never replaying queued taps), orientation changes require a current client mapping, network transitions (Wi-Fi/cellular) re-evaluate the VPN route — migration never overrides changed peer identity or expired authority; safe areas, dynamic type, dark mode, accessibility labels; signing/entitlements per platform mechanism.

title: Mobile FFI boundary: Swift package and Kotlin/JNI bindings over fr-client
description:
WHY: v1.4 commits both mobile apps to first-class native UIs over the shared Rust core through ONE narrow audited boundary per platform — all logic stays in Rust; the bindings move calls, callbacks, and buffers, nothing more.

SCOPE: Per the mobile-FFI decision note: a C-ABI surface over fr-client (session lifecycle, host connection, display/viewport state, input submission, capability/diagnostic queries, media handles for platform decode paths, audio uplink control, file-transfer operations) with lifecycle-safe handle semantics (no use-after-free reachable from Swift/Kotlin misuse — handles generation-checked at the boundary); a Swift package wrapping it idiomatically (async/await bridging to the Rust core's completion model, Sendable-correct types); a Kotlin/JNI wrapper equally idiomatic (coroutines bridging, no leaked global refs); build integration in-monorepo — repository-owned commands build the Rust core for iOS (aarch64-apple-ios) and Android (aarch64/armv7 as decided) targets and package the XCFramework/AAR; the boundary is audited like fr-ffi: documented ownership, callback threading, and shutdown order.

CONSTRAINTS: no product logic in bindings; decoded video never routed through the FFI as CPU pixels — media handles hand off to VideoToolbox/MediaCodec platform paths.

ACCEPTANCE: binding unit tests on both platforms (including deliberate misuse: double-free, stale handle, callback after shutdown — all safely refused); a headless smoke connecting to a real host from an iOS simulator/Android emulator where transport permits, else on-device; CI lane building both packages from the monorepo. Provenance: plan section 16.2 (v1.4), P0 decision notes.
notes: REALITY-CHECK REMEDIATION (2026-09-23): The current mobile_ffi.rs is fake (connect flips a flag; input discarded) and its JNI signatures are undefined behavior (jstring/jobject read as *const c_char / *mut struct); fr-rc-truth-neutralize-fakes-ny0 gates it off desktop targets. Rebuild over fr-client after fr-rc-budget-one-client-core-clw: C ABI with generation-checked handles; JNI via proper JNIEnv string/object access (or a vetted binding generator per the decision note); crate-type staticlib/cdylib; XCFramework and AAR produced by scripts/build-mobile.sh in CI; misuse tests (double free, stale handle, wrong thread).

title: Mobile qualification: thermal, lifecycle, rotation, and network-transition evidence
description:
WHY: Phones fail differently: thermal throttling, aggressive background suspension, IME complexity, and route flapping. The Phase 3 exit gate needs device evidence that none of these can preserve stale control or misrepresent the decode envelope.

SCOPE: On representative iOS and Android hardware (recorded models/OS builds): sustained-decode thermal equilibrium (not cool-phone bursts) at the negotiated operating points; background/foreground cycling under memory pressure with authority assertions after every resume; rotation during active control; Wi-Fi-to-cellular and cellular-to-Wi-Fi transitions mid-session (route re-evaluation, identity revalidation, no stale-authority carryover — mobile suspension may prevent clean client teardown, which is exactly why host lease expiry is mandatory: verify it fires); IME composition cancelled across reconnects; hardware-keyboard rows; audio both ways on-device; capability matrix rows filled per device.

ACCEPTANCE: the mobile rows of the capability matrix with retained measurements; every lifecycle test logged with host-side authority traces proving expiry did its job. Provenance: plan sections 16.2, 23 Phase 3, 24.2.

title: fr-web: WASM state machine, JS boundary, WebCodecs pipeline, self-hosted assets
description:
WHY: The browser client runs the SAME Rust core compiled to WASM, with a deliberately narrow JavaScript boundary for what only the browser can do — transport handles, WebCodecs, presentation, DOM input, audio nodes. Chrome and Safari are the qualification bar (v1.3).

SCOPE: fr-web WASM entrypoint over fr-client; JS boundary modules for WebTransport (and WSS), VideoDecoder configuration from exact negotiated hvcC with complete access units (one EncodedVideoChunk per admitted AU, correct key/delta designation, timestamps in API units; in-band parameter-set changes rejected until renegotiation), presentation to a browser surface, keyboard/pointer/pointer-lock/fullscreen capture with browser-reserved-shortcut capability rows, lifecycle handling (pagehide, bfcache restoration, hidden-tab throttling, decoder reclamation, worker failure) each triggering a fresh usable-view check before control resumes — hidden tabs never preserve input authority; VideoFrame objects closed promptly with bounded decode queue AND renderer retention, worker-based decode where supported, no per-frame flush; asset serving from frd — self-hosted, no CDN, no third-party scripts/fonts/analytics, bounded sizes, version handshake so a stale cached client renegotiates or reloads without replaying input; no service-worker authority; the browser build inherits zero desktop FFI (feature-graph enforced).

ACCEPTANCE: real Chrome session against a real host end to end; lifecycle tests (tab hide, bfcache, decoder reset) proving authority never survives staleness, with browser-console and host logs captured; asset-version skew test. Provenance: plan sections 16.3, 23 Phase 3.

ADDED SCOPE (polish round 1): the browser client's user interface itself — machine entry (saved hosts and host links; no local-API enumeration in a browser), session viewer chrome, input toolbar and mode controls, the talk toggle, connection-quality panel, permission/capability explanations (including the typed unsupported-combination message from the probe), and settings — kept deliberately small, self-hosted, dependency-free, and consistent with the desktop shells' information architecture. UI tests: capability-refusal rendering, stale-asset version-handshake reload, and keyboard-capture indicator states, driven through the e2e harness with browser console + host logs captured.
notes: REALITY-CHECK REMEDIATION (2026-09-23): The current fr-web + app.js is a mockup (no wasm-bindgen; invented JSON protocol; hard-coded hvc1.1.6.L93.B0 regardless of stream; auth_ok grants control; worker.js drops delta frames and keeps decoding - broken references). Rebuild as fr-client compiled to WASM with a narrow JS boundary; codec string from the negotiated hvcC; one EncodedVideoChunk per admitted access unit; no delta dropping (skip presentation, never references); control only after observation + readiness + lease; served by frd over a real H3/WebTransport listener (and WSS fallback) - neither exists yet.

title: WSS compatibility profile: bound channels, receiver credit, honest degradation labeling
description:
WHY: WSS is the explicit degraded fallback for browsers without qualified WebTransport (expected: some Safari versions) and for native clients behind hostile networks. It must keep every authorization and expiry semantic while being honest that TCP head-of-line exists.

SCOPE: Separately bound control, video, and audio WSS channels, each attached to the admitted peer/session via role-specific one-use capabilities; a media replacement never implicitly acquires a fresh controller; if the implementation multiplexes over one TCP connection, the shared-transport limitation is labeled; bounded application send queues PLUS receiver-granted outstanding-byte/frame credit for media (bufferedAmount is outbound-only; browser WS has no receive backpressure — the host never sends merely because its socket accepts bytes); credits returned only when the application frees receive budget; receipt/decode/presentation acks distinguishable; stale-channel replacement fences the old generation immediately, stops writing, closes from the capable endpoint, ignores late old-generation data; bounded concurrent closing channels with backoff so resets cannot become their own attack; input lease retention governed by view freshness, never socket-open state; compression disabled for media and sensitive control; clipboard stays off the input channel; the profile is labeled degraded in diagnostics and never presented as datagram-equivalent.

ACCEPTANCE: credit-starvation and channel-replacement lab tests; an e2e browser session forced onto WSS with measured behavior recorded separately from native-datagram results; downgrade attempts that would remove security checks rejected. Provenance: plan sections 12.5, 17.3.
