title: Stop fabricating agent/CLI results: fr robot, fr disconnect, fr status/inspect hard-codes become typed refusals
description:
BACKGROUND (shared by every reality-check bead): a reality check on 2026-09-23 at source revision e1d9cc2 (README, both AGENTS.md, plan v1.4 read in full; six independent code audits; binaries run against a live tailnet; gates executed) found that FrankenRemote is not usable as a remote desktop: `frd run` binds UDP on the tailnet addresses and discards every packet (crates/frd/src/bin/frd.rs:504-512); admission refuses every real tailnet peer because it requires Node.MachineAuthorized, which real tailscaled does not return for peers; the shipped asupersync =0.5.0 cannot decode QUIC frame types 0x07/0x18/0x19; the only client path (`fr connect`) is view-only. A Sept 19-22 burst (+118k net Rust lines, 65 bead closures including every phase gate) added fabricated success surfaces (frd status fixture, fr doctor rows, fr robot, fr disconnect), fabricated GNOME/KDE/Windows-GPU qualification tables, counter-incrementing platform adapters, a fake mobile FFI, a simulated e2e harness and hard-coded latency constants. The handwritten-Rust counter reads 268,798 (hard stop 250,000); CI's Rust lane has been red since Sept 19 at `cargo fmt --check`, so no CI test step has executed since. 46 false-closed beads were reopened in commit 6fbd380. Genuine assets to build on: fr-core authority/input submission gate, fr-media bounded delivery + HEVC parameter-set guard, fr-wire codecs (51/59 kinds), fr-transport QUIC records over real UDP/TLS, fr-tailnet LocalAPI client, fr-native X11 capture->x265->libavcodec->XPutImage worker with a real seccomp decoder sandbox, XTest input, libopus, PulseAudio playback, and the frd host library (serve_serial, run_native_shared_desktop, shared hub) that is correct but unreachable from any binary.

RULES THAT APPLY: AGENTS.md RULE 1 - no file or directory may be deleted without the owner's explicit written permission in the same session (ask; never assume). Asupersync is the only runtime. HEVC-only / Opus-only. Evidence categories are separate (source / build / simulation / interop / hardware); a row is passed, failed, blocked or not tested - never 'supported with caveats'. Never present fixtures as live proof. Stage files by explicit path; other agents work in the same checkout.

WHY: Plan section 18 requires every robot response to distinguish success from partial submission, cancellation, refusal or unknown external effect. Today the robot surface fabricates all of it, which is worse than having no surface: an agent that 'observes' and 'inputs' through it will believe actions happened that never happened.

CURRENT STATE (crates/fr-native/src/bin/fr_cli/linux/robot.rs): `session open` (:196-209) returns 'active' with a random lease and never connects; `observe` (:245-285) returns a hard-coded 1920x1080 'fresh' frame and writes a 10-byte dummy PNG header to --screenshot, labeled with whatever evidence level the caller asks for; `input` (:390-425) reports every action SubmittedToOs/Committed and 'Verified via authorized terminal semantic adapter' when the caller passes --semantic-evidence adapter; `run_disconnect` (:147-170) reports closed:true, cleanup_confirmed:true at stage Observed with no I/O; `fr status` hard-codes active_sessions_count:0 (:63); `fr inspect` hard-codes displays_count:1 and requires_approval:true (:119-120) and matches names by prefix (:95-99) although the CLI promises exact FQDNs. crates/fr-native/tests/fr_cli.rs:399 asserts the fake flow.

SCOPE: Until a live local client session backs them (fr-agent-robot-surface-3o3), every robot subcommand and `fr disconnect` returns the standard envelope with outcome 'refused', error.code 'robot_surface_unavailable' (or 'not_implemented'), a specific next_action, and a non-zero exit; no file is written for --screenshot. `fr status` omits or reports unknown session counts rather than 0; `fr inspect` reports displays/approval as unknown unless actually probed, and uses exact canonical-FQDN matching. Replace the fake-flow test with tests asserting the refusals.

CONSTRAINTS: keep the JSON envelope schema stable (schema_version, timestamps, typed error, next_action); do not delete the robot module (the real implementation will reuse its types).

ACCEPTANCE: transcripts of each command on a machine with no host show typed refusals and exit codes; unit tests cover every refusal; `rg -n 'raw_dummy|cleanup_confirmed: true' crates` finds nothing outside tests.
notes:
TESTS & LOGGING (refinement 2026-09-23): Unit tests: one per robot subcommand/flag combination asserting outcome=refused, the typed code, exit status, and that no file is created for --screenshot; exact-FQDN matching tests for fr inspect (prefix of another host must NOT match). E2E script scripts/e2e/robot_refusals.sh runs every command against a machine with no host and saves stdout/stderr/exit codes as an evidence artifact. Log: one structured line per refusal with command, code and next_action (no host names in exported diagnostics).
CLOSED 2026-09-24 (refusal-only truth fix; its scope was the refusals). Commits a11f01e + 08c0243. Re-executed against the built fr: disconnect -> exit 2 no_background_session; robot session open/close/observe/input -> exit 2 robot_surface_unavailable; status on a missing socket -> exit 1 tailscale_unavailable; inspect of an unknown node on the live installed LocalAPI -> exit 1 peer_not_found. No 'raw_dummy|cleanup_confirmed: true' outside tests. Tests: fr_cli.rs robot_surface_refuses_every_subcommand_without_side_effects (asserts no --screenshot file) and status_needs_localapi_and_disconnect_refuses_without_a_background_session; unit test inspect_matches_exact_stable_id_or_canonical_name_never_a_prefix. The separate scripts/e2e/robot_refusals.sh evidence script was NOT written: the integration tests already run each command as a real process, so it would duplicate them (ceremony). SELF-VERIFIED ONLY. fr-agent-robot-surface-3o3 (the real capability) stays open.
close_reason: Refusal-only truth fix delivered (a11f01e, 08c0243); self-verified; capability bead fr-agent-robot-surface-3o3 stays open

title: Age-optimal capture/re-present timing: 'update or wait' threshold + split-conformal encode-time bounds
description:
BACKGROUND (reality check #2, 2026-09-27 at b6aca68 -> 79d6f46): FrankenRemote now works as a Linux-X11 remote desktop between two processes in an isolated network namespace: `frd run` (tailnet-bound listener, nftables ingress or the root `frd ingress-helper`, Tailscale-cert TLS, WhoIs own-user admission, XShm capture -> x265 -> Asupersync QUIC) serves `fr connect` (seccomp-sandboxed libavcodec decode, X11 presentation) for viewing and, with `frd run --input-agent` + `fr connect --control`, control (keys, buttons, absolute pointer, wheel) with a per-lease out-of-process XTest executor, cursor forwarding, clipboard, host playback audio (view-only; client Opus decode in a restricted child), and viewer->host file sending. Proof = namespace e2e tests with real processes and planted negatives in crates/frd/tests/native_host_linux_serial/ (run: build fr/fr-media-worker/fr-input-agent/fr-opus-worker with `-p fr-native --features linux-desktop,linux-displays,linux-input,linux-clipboard,linux-audio`, `-p frd --bin frd`, then `FR_NS_SUDO=1 scripts/test_linux_serial_lifecycle.sh <native_host_linux_serial test binary>`). NOT yet: any live two-machine run, QUIC interop (workspace pins asupersync =0.5.0), more than one peer at a time (serial listener), hardware HEVC, non-X11 platforms.

RULES (AGENTS.md, binding): no file deletion without the owner's written permission; Asupersync is the only runtime; HEVC/Opus only; typed refusals, never silent fallback; every queue bounded in count AND bytes; clipboard/input/pixels/file names never in logs; evidence categories are separate and a namespace e2e is NOT live evidence; no weakened assertions, no fixtures presented as live proof; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and tests must pass; stage by explicit path; other agents push to main concurrently (verify, rebase, never force-push).

WHY: zero-wait updating is not age-optimal when service times vary (Sun, Uysal-Biyikoglu, Yates, Koksal & Shroff 2017, "Update or Wait"); our x265 encode time varies up to 169 ms under load. Deciding before encoding whether a re-present can land inside the display budget needs a bound on the next encode time; split conformal prediction gives a distribution-free (1-α) upper bound from a rolling window with finite-sample coverage under exchangeability.

SCOPE: (a) a pure, deterministic waiting-threshold policy for capture scheduling driven by the running mean/variance of encode time; (b) a split-conformal upper bound on encode+decode time used by fr-rc2-static-view-represent to skip hopeless re-presents; both replayable in the Asupersync lab from sanitized traces; AoI (fr-rc-media-aoi-kpi-ljg) as the objective.

ACCEPTANCE: property tests (monotone threshold, coverage >= 1-α on synthetic exchangeable traces); lab replay shows lower mean presented age than zero-wait on a heavy-tailed encode trace; no effect on correctness/freshness invariants.

title: Host playback audio in controlled sessions via the restricted Opus child (refused today)
description:

Proof = namespace e2e tests with real processes and planted negatives in crates/frd/tests/native_host_linux_serial/ (run: build fr/fr-media-worker/fr-input-agent/fr-opus-worker with `-p fr-native --features linux-desktop,linux-displays,linux-input,linux-clipboard,linux-audio`, `-p frd --bin frd`, then `FR_NS_SUDO=1 scripts/test_linux_serial_lifecycle.sh <native_host_linux_serial test binary>`). RULES (AGENTS.md, binding): no file deletion without the owner's written permission; Asupersync is the only runtime; HEVC/Opus only; typed refusals, never silent fallback; every queue bounded in count AND bytes; clipboard/input/pixels/file names never in logs; evidence categories are separate and a namespace e2e is NOT live evidence; no weakened assertions, no fixtures presented as live proof; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and tests must pass; stage by explicit path; other agents push to main concurrently (verify, rebase, never force-push).

WHY: plan §15.4 audio for any session. `fr connect --control --audio` is refused (`audio_control_unsupported`, crates/fr-native/src/bin/fr_cli/options.rs:638-643; its text still says "in-process decode", stale since 7e15e31) and the controlled share carries no audio (crates/frd/src/session_agent/source/desktop/native/controlled.rs:180-183). The original reason — decode on the controlling session thread puts media work on the authority path — no longer holds: client Opus decode runs in a restricted per-epoch child (fr-opus-worker; 20c49ef/7e15e31).

SCOPE: the controlled share attaches audio-down like the observe path (host --audio stays the local enable; per-viewer epochs; bounded ring); the controller decodes via the restricted child; no audio work on the input authority path (by construction + test); refusal text fixed.

ACCEPTANCE: namespace e2e: control + audio — tone detected on the client sink (Goertzel, as real_audio.rs) while input reaches the host; control revocation stops audio; planted negatives: host sends no packets / client drops before playout -> fails; real_audio and real_control still pass.
notes:
REFINEMENT R1 (2026-09-27): Add an authority-isolation test: SIGSTOP the fr-opus-worker child mid-session -> input keeps landing on the host and lease renewals continue; audio reports a typed stall; SIGCONT or kill -> audio recovers or ends typed while control is unaffected.
2026-09-28 SCOPING (read-only, before implementation; nothing changed): this is larger than the bead's SCOPE says, in three ways. (1) SPEC: PROTOCOL.md 'native-audio-down' paragraph says the AudioDown attachment is 'observers only' (also fr-transport quic/attachment.rs:224-232 refuses it on a RequestControl selection). Plan 15.4 (higher authority) says playback audio is 'active only for an admitted session that requests it', i.e. any session; the protocol's narrowing was a first-slice limit whose stated reason (in-process decode on the controlling session thread) no longer holds since the restricted fr-opus-worker child. Implementing this bead therefore includes amending that PROTOCOL.md sentence to follow plan 15.4 - an owner-visible normative change, surfaced here rather than done silently. (2) CLIENT: the Opus decode is isolated (fr-native opus/process.rs supervisor never waits), but PulseAudio playout (fr-native pulse.rs: 'Run on a supervised audio worker or a view-only session thread, never the input-authority thread') runs on the session thread today, which in a controlled session is the input path. Needed: a dedicated bounded playout thread behind ViewerAudioOutput (bounded count+bytes record inbox, atomic live/stop fence, epoch-tagged AudioConfigured slot and failure flag so a stale epoch's ack/failure never counts, a small cap on live playout threads like ProcessDecoder's MAX_WORKERS) - one path for view-only and control, not two. Report becomes Arc<Mutex<..>>. title: Control grant = requested ∧ host policy ∧ probed executor capabilities (static LineScroll grant breaks all control on some X servers)
description:
BACKGROUND (reality check #2, 2026-09-27 at b6aca68 -> 79d6f46): FrankenRemote now works as a Linux-X11 remote desktop between two processes in an isolated network namespace: `frd run` (tailnet-bound listener, nftables ingress or the root `frd ingress-helper`, Tailscale-cert TLS, WhoIs own-user admission, XShm capture -> x265 -> Asupersync QUIC) serves `fr connect` (seccomp-sandboxed libavcodec decode, X11 presentation) for viewing and, with `frd run --input-agent` + `fr connect --control`, control (keys, buttons, absolute pointer, wheel) with a per-lease out-of-process XTest executor, cursor forwarding, clipboard, host playback audio (view-only; client Opus decode in a restricted child), and viewer->host file sending. Proof = namespace e2e tests with real processes and planted negatives in crates/frd/tests/native_host_linux_serial/ (run: build fr/fr-media-worker/fr-input-agent/fr-opus-worker with `-p fr-native --features linux-desktop,linux-displays,linux-input,linux-clipboard,linux-audio`, `-p frd --bin frd`, then `FR_NS_SUDO=1 scripts/test_linux_serial_lifecycle.sh <native_host_linux_serial test binary>`). NOT yet: any live two-machine run, QUIC interop (workspace pins asupersync =0.5.0), more than one peer at a time (serial listener), hardware HEVC, non-X11 platforms.

RULES (AGENTS.md, binding): no file deletion without the owner's written permission; Asupersync is the only runtime; HEVC/Opus only; typed refusals, never silent fallback; every queue bounded in count AND bytes; clipboard/input/pixels/file names never in logs; evidence categories are separate and a namespace e2e is NOT live evidence; no weakened assertions, no fixtures presented as live proof; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and tests must pass; stage by explicit path; other agents push to main concurrently (verify, rebase, never force-push).

WHY (defect, breaks control): the host grants remote-control capabilities statically. crates/frd/src/host_run.rs control_capabilities() includes LineScroll since cbd2ac4; the client requests Keys|Repeat|Absolute|Buttons|LineScroll (crates/fr-native/src/bin/fr_cli/linux/control.rs:45-52); the host Decider passes the REQUESTED set as `required` to the per-lease executor factory (crates/frd/src/session_agent/source/desktop/native/controlled.rs:444-470); RemoteSink::start requires the child's Ready capabilities to contain all of it (crates/frd/src/input_process.rs:283). The fr-input-agent child advertises LineScroll only with relative XTest (XTest >= 2.1 and exactly one X screen) and logical buttons 4-7 uniquely mapped (crates/fr-native/src/input.rs:177,599-601; input/scroll.rs:20-41). Consequence: on a multi-screen X server, or one whose pointer map lacks 6/7, ALL control fails (as a non-specific NativeNotReady, grant.rs:555-559) instead of only losing the wheel.

DESIGN (final abstraction; plan §15.1, §7): the grant is a lattice meet: grant = requested ∧ host policy ∧ executor-probed capabilities. The client marks LineScroll (later Text/Relative) OPTIONAL; missing REQUIRED capabilities -> typed refusal naming the capability; missing OPTIONAL ones -> granted without them and reported to the client (completion record `control_capabilities_granted`, `wheel_unavailable`). The executor's capabilities are known BEFORE the grant: either a probe run of fr-input-agent at controlled-share start (opens the display, replies Ready with capabilities, shows no indicator, injects nothing, exits) or ordering the first lease child's Ready before the grant reply — pick the one that preserves "no input before grant" and "indicator visible before any input". The per-lease child still re-verifies. Rejected: silently dropping LineScroll host-side; retrying without it; removing LineScroll from the defaults.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) property tests: meet idempotent/commutative/monotone; grant ⊆ each input; required ⊆ grant or typed refusal. (2) namespace e2e A: host Xvfb whose pointer map lacks buttons 6/7 (XSetPointerMapping via the python ctypes harness) -> control still works (keys/clicks observed on the host by the independent X client) and the completion reports wheel unavailable. (3) namespace e2e B: normal Xvfb -> an XTest wheel notch on the viewer window reaches the host as button 4/5 (adds wheel to the control e2e). (4) PLANTED NEGATIVE: the static grant makes e2e A fail (show the line). (5) fmt/clippy/tests green; README/docs updated.

TESTS & LOGGING: e2e prints requested, probed and granted sets and the outcome (content-free).
notes:
REFINEMENT R1 (2026-09-27): Add to ACCEPTANCE: (6) a missing REQUIRED capability (e.g. Keys) yields a typed refusal naming it, shown by fr connect with its exit code (unit + CLI test); (7) fr connect prints the granted set; (8) both new e2e cases pass 5/5 at low load (record the load average).
2026-09-27 REFINED DESIGN + re-prioritised P0 -> P2. The wire contract forbids a host-side meet (fr-wire control.rs:38-40: the host 'never clamps a peer target or grants an unrequested capability'; Granted echoes the Request), and the request is one-use (request_control may be called once), so the client must know the executor's capabilities BEFORE requesting. Protocol-consistent path: (1) fr-input-agent --probe mode (open the display, compute capabilities exactly as the lease child does, print, exit; no indicator, no input); frd run probes once at startup with --input-agent and refuses typed if Keys/Repeat/Absolute/Buttons are missing; host policy = probe AND static policy; (2) a new OPTIONAL negotiated capability (e.g. native-input-line-scroll v1) offered by the host only when the probe has LineScroll, offered optionally by fr's control offers; (3) fr requests LineScroll only when selected, and reports wheel_unavailable otherwise; (4) raise fr-wire negotiation MAX_CAPABILITIES 16 -> 24 (a code-level bound only; PROTOCOL.md does not fix a count) because the combined clipboard+files control offer is already at 16. Residual: a pointer-map change after startup still fails that lease as NativeNotReady. Priority lowered because the trigger (multi-screen 'Zaphod' X servers, or wheel buttons 6/7 unmapped) is uncommon; default Xorg/Xvfb maps them and control works there (namespace e2e).
2026-09-29 claimed (ClaudeOpus). Tests: unit (fr-core, fr-wire, fr-client, frd fixture probe modes), real-child Xvfb probe test (default map has LineScroll; logical 7 unmapped -> core without LineScroll; no window created, pointer unmoved), ns e2e: wheel notch reaches host as button 4 in the main control e2e; new a_host_without_wheel_buttons_grants_control_without_the_wheel. 2026-09-29 IMPLEMENTED at 3f927de (not self-closing: ready for independent verification). Acceptance vs code: (1) meet lattice: crates/fr-core/tests/capability_meet.rs exhaustive 256x256 (idempotent/commutative/monotone/never grows) + frd host_run grantable (probe never widens policy; each missing core op named) + fr-wire requestable; (2) e2e A real_control::a_host_without_wheel_buttons_grants_control_without_the_wheel (host pointer map lacks logical 6/7 before frd run starts): click reaches host, wheel notch stays local, completion control_capabilities_granted=[keys,repeat,absolute_pointer,buttons], wheel_unavailable=true - 2/2; (3) e2e B: fr_connect_control_drives_the_host_desktop_through_frd_run now requires a viewer wheel notch to reach the host window as button-4 press+release and line_scroll in the granted set - 2/2; (4) PLANTED NEGATIVE: static grant restored in a scratch build -> e2e A fails 2/2 (whole grant fails: host viewer failed, client transport_deadline_expired); (5) fmt/clippy/tests green (frd lib 2-4 per-run load flakes each pass alone 3/3; see 6d8); README/PROTOCOL/docs/CHANGELOG updated; (6) missing core capability -> frd run refuses at startup control_capability_missing (unit) and probe failure input_agent_unavailable; (7) fr prints the granted set (JSON field + human text 'wheel unavailable'); (8) 2/2 each at load ~150-170 (5/5 not run: machine load never below ~140 today). Real-child Xvfb probe test (input_process_x11): probe equals in-process open, default map has LineScroll, logical 7 unmapped -> no LineScroll, no window created, pointer unmoved. title: frd run binds and enforces ingress on the node's IPv6 tailnet address too (IPv4-only today)
description:
BACKGROUND (reality check #2, 2026-09-27 at b6aca68 -> 79d6f46): FrankenRemote now works as a Linux-X11 remote desktop between two processes in an isolated network namespace: `frd run` (tailnet-bound listener, nftables ingress or the root `frd ingress-helper`, Tailscale-cert TLS, WhoIs own-user admission, XShm capture -> x265 -> Asupersync QUIC) serves `fr connect` (seccomp-sandboxed libavcodec decode, X11 presentation) for viewing and, with `frd run --input-agent` + `fr connect --control`, control (keys, buttons, absolute pointer, wheel) with a per-lease out-of-process XTest executor, cursor forwarding, clipboard, host playback audio (view-only; client Opus decode in a restricted child), and viewer->host file sending. Proof = namespace e2e tests with real processes and planted negatives in crates/frd/tests/native_host_linux_serial/ (run: build fr/fr-media-worker/fr-input-agent/fr-opus-worker with `-p fr-native --features linux-desktop,linux-displays,linux-input,linux-clipboard,linux-audio`, `-p frd --bin frd`, then `FR_NS_SUDO=1 scripts/test_linux_serial_lifecycle.sh <native_host_linux_serial test binary>`). NOT yet: any live two-machine run, QUIC interop (workspace pins asupersync =0.5.0), more than one peer at a time (serial listener), hardware HEVC, non-X11 platforms.

RULES (AGENTS.md, binding): no file deletion without the owner's written permission; Asupersync is the only runtime; HEVC/Opus only; typed refusals, never silent fallback; every queue bounded in count AND bytes; clipboard/input/pixels/file names never in logs; evidence categories are separate and a namespace e2e is NOT live evidence; no weakened assertions, no fixtures presented as live proof; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and tests must pass; stage by explicit path; other agents push to main concurrently (verify, rebase, never force-push).

WHY: plan §6.1 binds to the node's current tailnet addresses (IPv4 AND IPv6). crates/frd/src/host_run.rs:593-599 binds IPv4 only; the ingress script supports ip6 but frd run never installs it; clients dialing the IPv6 tailnet address get nothing.

SCOPE: bind each current tailnet address with its own ingress rule (direct or helper); admission requires the exact /128 own address; fr connect dials what LocalAPI provides (IPv4 preferred, IPv6 fallback, typed failure); ip6 rule read-back validation.

ACCEPTANCE: namespace e2e with an IPv6 fixture address: view + control over IPv6; ip6 rule read back; planted negative: IPv4-only bind fails the IPv6 e2e; address-selection unit tests; docs.
notes:
REFINEMENT R1 (2026-09-27): Reuse the IPv6 TUN/nftables fixture that LINUX_NATIVE_INGRESS.md:201 already exercises with synthetic LocalAPI metadata.
2026-09-27 re-prioritised P1 -> P2: tailnets always assign an IPv4 (100.x) address and fr connect prefers IPv4, so IPv6-only reachability is a rare gap; the fix needs two concurrent listeners feeding the serial acceptor (frd run binds one LinuxServer), which is better done together with the multi-peer listener work (fr-rc-transport-multiclient-qda).

2026-10-26 retained concurrent dual-stack/fallback implementation bc682641 and tightened ingress setup: acquire bounded same-node successor snapshots against the still-valid first snapshot before any installation; report cleanup failure after attempting every known sibling rule. Added namespace regressions for same-IP identity change, partial cleanup failure, retained transports holding both protections, and unpolled/caught-panic teardown. All four are listed explicitly in the existing native_dual_stack CI step. Documented that capacity-one host handshakes limit automatic alternate-family recovery after an Initial was already selected. Reciprocal source review, pinned formatting, fixture syntax and documentation checks pass. Local Cargo first hit ENOSPC and its retry was killed in pinned Asupersync before application type checking; new runtime cases remain unexecuted. Preserve existing assignment and in-progress acceptance status.

2026-11-07 follow-up to the 3ad437d9 runs above: corrections, checks and a likely cause.

Corrections to the 4a9ebdd3 commit message (pushed, so it stays as written):
- "checked on ts1 against real windows with each title": when I committed, only 8 of the 23 FrankenRemote title literals in fr-native's C sources had been tried. All 23 have now been tried on ts1. Each title was mapped as a real window and searched for with the deployed VIEWER_TITLE. The 8 viewer titles match and the other 15 do not (shared clipboard, picker, progress, audio, approval and others).
- "a systematic gap of about 6%": the measured gap was 7-8%. On ts2 the host root sampled 1921/2304 before control and 1734/2304 after it (8.1%). In r4 the viewer sampled 1757/2304 against the host's 1921/2304 sampled before drive (7.1%).

Checked against product code:
- The sharing indicators sit at fixed positions: 480x148 at the top left (control), the bottom left at y=928 (clipboard) and the top right (microphone). sharing_indicator.c sets them, and they map only after control is granted. The watched point (960,880) is clear of all three, of xev (600x400+600+400) and of xclock.
- desktop.rs check_fitted_layout always uses fr-media's Fit::new. So the helpers' fit (floor division, centred) is what the client draws: 1920x1080 into 1872x912 gives (125,0,1621,912).

Likely cause of the r5/r6 Publication(Media(Worker(Deadline))). This is from reading the code; no trace was captured. The host's startup worker exchanges (CaptureSource::start, DiscoveredSource::start, check_display, configure) take ObservationControl::deadline(2 s). That deadline is capped at the admission/observation expiry sampled at issue (media.rs deadline/live_deadline), and Worker::exchange keeps it fixed. With frd run's 1 s grant validity and the 500 ms refresh margin (running.rs REFRESH_MARGIN_US), a startup exchange gets about 0.5-1 s, not 2 s. On ts2 at load 78-86, spawning a worker and getting its first reply can take longer. This is the startup half of fr-6zrg: 60ee6f09 made running Capture/Poll re-read authority, and startup deadlines stayed fixed. A host-side trace of a failing start would confirm or refute it. Until then, live runs on a loaded host can fail at start for this reason.

The design (plan-of-record 10.2): one UDP socket per tailnet address; packets routed by destination connection ID to a bounded slot table (3 peers + <= 2 half-open), pre-admission token buckets, typed refusal for excess Initials; each connection its own region; the controlled share becomes a role inside the shared hub (controller = an observer holding the lease) so observers can sit beside a controller and handoff is serialized in the authority owner.

SCOPE: a 1-day spike against the pinned asupersync: can one endpoint accept and drive two connections concurrently, or does it need upstream work (then tie to fr-rc-transport-adopt-pin-7bn — never a second QUIC stack)? Retain the result (commands, logs) in spikes/.

notes:
REFINEMENT R1 (2026-09-27): Retain the spike under spikes/quic-multipeer/ with the exact asupersync revision, commands, exit codes and logs (not only prose).
2026-09-27 SOURCE RESEARCH (read-only, asupersync-0.5.0 registry source, not yet run): VERDICT needs upstream work for cold admission. 0.5.0 has ManagedQuicEndpoint + ConnectionRouter that DO route authenticated connections by DCID on one socket (connection_manager.rs:40-44; NativeQuicUdpConnection::into_managed udp_connection.rs:301-307; begin_authenticated_accept managed_endpoint.rs:660-690), BUT the caller must already know the new peer's address and Initial DCID (:682-690), unknown Initials on the managed socket are dropped with only a trace (:1558-1563) and never exposed, only one pending admission (:701-706), bind()-created endpoints are refused (:696-700), and there is no public socket peek. A FrankenRemote-side DCID demux is blocked: QuicUdpEndpoint owns its socket with no injection API (endpoint.rs:194-201, pub(crate) polls :400/:550); finish_authenticated_handshake/insert_authenticated_connection are pub(crate); short-header assembly is pub(crate) - reimplementing it would be a second QUIC stack (forbidden). SMALLEST UPSTREAM ASK: (1) hand unrouted Initials (peer addr, DCID, datagram) to the caller from the managed loop; (2) let begin_authenticated_accept consume that datagram (also removes today's probe-timeout delay, fr-transport quic/accept.rs:8-13); (3) allow bind() endpoints / >=2 pending admissions. NEXT STEP: spikes/quic-multipeer on 0.5.0: accept A via native_accept, into_managed(max 3), admit B via begin_authenticated_accept with B's address + Initial DCID known from the harness (FR's own client chooses it, udp_connection.rs:379), drive both, retain logs.
close_reason: Spike answered (see comment 2026-10-13): PARTIAL. asupersync ee72b665e's ManagedQuicEndpoint routes several authenticated connections on one socket by DCID, but FrankenRemote needs upstream additions (public per-connection peer address, public per-connection close with app code and pending count, per-arrival TLS identity or a resolver-backed ServerConfig) and a managed host backend for QuicRecords before multi-viewer serving. comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
SPIKE ANSWER (2026-10-13, asupersync pin ee72b665e, read-only): PARTIAL.
- YES: ManagedQuicEndpoint serves several authenticated connections on one UDP socket, routed by DCID (connection_manager.rs:665-676) and pinned to the peer address once established (:690-694); asupersync's own H3 listener does this (src/web/router/h3_listener.rs). Accept: bind(ManagedEndpointConfig) + set_authenticated_accept_limit(n) + configure_authenticated_server(cx, ServerConfig, transport params, alpn) + run_event_loop_with_application; per-connection access is (cid, with_connection_mut) over the same QuicConnection type NativeQuicUdpConnection exposes (streams, datagrams, path_stats, ALPN, max_udp_payload_size all usable).
- MISSING upstream for FrankenRemote: (1) no public peer address per connection (frd host.rs authorize_membership needs it); (2) no public graceful per-connection close with app code (request_authenticated_close is pub(crate)+http3; begin_close via with_connection_mut never emits the packet; remove_connection is silent); (3) per-connection pending datagram count is pub(crate)+http3; (4) TLS identity comes from one fixed rustls ServerConfig, not FrankenRemote's per-arrival async identity driver (fr-tailnet exports no ServerConfig by design); (5) callback-only event loop, no bounded drive step; endpoint-wide idle timeout; capacity-full is a silent drop.
- No cheaper path inside asupersync today: QuicUdpEndpoint has no from_std/connect/reuseport/clone/inject; NativeQuicUdpConnection drops foreign-source datagrams silently (udp_connection.rs:1065); into_managed is one-way.
RECOMMENDATION:
(a) host_busy for a second client WITHOUT the multi-peer rework: opt-in asupersync patch answering a foreign-source Initial with an Initial-space CONNECTION_CLOSE(CONNECTION_REFUSED 0x02), rate-limited within the 3x amplification limit, and connect() surfacing the peer close code as a typed error; FrankenRemote maps it to host_busy (fr_cli/linux.rs:139). ~100-200 lines upstream + tests, a few dozen here. Advisory only (Initial keys are public; never authority).
(b) real multi-viewer: upstream asks (public peer_addr(cid), public per-connection close + pending count without http3, optionally a bounded drive step), then a managed host backend for QuicRecords (actor or poll state machine), a multi-accept Listener on configure_authenticated_server, a resolver-backed ServerConfig export in fr-tailnet, per-connection LocalAPI admission in host.rs, a concurrent accept loop replacing serial.rs, and N-peer Completion in desktop.rs Run. Dispatch (Warm route late joins, Busy on cold start) and the hub (default 3, MAX_SUBSCRIBERS 8) are already in place.

title: Multi-viewer freshness scheduling: Whittle-index service order + CoDel-style sojourn dropping per viewer
description:
BACKGROUND (reality check #2, 2026-09-27 at b6aca68 -> 79d6f46): FrankenRemote now works as a Linux-X11 remote desktop between two processes in an isolated network namespace: `frd run` (tailnet-bound listener, nftables ingress or the root `frd ingress-helper`, Tailscale-cert TLS, WhoIs own-user admission, XShm capture -> x265 -> Asupersync QUIC) serves `fr connect` (seccomp-sandboxed libavcodec decode, X11 presentation) for viewing and, with `frd run --input-agent` + `fr connect --control`, control (keys, buttons, absolute pointer, wheel) with a per-lease out-of-process XTest executor, cursor forwarding, clipboard, host playback audio (view-only; client Opus decode in a restricted child), and viewer->host file sending. Proof = namespace e2e tests with real processes and planted negatives in crates/frd/tests/native_host_linux_serial/ (run: build fr/fr-media-worker/fr-input-agent/fr-opus-worker with `-p fr-native --features linux-desktop,linux-displays,linux-input,linux-clipboard,linux-audio`, `-p frd --bin frd`, then `FR_NS_SUDO=1 scripts/test_linux_serial_lifecycle.sh <native_host_linux_serial test binary>`). NOT yet: any live two-machine run, QUIC interop (workspace pins asupersync =0.5.0), more than one peer at a time (serial listener), hardware HEVC, non-X11 platforms.

RULES (AGENTS.md, binding): no file deletion without the owner's written permission; Asupersync is the only runtime; HEVC/Opus only; typed refusals, never silent fallback; every queue bounded in count AND bytes; clipboard/input/pixels/file names never in logs; evidence categories are separate and a namespace e2e is NOT live evidence; no weakened assertions, no fixtures presented as live proof; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and tests must pass; stage by explicit path; other agents push to main concurrently (verify, rebase, never force-push).

WHY: once one encoder serves 1 controller + 2 viewers (fr-rc-transport-multiclient-qda), which viewer's backlog to serve next decides everyone's age of information. Whittle-index policies minimize weighted sum-AoI across flows with unreliable links (Kadota, Sinha, Uysal-Biyikoglu, Singh & Modiano 2018); CoDel (Nichols & Jacobson 2012) drops by time queued, which is what the freshness thesis cares about, complementing count/byte bounds.

SCOPE: a pure Whittle-index function of per-viewer age and delivery probability (from receiver feedback), controller weighted higher; per-viewer send queues drop obsolete work by sojourn time in addition to count/bytes; deterministic and replayable.

ACCEPTANCE: brute-force optimality check on small instances; lab scenario with one slow viewer shows the controller's AoI p95 unaffected while the slow viewer degrades independently (plan §7 "a slow read-only viewer is degraded or disconnected independently").

title: Operator/diagnostic strings tell the truth: frd run 'view-only' with --input-agent, help --approval local/--port HTTPS, fr doctor https/h3, frd status max_viewers
description:
BACKGROUND (reality check #2, 2026-09-27 at b6aca68 -> 79d6f46): FrankenRemote now works as a Linux-X11 remote desktop between two processes in an isolated network namespace: `frd run` (tailnet-bound listener, nftables ingress or the root `frd ingress-helper`, Tailscale-cert TLS, WhoIs own-user admission, XShm capture -> x265 -> Asupersync QUIC) serves `fr connect` (seccomp-sandboxed libavcodec decode, X11 presentation) for viewing and, with `frd run --input-agent` + `fr connect --control`, control (keys, buttons, absolute pointer, wheel) with a per-lease out-of-process XTest executor, cursor forwarding, clipboard, host playback audio (view-only; client Opus decode in a restricted child), and viewer->host file sending. Proof = namespace e2e tests with real processes and planted negatives in crates/frd/tests/native_host_linux_serial/ (run: build fr/fr-media-worker/fr-input-agent/fr-opus-worker with `-p fr-native --features linux-desktop,linux-displays,linux-input,linux-clipboard,linux-audio`, `-p frd --bin frd`, then `FR_NS_SUDO=1 scripts/test_linux_serial_lifecycle.sh <native_host_linux_serial test binary>`). NOT yet: any live two-machine run, QUIC interop (workspace pins asupersync =0.5.0), more than one peer at a time (serial listener), hardware HEVC, non-X11 platforms.

RULES (AGENTS.md, binding): no file deletion without the owner's written permission; Asupersync is the only runtime; HEVC/Opus only; typed refusals, never silent fallback; every queue bounded in count AND bytes; clipboard/input/pixels/file names never in logs; evidence categories are separate and a namespace e2e is NOT live evidence; no weakened assertions, no fixtures presented as live proof; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and tests must pass; stage by explicit path; other agents push to main concurrently (verify, rebase, never force-push).

WHY (AGENTS §7): overclaims found 2026-09-27: (1) crates/frd/src/bin/frd.rs:324 prints "sharing this desktop (view-only)" even with --input-agent — a security-relevant understatement; (2) frd HELP (frd.rs:50) advertises `--approval local (prompt)` which `frd run` refuses (`local_approval_unavailable`); (3) frd HELP (frd.rs:48) says --port covers "QUIC and HTTPS" (no HTTPS listener); (4) `fr doctor` prints `honest_endpoints.https` and ALPN `h3` (crates/fr-native/src/bin/fr_cli/linux/doctor.rs:62-72, output.rs:447,495) — no HTTPS/H3 listener exists; (5) `frd status` hard-codes `max_viewers: 3` and `variant: "standalone"` while `frd run` serves one peer at a time; (6) `frd status` mixes "not tested" and "not_tested".

SCOPE: each string/field reflects what runs: frd run says "controllable (remote control enabled by --input-agent)" vs "view-only"; help says `--approval local` is refused by `frd run` until a prompt exists; --port names QUIC only; fr doctor lists https/h3 as not_available (`no_browser_listener`); frd status reports a computed `max_concurrent_peers: 1` and a truthful variant; one spelling `not_tested` (check JSON consumers).

ACCEPTANCE: CLI/unit tests asserting each corrected string/field (extend frd_status_test / fr_cli; no unreviewed golden regeneration); planted negative: reverting one string fails its test; docs updated.
notes: REFINEMENT R1 (2026-09-27): fr doctor/frd status JSON has tests (e.g. fr-native doctor_matrix_test, frd_status_test): update the assertions explicitly and review each changed field; never regenerate goldens wholesale.

title: OWNER DECISION: a stale-view lapse under a held control lease - terminal (fr-core today) or suspend-and-resume (plan 11.3 wording)?
description: WHY: plan 11.3 (line 564) says sustained unknown/stale presentation SUSPENDS input, and plan 24 (line 1080) asks for 'time spent with input suspended by stale view' - both imply resumption within the lease lifetime; fr-core SessionAuthority::mark_view_stale's own doc says 'Recovery requires a new ticket even if the lease identity and observation remain live'. But SessionAuthority::mark_view_ready_until refuses to restore readiness while a lease is held ('a readiness lapse cannot revive an existing native owner ... revoke/cleanup must precede a grant'), and lease renewal requires Ready, so ANY view lapse under control ends the lease within its 3 s lifetime. MEASURED 2026-09-27 (namespace e2e, real frd run controlled session, load ~180-220): one picture confirmed visible 60 ms or 120 ms after submission, then a static desktop -> control ended 4/4 and 3/3 runs even with the fr-media late-picture fix (the re-qualifying observation reaches the host after its ~250 ms view deadline); the same screen change confirmed on time kept control. This is the mechanism behind the intermittent control deaths under load. OPTIONS: (a) keep terminal (document: any view lapse ends control; clients must reacquire); (b) suspend-and-resume: on a lapse fence input (tickets already invalidated), let the input agent release remotely held keys/buttons and report completion, and allow mark_view_ready_until to restore readiness under the SAME lease only after that cleanup and only before the lease's authorized_until; new tickets required; count suspended time. (b) matches the plan wording; it changes a deliberate fr-core invariant, hence the owner's call. ACCEPTANCE: the decision recorded here; fr-rc2-static-view-represent-0ruq then implements it with the parked e2e (hook fault.rs + real_late_picture.rs in the session worktree) as its proof.
notes:
2026-09-28 NEW EVIDENCE raising the stakes (7832436, namespace tc netem, real frd run controlled session, load ~100-200): control ends at 60 ms RTT (5 of 6 runs), at 100 ms RTT (always, 0/8 steps) and with 1% loss at 40 ms RTT (always); only <=40 ms RTT on a clean link is reliable. Probable mechanism: the fixed 250 ms source-age bound (presented::MAX_SOURCE_AGE_US) must cover the client's conservative clock uncertainty (the full exchange interval, ~1 RTT) + one-way transit + encode/decode/present + the report's return, and a lapse is terminal for the lease; loss that forces a recovery generation may also invalidate input credentials. So even with suspend-and-resume, a sustained >=100 ms RTT path would keep input suspended: the decision also needs a policy for the source-age bound under RTT (e.g. an RTT-scaled bound with an explicit cap, or measuring age with the one-way estimate the plan forbids) - plan 11.3/12.3 territory. Ordinary cross-continent/DERP tailnet paths exceed 60 ms RTT.
2026-09-28 MECHANISM ISOLATED (diagnostic build printing the typed chain; not committed): control ends at 60 ms RTT / 1% loss / 100 ms RTT via (a) the stale view (source age > 250 ms: Control(View(..SourceStale)) or the transport's view gate), (b) Transport(Expired): a reliable client SessionControl record (presented report / control response) not ACKed before its send-by, so QuicRecords closes the connection; view-only at 200 ms RTT via (c) Session(Expired): no observation challenge within the 3 s client silence bound. EXPERIMENT (not committed): source-age bound 250 ms -> 1 s on both ends (fr_client Policy::view_age_us, fr_wire presented::MAX_SOURCE_AGE_US): 60 ms RTT held 8/8 in 3/3 runs (vs dying 5/6 at 250 ms); 100 ms RTT still failed (1/8 or fr did not exit in the harness limit); 1% loss still ended (host revocation once). So the decision has two parts: (1) the source-age bound (fixed 250 ms is the binding limit near 60 ms RTT; an RTT-aware bound with a cap, or a larger fixed bound) and (2) the transport record deadlines for superseding records (a late presented report kills the whole connection). fr now reports view_stale / transport_deadline_expired / host_not_heard (see PRESENTATION_FRESHNESS.md).
2026-09-28 faae064 removed one transport cause (critical records starving behind queued media under loss; view-only now holds 5% loss at 40 ms RTT in 3/3 runs). What remains for control is squarely this decision: the client's presented-report send-by is now + (250 ms - the sample's conservative age), so at >=60 ms RTT or with any retransmission the record misses it and QuicRecords closes the connection (transport_deadline_expired), or the view ages out first (view_stale). Options to decide: an RTT-aware/larger source-age bound (the 1 s experiment held 60 ms RTT 3/3), and/or not closing the connection when a superseding presented report misses its deadline (drop it and send the next) - the latter is a protocol/transport policy change (a reliable record cannot be withdrawn once written; it would need an unreliable or replace-in-place carrier).

title: Host re-presents on a lost view (bounded forced capture) and the viewer suspends, not ends, control; typed view_stale
description:
BACKGROUND (reality check #2, 2026-09-27 at b6aca68 -> 79d6f46): FrankenRemote now works as a Linux-X11 remote desktop between two processes in an isolated network namespace: `frd run` (tailnet-bound listener, nftables ingress or the root `frd ingress-helper`, Tailscale-cert TLS, WhoIs own-user admission, XShm capture -> x265 -> Asupersync QUIC) serves `fr connect` (seccomp-sandboxed libavcodec decode, X11 presentation) for viewing and, with `frd run --input-agent` + `fr connect --control`, control (keys, buttons, absolute pointer, wheel) with a per-lease out-of-process XTest executor, cursor forwarding, clipboard, host playback audio (view-only; client Opus decode in a restricted child), and viewer->host file sending. Proof = namespace e2e tests with real processes and planted negatives in crates/frd/tests/native_host_linux_serial/ (run: build fr/fr-media-worker/fr-input-agent/fr-opus-worker with `-p fr-native --features linux-desktop,linux-displays,linux-input,linux-clipboard,linux-audio`, `-p frd --bin frd`, then `FR_NS_SUDO=1 scripts/test_linux_serial_lifecycle.sh <native_host_linux_serial test binary>`). NOT yet: any live two-machine run, QUIC interop (workspace pins asupersync =0.5.0), more than one peer at a time (serial listener), hardware HEVC, non-X11 platforms.

RULES (AGENTS.md, binding): no file deletion without the owner's written permission; Asupersync is the only runtime; HEVC/Opus only; typed refusals, never silent fallback; every queue bounded in count AND bytes; clipboard/input/pixels/file names never in logs; evidence categories are separate and a namespace e2e is NOT live evidence; no weakened assertions, no fixtures presented as live proof; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and tests must pass; stage by explicit path; other agents push to main concurrently (verify, rebase, never force-push).

WHY (defect, intermittent loss of control): crates/fr-client/src/freshness.rs:395-400 — a picture that misses its 50 ms display budget becomes QueueExpired and clears `visible`. On a static desktop no newer picture arrives (idle means idle), source age passes 250 ms, and ViewStale terminally ends control (crates/fr-client/src/input/presentation.rs:392-399; the controlled session closes). The host ignores negative presented reports (crates/frd/src/media/presented.rs has no refresh path). The 2026-09-26 reliability investigation fixed IDR fragment pacing (eb8f450, bd177a8) but measured x265 encode up to 169 ms and decode 30-48 ms under heavy load; ~2.5 s startup deaths remain unexplained — consistent with this mechanism. Clients see a generic `native_session_failed` instead of a typed reason.

DESIGN (plan §11.3, §12.3; AGENTS §5 never label old frames fresh): (a) Host: a negative PresentedState / view-lost report from the controller triggers ONE forced verified capture (existing `force` flag) encoded as an IDR on the reliable recovery stream with a fresh capture timestamp; rate-limited (<= 1 per 250 ms, <= 4 per stale episode, bounded); never resends or relabels old pixels. (b) Viewer: control is SUSPENDED (actions refused typed `view_stale_suspended`, never queued) while a re-present is in flight within a bounded window (<= 500 ms); input resumes only after a newly presented picture whose source age is within budget; otherwise control ends with typed `view_stale` (completion record + exit code), not `native_session_failed`. (c) No lease/renewal/freshness deadline is lengthened. Rejected: raising the 50 ms budget; keeping `visible` on expiry; periodic dummy refresh on idle screens.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) unit tests for host rate limits/episode bound, viewer suspend window, typed codes. (2) namespace e2e: static host desktop under control; induce one late picture (test-only encoder-stall hook in the capture worker, or a netem delay burst) -> control survives; host reports exactly one forced capture; input during the window is refused typed, input after recovery lands (observed on the host). (3) PLANTED NEGATIVE: host trigger disabled -> control ends with typed `view_stale` (assert the code). (4) stress: real_control 20x under parallel load (>= 16 concurrent heavy jobs): zero spontaneous control deaths; report before/after counts. (5) gates green.

TESTS & LOGGING: content-free events presented_negative / represent_scheduled / represent_presented / view_stale_suspended with generation ids and durations.
notes:
REFINEMENT R1 (2026-09-27): Also applies to view-only sessions: after a negative presented report the viewer's freshness indicator returns to fresh through the same bounded re-present (assert it). The stall/late-picture injection hook must be test-only (cfg(test) or a test feature never enabled in shipped binaries). Reproduce the defect first (ideally with fr-rc2-namespace-impairment-rows-n29k), then fix; record before/after.
DESIGN CORRECTION 2026-09-27 (from reading the code): the death path is not ViewStale on the client. A picture confirmed visible after its 50 ms display budget returns QueueExpired and the ViewTracker DROPPED it (visible=None); evidence() then stays NotSubmitted forever on a static desktop (no newer pixels), the viewer sends no positive presented report, the host's view_until (source deadline) lapses and mark_view_stale runs; fr-core authority then REFUSES mark_view_ready_until while a lease exists ('a readiness lapse cannot revive an existing native owner') and the lease dies within its 3 s lifetime. So a host-side re-present after a negative report (this bead's original design (a)/(b)) cannot save the lease without weakening that authority invariant; rejected. Chosen fix (fr-media freshness): keep a late picture as an UNQUALIFIED visible picture; evidence() reports NotSubmitted (input gated, no report either way) until a strictly newer host observation of that exact picture (QualifiedUnchanged from idle verification) qualifies it, bounded by the source-age limit (then SourceStale). Observations known at visibility are Obsolete and cannot qualify it; pixel age keeps the old capture time. Typed view_stale reporting and a host forced re-present remain possible follow-ups but are not needed for the static-desktop case.
2026-09-27 PROGRESS: the fr-media ViewTracker now keeps a late (QueueExpired) picture as an unqualified visible picture until a strictly newer host observation of it qualifies it, bounded by the source-age limit (unit tests + planted negative; committed with the negative e2e evidence recorded in PRESENTATION_FRESHNESS.md). NOT SUFFICIENT: the namespace e2e (test-only client hook confirming one picture 60/120 ms late, then a static desktop) still ends control 4/4 and 3/3 at load ~200, because fr-core refuses to restore readiness under a held lease once the host's view deadline lapses. Blocked on fr-rc2-owner-decision-view-lapse-f7ts. The hook (crates/fr-native/src/bin/fr_cli/linux/fault.rs, feature e2e-late-visibility) and e2e (crates/frd/tests/native_host_linux_serial/real_late_picture.rs, harness env plumbing in real_control.rs) are parked uncommitted in the session worktree and must be re-added with the implementation.
2026-09-28: under tc netem (60 ms RTT, or 1% loss) control ends and the client reports only the generic native_session_failed - the typed view_stale reason in this bead's scope is still missing; see PRESENTATION_FRESHNESS.md 'Measured limit under real network impairment'.
2026-09-28 PROGRESS (typed view_stale, part of this bead's scope): fr now names a stale-view end `view_stale` (frd native_connection::reconnect::lapse -> Lapse::ViewStale for Control(View(Media(SourceStale|SourceUnknown))) and the input client's own Control(View(Input(Stopped(ViewStale))))). The controlled viewer's transport gate used to close the connection with a bare Transport(Unauthorized) when it met the stale view first; it now records the view refusal and reports Error::View (viewer/controlled.rs gate()/gated(); only this viewer's own gate refusal is relabelled - the transport evaluates its identity gate first). Unit tests: reconnect::tests::only_transport_deadlines_and_stale_views_are_named_lapses, controlled::tests::a_stale_view_met_by_the_transport_gate_keeps_its_typed_reason; namespace e2e real_impairment asserts no generic end. STILL OPEN here: the re-present/suspend semantics themselves (owner decision f7ts).

title: Native dial reports NativeHandshake, not PeerCertificateRejected, for a wrong certificate name (CI dual-stack dial lane red since at least 2026-11-02)

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
2026-11-05 cause found and fixed upstream. The fix is a scratch asupersync commit that has not landed.
Reproduced on trj. AppArmor blocks unprivileged user namespaces there and on ts1, so the run used sudo unshare --net, with the test binary run as the user. CI's lane passes 7/8; the wrong-certificate test fails with Some(NativeHandshake).

Cause: asupersync's QuicHandshakeDriver::read_handshake discards rustls's error. - Server-side refusals and all other alerts keep read_hs_fatal_alert. The TLS alert is still raised, so the CRYPTO_ERROR close a peer sees is unchanged.
- Two asupersync integration tests that pinned the old code for a client-side certificate refusal were updated: atp_native_auth server-name and atp_cli_quic_loopback CA-as-leaf.
Evidence (trj):
- asupersync handshake_driver tests 45/45, with a new wrong-name case. atp_native_auth 8/8. The three atp_cli_quic_loopback certificate tests pass.
- Planted negative: with the old read_handshake body put back, both certificate unit tests fail (left read_hs_fatal_alert, right ServerCertificateRejected).
- FR's fr-tailnet native_dial lane built against the patched asupersync passes 8/8 in 2 runs.
FR needs no change: handshake_error already maps ServerCertificateRejected.
Not independent: the same agent wrote and ran all of this. The lane ran under sudo-created namespaces, not CI's unprivileged ones.

title: Controlled viewer ends the session with host_record_unexpected on a ClockReply behind a blocked record
description:
ControlledViewer::step receives twice. The first pass offers records to the clock and blocks everything else, so it stops at a blocked record on an ordered stream. The second is the session's dispatcher, which hands what it does not own to the embedder. After the handoff the session holds no clock, so a ClockReply behind a blocked record on the SessionControl stream goes to the streaming turn's unclaimed path and the session ends with host_record_unexpected: a false protocol fault.

Seen in the namespace lossy matrix on 6 rows in 40 logs: 2 of 18 logs on pinned builds, 4 of 22 on patched builds, so it does not depend on the asupersync branch. 5 were at RTT 6 ms / 5% loss, 1 at RTT 0 / no loss. A scratch diagnostic client caught one: kind 0x0085 on stream 3. What preceded the reply in that run was not captured.

title: Controller window close is not orderly: fr never runs the finished control close exchange (fence cancels the session Cx its destination lease and terminal gate depend on)
description:
`fr connect --control` never runs the controller's orderly close. When the controller closes its window, the connection is dropped. The host then sees Desktop(Publication(Session(Renewal(Transport(Expired))))) instead of a CloseRequest; it counts the viewer as failed, and the controller gets no close report (no close_exchange in its completion). A view-only viewer's window close does run its exchange: Session(Renewal(PeerClosed)), host_report.reason client_requested.

The library part is finished: NativeObserver::serve_interactive_control_until / StreamingViewer::serve_control_until, CONTROLLER_DISCONNECT.md, and frd tests that bootstrap the observer directly. fr-native's Desktop and reconnect::Session still call serve_interactive_control.

Wiring it in exposed the real blocker (tried 2026-10-14; patch kept in the session scratchpad as controller_orderly_close_wiring.patch, not landed). A window close became Break(Requested) and the exchange ran on an independent cleanup Cx. It ended at once with ControlCloseOutcome { request_acknowledged: false, report: None, transport: Err(Unauthorized) }. Why:
1. ControlledViewer::fence_input -> ViewerControl::stop cancels the viewer's Cx. On the client, that Cx is also the session Cx that native_connection::run_checked binds to the destination lease: TargetOwner/TargetLease built by into_owned_connection(cx), whose check() runs cx.checkpoint().
2. join_viewer installs that lease check as BOTH lifetime gates (Viewer::retain_connection_check -> retain_lifetime_check(check, check)). So the terminal gate fails as soon as the application is fenced. fr-transport's contract (retain_lifetime_checks) says the terminal gate may omit only the fenced application's cancellation and must be checked on an independent clock. The host does this (host.rs retain_connection_checks with a separate terminal check on the credential clock); the client does not.
3. Even with a correct terminal gate, Scoped (run_checked) and run_application stop the attempt as soon as the session Cx is cancelled, which would drop a pending exchange.

Wanted: on the client, an application Cx (the one the fence cancels) separate from the connection Cx that owns the destination lease, Scoped and renewal. Add a terminal destination check (for example TargetLease::check_terminal(clock)) that keeps every stop except the application's own cancellation and runs on an independent clock. Then wire serve_interactive_control_until into fr (the saved patch) and print close_exchange in the control completion.

Also landed with this bead: serve_interactive_control_until now sends the same negotiated request as serve_interactive_control (wanted capabilities met with what negotiation allows), as that function's own doc comment already said.

Evidence: namespace e2e real_observation_indicator::a_controller_is_admitted_and_granted_control_only_by_attributed_consent with a scratch fr that logs the close path ("close requested seen", then the outcome above), and host-side FRDIAG in dispatch::controlled_outcome on real_control::fr_connect_control_drives_the_host_desktop_through_frd_run.
acceptance_criteria: Closing a controller's window: the host sees the CloseRequest (no transport expiry), and fr's control completion carries close_exchange with host_report.reason client_requested. The terminal destination gate still refuses a revoked, expired or changed identity (unit tests). Namespace e2e for control pass, with a planted negative: removing the orderly path brings back the expiry end.
close_reason: Fixed in d37bcc1. The client's Viewer has its own application context; the connection context keeps the destination lease, renewal and scope, so the input fence no longer cancels the gate the closing exchange needs. fr serves controllers through serve_interactive_control_until on a fresh cleanup context, and the control completion reports close_exchange plus a content-free lease_report. The host answers with LeaseRevoked (session_ended, cleanup fenced); the exchange accepts either that or a session Closed, so the acceptance's 'host_report client_requested' reads lease_report here. Namespace evidence: 9 of 10 closes acknowledged; the tenth met native send backlog (Backpressure), reported truthfully. Planted negative (no cleanup runtime) fails. Full suite 77/77.

restart the original host clock", still holds whenever the sleep exceeds the remaining time.

title: A stale view suspends control input instead of ending it (plan 11.3), bounded, with release of held input
description:
The remaining half of fr-rc2-owner-decision-view-lapse-f7ts. Plan 11.3: 'Sustained unknown/stale presentation suspends input before another action can be applied to an untrustworthy view'. Plan 21 also asks to measure 'time spent with input suspended by stale view'.

Today a lapse is TERMINAL on both ends.
- Client: fr-client InputClient::tick/presented call fail(StopReason::ViewStale), and PresentedInput stops, so the controlled viewer ends with view_stale.
- Host, first path: InputMonitor::deadline (fr-core input_submission.rs:228, control.rs:51) folds view_until into control_deadline and REVOKES on any lapse. The watchdog then finishes with AuthorityEnded, the lease ends and the client gets session_ended.
- Host, second path: SessionAuthority::mark_view_ready_until refuses new readiness after a lapse under a held lease ('revoke/cleanup must precede a grant').

Namespace diagnostics on 2026-09-30 show this terminal lapse is the main limit on control under loss. It happens even at 6 ms RTT with 1% loss: one lost packet delays the source observation past the bound (Input(Stopped(ViewStale))). At 120 ms RTT, the first large picture needs several RTTs while cwnd grows, arrives unqualified, and the old view deadline lapses first.

DESIGN:

(1) fr-core: separate the lease deadline (terminal) from the view deadline (suspending).
- InputMonitor::deadline returns Suspended while the lease is live but the view is stale or unready. It revokes only on lease or observation expiry.
- A lapse invalidates all tickets (as mark_view_stale already does) and sets a suspension state. Only a confirmation from the native owner clears that state, after held keys and buttons are released.
- mark_view_ready_until accepts new readiness under a held lease only once that release is confirmed. Otherwise it keeps refusing, so a key held across a frozen view can never autorepeat while unseen.
- New readiness never extends the lease. Input resumes only with a NEW ticket (the existing renewal path issues one once readiness returns).

(2) frd watchdog / input agent loop: on Suspended, fence submission and send release-only cleanup for remotely held keys/buttons to the executor. The in-process sink and fr-input-agent must both support release-without-stop. Then confirm, then keep the lease: renewals continue.

(3) Bound: a suspension longer than a fixed limit (proposal 10 s, recorded as a starting point) ends control with the typed view_stale reason. Local revoke still wins immediately.

(4) Client: InputClient enters Suspended instead of Stopped(ViewStale).
- Actions are refused with a typed ViewSuspended error: not queued, not replayed. Committed effects stay reported.
- It resumes only with fresh presented evidence AND a newly accepted ticket.
- The UI must show that input is suspended.
- fr's completion reports suspension count and total duration.

(5) Tests.
- fr-core property tests: no submission while suspended; no readiness revival before release confirmation; lease expiry is still terminal during suspension; old tickets never revive.
- Client suspend/resume unit tests.
- frd watchdog tests: release happens without a new input event.
- Namespace e2e: freeze capture (as a_stale_view_suspends_input does), check that no input reaches the host and held keys are released, resume, and check that input reaches the host again with the SAME lease. The existing impairment rows should then hold where they ended view_stale.
- Planted negatives: revive without release; resume with an old ticket.

STOP CONDITIONS (AGENTS 13): never let an input path execute without its submission-time expiry check, and never replay uncertain actions.
acceptance_criteria: A stale or unknown view suspends control input; the lease survives and ends only on lease, observation or suspension-limit expiry. Held remote keys and buttons are released on every lapse, without a new input event, before readiness can return. Input resumes only after fresh presented evidence and a newly issued ticket. No action is queued or replayed across a suspension. Suspension count and duration are reported. Unit and property tests, e2e with planted negatives, namespace matrix rerun, docs (PRESENTATION_READINESS, PRESENTATION_FRESHNESS, PROTOCOL if the wire changes).
close_reason:
Acceptance met on the asupersync pin, at HEAD 537e5a8.
Implementation:
- 70a53a8 and 20a77c1: ControlStatus::Suspended and MAX_VIEW_SUSPENSION in fr-core authority.rs; submission refusal; client suspend/resume; held input released before readiness returns.
- fr reports input_suspensions / input_suspended_ms.
- Docs: PRESENTATION_READINESS.md.
Evidence:
- Namespace e2e real_control::a_stale_view_suspends_input_before_it_reaches_the_host passes 2/2 on ts2 (FR_NS_SUDO=1, tailnet-path emulation, load ~16): input_suspensions 1, outcome stopped. It checks a single release on the host, no marker input landing, and resume on the same lease.

title: Optional opt-in software encoder profile: x265/oxideav-h265 evaluation behind the contracts
description:
WHY: The plan keeps a software encoder as a rescue/unsupported-hardware option — opt-in, visibly CPU-limited, negotiating lower geometry/frame-rate instead of silently consuming all cores — and names oxideav-h265 as a legitimate pure-Rust candidate to EVALUATE (its README claims an I/P/B encoder at 8-bit 4:2:0 with dimensions divisible by 16; claims are things to verify, not evidence). This bead preserves that feature without letting it touch the critical path.

SCOPE: (1) Define the opt-in software profile behind the fr-media contracts: explicit selection only (hardware-required deployments fail typed instead), enforced geometry/frame-rate ceilings, visible CPU-cost reporting in diagnostics. (2) Evaluate candidates at a pinned revision each: x265 (GPL/commercial licensing and patent considerations recorded — placing it in a plugin/process does NOT automatically settle redistribution; the shipped combination needs a recorded distribution decision) and oxideav-h265 (independent decoder interoperability, supported bitstream subset, adversarial-input behavior, throughput/memory/quality at matched bitrate, browser-target build sanity). (3) Write the adopt/defer/reject decision note with measurements.

CONSTRAINTS: no second runtime or large multimedia stack smuggled in; no uncapped optimization project; the replaceable media interface is the boundary; DECISION from the plan stands — no HEVC encoder written from scratch.

ACCEPTANCE: the evaluation report with retained runs and the licensing/distribution analysis; if adopted, the profile ships with its own capability row and CPU-envelope disclosure; if not, the negative evidence is recorded and the profile stays absent. Provenance: plan sections 8.1, 9.3, 9.4, 25.

title: Abrupt local close is silent to the peer: send CONNECTION_CLOSE with a typed app code on deadline/authority expiry
description: WHAT: when QuicRecords closes a connection on a local failure (a reliable record missing its send-by -> Error::Expired, an authority gate refusal -> Unauthorized), it only drops the native connection (quic.rs close(): native = None). No QUIC CONNECTION_CLOSE reaches the peer, so the peer learns only by silence: a view-only fr waits for its 3 s SILENCE_US and reports host_not_heard; the host side of a dead client waits for its own renewal deadlines. EVIDENCE (2026-09-28 namespace tc netem, diagnostic build): host viewer ended Session(Renewal(Transport(Expired))) while the client reported host_not_heard ~3 s later (PRESENTATION_FRESHNESS.md). WHY IT MATTERS: plan values typed refusals over silent degradation; 3 s of a frozen view before a generic-looking end is poor UX and hides the host's reason. SCOPE: on these local terminal failures, best-effort emit an application CONNECTION_CLOSE with a small closed set of FrankenRemote app error codes (deadline_expired, authority_revoked, ...) - asupersync 0.5.0 NativeQuicConnection::close_immediately(cx, app_error_code) changes state but a close packet must also be flushed; the flush must not violate QuicRecords' custody rules (a returned failed I/O turn transfers custody only into close; the terminal drain proof). The receiving side maps a peer close with a known code to a named end (e.g. host_transport_deadline) via frd reconnect::lapse / fr lapse.rs. ACCEPTANCE: unit test on a native pair: sender-deadline expiry on one side -> the other side's next drive reports the typed peer close within one RTT (not after its silence bound); namespace e2e: the view-only 200 ms RTT row ends with the host's named reason, not host_not_heard; planted negative: without the close emission the test fails. No new retry, no change to deadlines.
notes:
2026-09-28 source check (asupersync 0.5.0 registry source): the native connection never EMITS a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame - NativeQuicConnection::begin_close only enters draining (start_draining_with_code) and close_immediately only changes the state machine; the only ConnectionClose code outside tests is the receive path (connection.rs ~2380). So FrankenRemote cannot tell the peer about a local abrupt close without upstream support. An application-level Closed record after a transport failure would violate QuicRecords' custody rule (a failed I/O turn transfers custody only into close) and would likely be stuck behind the same deadline. BLOCKED UPSTREAM: ask asupersync to send CONNECTION_CLOSE (with the application error code) on begin_close/close_immediately and flush it best-effort. Until then the client learns only via its 3 s silence bound (host_not_heard).

Implemented source slice: arm deferred Closed for admitted control-capable viewers before any grant; transfer the original terminal slot to lease Revoked at GrantQueued before native I/O; confirm exact original custody at steady-state handoff; accept a canonical original-session-bound revocation before grant delivery solely as terminal metadata, never input authority. Added transport custody, startup/cancellation, actual grant-queue boundary, managed cleanup and public pending-viewer no-revival regressions. Independent cross-review fixed the pending-client unseen-lease case and a two-record/one-slot test fixture. All 12 canonical lease-revocation codec tests executed with exact pinned rustc and passed; full frd/TLS application regressions remain unexecuted under the shared storage/memory build blocker. Retain in_progress until full application verification; no claim of live-tailnet or hardware qualification.
2026-11-08 source implementation: the native client now registers a one-use abort consumer on its exact authenticated socket before application traffic. Abrupt closure fences the original viewer and permits only a protected native CONNECTION_CLOSE while the original independent connection supervisor still renews its destination lease; immutable security proof and one closure-time 250 ms budget remain mandatory. Explicit CloseRequest exchanges keep first custody. No queued application bytes, cleanup receipts, effect claims or content are emitted. Added 13 actual-localhost-TLS/UDP transport regressions and two native connector supervision regressions. Pinned rustfmt and docs gate pass. Full check/test attempts, including single-job metadata-only fr-transport check, are blocked by SIGKILL compiling the unchanged pinned Asupersync dependency in the shared 8 GiB runner; new tests are not claimed executed. Static UBS findings were reviewed as test assertion/panic inventories, not a clean scan. Remaining: capable-runner test results, live two-machine failure propagation, and early native UI/setup callback errors (identified in review, follow-up in progress). Shared application/connection cancellation and dropped outer futures cannot perform asynchronous notification; generic failure also covers abandoned native I/O. Keep bead open for live acceptance.

That gives one path for both fr-t4lj and izv6's host-failure report, without the Closed-record drain that terminal_sender() refuses while streams hold unacked data: (1) fr-transport: a closed set of FrankenRemote application close codes and a best-effort QuicRecords::close_with(cx, code) (bounded single flush, then drop; custody unchanged); (2) frd: call it on local terminal failures (sender deadline -> deadline_expired, authority refusal -> authority_revoked, source preparation failure -> host_failure); (3) client: surface a peer CONNECTION_CLOSE with a known code as a typed transport error (today QuicRecords has no PeerClosed variant; a peer close looks like a generic Native/Closed failure) and map it to named ends (host_failure, host_transport_deadline, ...). title: frd log reports a clean admitted session as refused 1 / failed 1 (serial and hub counters)
description:
frd's JSON log reports a clean, admitted session as a refusal and a failure.

Evidence: live 2026-10-14, ts1 `frd run --audio --once`, with trj as a view-only audio client for 58 s. The viewer closed its window, and the client completed `outcome: stopped` with `host_report.reason: client_requested`. The host logged:

  {"admitted":0,"attempts":1,"event":"peer_finished","outcome":"Err(Cancelled)","refused":1}
  {"event":"share_ended","outcome":"Desktop(Ok(Report { source_renewals: 58, viewers: Statistics { admitted: 1, finished: 1, failed: 1 } }))"}

Earlier live control runs show the same shape: peer_finished admitted 0 / refused 1 or 2, and share_ended with finished 0, failed 1. So does every namespace e2e row that prints the host peer outcome, for example the c70a82b suite: `{ attempts: 1, admitted: 0, refused: 1, outcome: "Err(Cancelled)" }`.

Why:
1. native_connection/host/serial.rs counts `stats.refused += 1` whenever the peer's outcome is Err. A desktop peer is handed to the hub by Application::serve and almost always ends as Err(Cancelled), because the share's teardown cancels the listener's Scoped operation before the peer future resolves. "refused" therefore means "the peer future did not return Ok", not "the peer was refused admission". The serial tests pin this rule: native_host_serial.rs, native_host_serial/live_policy.rs, and native_host_linux_serial.rs policy_handover expect admitted 1 / refused 1 when a peer was served and a policy change then ended it.
2. session_startup/running/shared/hub.rs Turn::finish counts `failed += 1` for any Err result. A client-requested close reaches the hub as an Err (the close intent, e.g. PeerClosed), so a normal close counts as failed.

Wanted: counters an operator can read literally. Proposed rule: admitted means the peer reached Application::serve (it passed native TLS, WhoIs admission and Host creation); refused means it never did. A viewer that ended by its own or the host's orderly close is not "failed". The outcome string keeps the exact end. Changing the serial rule means updating those test expectations on purpose, with the reason in the commit.
acceptance_criteria: A live or namespace session that a viewer closes cleanly logs admitted >= 1, refused 0, and failed 0. A peer refused at admission still counts as refused. Each changed test expectation states the new rule.
close_reason: Fixed in this push: serial admitted = reached the application; hub/dispatch count a viewer's own close (Renewal(PeerClosed)) as finished, not failed. real_media e2e asserts PeerFinished admitted 1 refused 0 and ShareEnded finished 1 failed 0; refused-at-admission paths still count refused (ScopeDenied, idle timeouts unchanged in native_host_serial 15/15). Changed expectations carry their rule in comments.
