title: fr-native display_inventory test process aborted once with glibc heap corruption
description: 2026-10-14, ts1 full workspace run (cargo test --workspace --all-features, line-tables-only): the display_inventory test binary died with SIGABRT, glibc 'corrupted size vs. prev_size while consolidating', while out_of_scope_handles_and_network_or_malformed_display_selectors_refuse ran in parallel with the other 11 tests (each starts its own Xvfb and opens Xlib connections; X11Inventory calls XInitThreads first). Not reproduced: 8 sequential + 40 and 60 parallel-instance runs of the same binaries (including the exact crashing build e268aed362103321), and 24 parallel runs of an AddressSanitizer build (RUSTFLAGS=-Zsanitizer=address, CFLAGS=-fsanitize=address; Rust and the C bridge instrumented, libX11/libxcb not). Suspects: a race inside uninstrumented libX11/xcb with concurrent XOpenDisplay on many displays, or memory corruption in a path the ASan runs did not hit. Next: run under valgrind (helgrind/memcheck) or with a libX11 built with ASan; MALLOC_CHECK_=3 with core dumps enabled on ts1 for the next occurrence. Production impact unknown: frd/fr open few displays per process.
close_reason: Test-only Xext cache race: Screen helper serializes in-process X11 use (56090fa); helgrind shows no Xext races

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 2026-10-14 diagnosis (valgrind on ts1, display_inventory test binary at c70a82b, 12 tests in parallel). memcheck: 13,548 errors from 19 contexts, ALL inside libx265 SIMD (estIntraPredChromaQT reading 0 bytes past posix_memalign'd Yuv blocks, plus uninitialised values in x265 asm): the usual x265/valgrind false positives, none in Rust or the C bridge. helgrind: besides std/parking_lot noise, real races in libXext's process-global extension cache. XextFindDisplay's UNLOCKED last-display fast path (extinfo->cur) races with XextCreateExtension/XextAddDisplay and display close on other threads; for example, the test helper support::Screen::monitor -> XRRSetMonitor on one test thread against the same on another, with libXrandr's single extinfo shared by every display in the process. XInitThreads does not cover this cache (input.rs already serializes XTest for the same reason). A plausible path to 'corrupted size vs. prev_size': one thread closes its display, which frees its dpyinfo via the close hook. Another thread's fast path reads the stale extinfo->cur and finds dpyinfo->display equal to its own Display* (malloc reused the freed Display). XRRFindDisplay then writes into the freed info. Production impact: low. X11Inventory is !Send and each frd/fr process opens one display for RandR, but nothing stops two inventories on two threads in one process. Fix options: (a) one fr-native process-wide lock around every Xext-based call (RandR, Damage, XFixes, XTest, XShm in the C bridge) and around XCloseDisplay of displays that used them, with input.rs's XTEST lock folded in; (b) for this test binary only, drive the helper's monitor changes with the xrandr CLI (a separate process, so no shared in-process cache) and serialize the inventories. Not fixed yet; logs are in ts1:~/fr_chk/uap4_{memcheck,helgrind}.log.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 2026-10-15 fix (56090fa): the four fr-native test binaries that share display_inventory/support.rs (display_inventory, selected_damage, cursor_capture, image_transfer) now serialize in-process X11 use: each Screen holds a process-wide lock from before XOpenDisplay until after XCloseDisplay, and a failed test does not poison it. Evidence: helgrind on display_inventory at 56090fa (ts1:~/fr_chk/uap4_helgrind2.log), 12/12 passed, ZERO race reports with Xext/XRandR/XDamage/XFixes frames (before: XextFindDisplay 18, XRRSetMonitor 10, XextAddDisplay 8, XRRGetMonitors 3, ...). The remaining 500 contexts are Rust std/hashbrown atomics noise, as before. display_inventory takes 1.2 s with the lock. CORRECTION: the 56090fa commit message's '12 passed in 0.33 s' came from a run before the lock reached ts1. The fr-native all-features suite did pass with the lock (c45b547 verification, 697 passed later). Production opens one inventory per media worker process; cursor_capture tests that do not use Screen are not covered. Closing.

title: Check macOS input authority after native event preparation and refuse unknown pointer positions
description:
Plan sections 6.3, 7.3, 15.1 and PROTOCOL section 6 require checking the original input lease, action ticket and generations immediately before every OS submission. The live macOS MacPointer::submit_checked currently invokes final_check before creating key, movement, button or scroll CGEvents; button/scroll can also query the current cursor after that check. A blocked allocation/query can therefore submit expired input. current_location also substitutes CGPointZero when its native query fails.

Prepare and retain the exact native event and proposed local state before the final check. Only post that prepared event after the original check succeeds. Discard it without submission on refusal; commit held/pointer/click metadata only for actual submitted effects, preserving release cleanup and partial-effect accounting. Refuse unavailable pointer evidence rather than fabricating coordinates. Keep native events behind the existing narrow fr-native FFI boundary, without new dependencies or alternate runtime.

Acceptance: deterministic regressions exercise the production Rust submission path for prepare/check/post ordering, delayed-preparation expiry, cancellation, native preparation failures, held-key/button state and click state; native tests retain real OS-event coverage. Run pinned formatter, relevant compiler/Clippy/tests and attempt full repository gates. Platform and hardware evidence remain explicitly separate from portable policy checks.
notes:
Implemented native event ownership with prepare/check/post ordering for key, movement, button and scroll input. Revalidate the selected native target after preparation; prepare text properties before the final check. Refuse missing/nonfinite pointer evidence, preserve click/position state on cancelled preparation, restore original holds on confirmed post refusal, and retain uncertain submission cleanup obligations.

Verification: 25 exact-production Rust component tests passed on nightly-2026-08-31 using an explicitly deterministic test-only FFI boundary; strict Clippy passed. Three principal regression cases fail on the preceding production source. Independent Rust/C ownership, ABI and receipt review found no blocker. Workspace formatting, docs lane and whitespace checks passed. Full all-feature metadata compilation was blocked when the unchanged pinned Asupersync dependency was killed with SIGKILL. title: Connect macOS host sharing to supervised console and sleep lifecycle evidence
description:
The macOS host currently passes no session monitor, so its existing local-stop/authority teardown is not connected to native console-session lifecycle evidence. Implement a supervised read-only macOS fr-session-monitor, mandatory for the shipped macOS frd run path and included by the signed installer.

Bind the actual inherited SecuritySessionId, UID and console set. Require documented typed CoreGraphics console/login properties and graphical access; consume AppKit switch-out, sleep, logout/power-off and protected-data loss only as negative terminal signals. Preserve original bounded native-read deadlines on Darwin's sleep-inclusive clock, service pipe replies while AppKit initializes/stalls, and never auto-resume the original owner. Native calls stay outside broker authority paths; old input, clipboard and capture are retired through the existing host supervisor.

Scope is console/switch/logout/sleep evidence, NOT guaranteed graphical screen-lock detection. Apple DTS explicitly does not guarantee protected-data loss on every screen lock and describes common screen-lock notifications as implementation details: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/850327. Keep this distinction in CLI status and docs; do not invent an unlocked state from an absent private property. Real Apple SDK compilation and physical switch/logout/sleep qualification remain required before claiming platform support. Plan sections 2.2, 7, 10.2, 19, 24.
notes: Implemented the supervised read-only native helper, immutable console identity and original sleep-inclusive evidence, fixed-size platform-specific IPC, mandatory macOS host wiring, checked installed-image launch, installer packaging and Apple SDK/target CI steps. Passed: 10 native policy tests, 4 responder tests, final 22 shared monitor tests, strict Linux and actual aarch64-apple-darwin component Clippy/typechecks (including unmodified helper source), 1672 original-workspace portable tests. Full application gates remain blocked locally by unchanged Asupersync rustc SIGKILL. Objective-C SDK compilation, physical Mac lifecycle events and tailnet behavior are unverified; no graphical screen-lock claim. Separate qualification bead fr-6y4w. Keep in progress until native/integration gates are retained.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: 2026-11-10 physical-Mac qualification (Claude; fix a678fc10 on main). Main's frd could not start on mac-studio (macOS 27.0.1, logged in, unlocked, display awake): session_monitor_unavailable, Host(SessionMonitor(Native(UnsupportedSession))), in every launch context. Two faults in fr-session-monitor: (1) fr_ms_open required [NSApp setActivationPolicy:Prohibited] to answer YES, but an unbundled helper already starts Prohibited and AppKit answers NO to a no-op switch; now the resulting policy is required. comments.author: ClaudeOpus55
comments.text:
2026-11-10 (Claude; measurements only, no code changed). mac-studio's LaunchAgent frd (a63edaec build) ended 3 runs with Host(SessionEnded(EvidenceExpired)) between about 18:14 and 19:06. launchd restarted it each time (runs 4 -> 6). There were none from 19:06 to at least 20:51. frd.log has no timestamps, so the times are bounded by log mtimes.
The parent queries the helper every 50 ms and caps each Active reply at the query's send time + 500 ms VALID_NS (session_monitor.rs accept). The helper stamps its own read start + 500 ms.
I ran a probe that copies the helper's AppKit setup (Prohibited policy, finishLaunching), its native reads (SessionGetInfo x2, CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary, CGMainDisplayID / CGDisplayIsOnline / CGDisplayIsAsleep, isProtectedDataAvailable) and its 20 ms pump. It ran for 15 min under an Interactive LaunchAgent, as frd does, at load 21-29 on 36 cores. Results: about 32.5k turns, max gap between read starts 170 ms, slowest single read 147 ms, 3 gaps over 100 ms, none over 250 ms. Two copies ran side by side, with and without the latency-critical activity assertion that the indicator helper holds, and the numbers were identical. So App Nap is not the cause here, and adding the assertion to this helper would not help.
The three ends coincided with heavier load: my local test builds ran until about 18:20, and earlier today load reached 90-150. A lapse needs a stall over 500 ms in the helper's read or in frd's own query thread, which means heavy overload.
Design question (owner/contributor): a lapse ends the run and drops any viewer. Suspending sharing until fresh evidence returns would ride out overload, but it would weaken "lost console-session evidence ends sharing".

comments.author: ClaudeOpus55
comments.text:
2026-11-10 (Claude): a live view-only session from mac-mini-old ended after 7 s on Host(SessionEnded(EvidenceExpired)) at load ~34. That was 1 of 14 sessions today. The error is the parent-side Error::EvidenceExpired, not Native(EvidenceExpired): no Active reply extended the bound for ~500 ms. It cannot tell a helper read stall from a supervisor stall.

Is QoS the lever? frd's and the helper's threads run at priority 31 (default QoS), the same as the compile jobs that load this Mac. I ran a 15-minute A/B under an Interactive LaunchAgent: 4 processes side by side, at load 22-35, with live view sessions during part of it.
- read/default (a copy of the helper loop: native reads plus a 20 ms pump): max gap 151.4 ms, slowest read 127.7 ms, 4 gaps over 100 ms, 0 over 250 ms.
- read/ui (the same with QOS_CLASS_USER_INTERACTIVE): identical, 151.4 ms max gap, 127.7 ms slowest read, 4 gaps over 100 ms.
- sleep/default and sleep/ui (frd's supervisor shape, 5 ms sleeps): max 12.5 and 9.5 ms.

The same slow native read hit both read variants at the same moment. So the stalls are inside the system calls (SessionGetInfo / CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary / display queries), shared across processes, not in scheduling, and raising QoS would not prevent a lapse. The remaining options are the design choices already noted: suspend vs end on a lapse, or a longer VALID_NS.

comments.author: ClaudeOpus55
comments.text:
2026-11-11 (Claude): every frd on mac-studio ends together, roughly every 20-60 min under load.

Observed today: at about 03:50, 04:17, 04:51:30, ~04:58, ~05:06 and ~05:59, every frd on mac-studio stopped at the same moment: the installed LaunchAgent host and my 1-3 test hosts on ports 8444-8447 (different builds, including main 61939487). Each logged frd-indicator Host(SessionEnded(EvidenceExpired)), or Host(Policy(Expired)). launchd restarted the installed host each time (pids 70036, 85993, 78707 since 05:00). Any live session ends with it.

Likely cause, from the code: session_monitor.rs accepts an Active reply only until min(reply.until_ns, sent + VALID_NS), with VALID_NS = 500 ms, and Evidence::check stops the run once now >= until_ns. Any stall of the frd or monitor processes longer than about 500 ms after a request is sent expires the evidence, and the run ends. Hosts with different binaries failing at the same instant points to a machine-wide stall rather than one build. This Mac runs at load 15-30 with other agents' builds, swap is at 6.2 of 7.2 GB, and on 11-10 I measured share-task stalls of 136-528 ms per poll at load 60-95. I have not caught a stall in the act (no timestamps in frd.log), so this cause is inferred, not proven.

Decision for the owner/contributor: ending the whole run on a single late reply is fail-safe but costly here. Options: (a) a longer VALID_NS (detects logout or user switch later); (b) on expiry, pause capture and input (send nothing) and resume when fresh Active evidence for the same session arrives, ending only after a longer bound. Option (b) keeps the never-share-without-fresh-evidence rule. I have not changed this code.

comments.author: ClaudeOpus55
comments.text:
2026-11-11 (Claude): which native call is slow. Interim result; the probe runs until ~10:45.

Setup: a read-only probe (ws_probe, no UI, no capture) repeats the monitor's macOS reads in one turn every ~30 ms on mac-studio: event pump, SessionGetInfo, CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary, display queries. It logs every turn over 100 ms.

06:45-07:45 (~120k turns):
- 11 turns over 100 ms. In every one the time is CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary: 102-348 ms. The pump took 26-30 ms; SessionGetInfo and the display queries took ~0.
- Worst turn: 378 ms (CGSession 348 ms) at 07:20:55. No turn passed 500 ms in this hour, and no frd on mac-studio ended in it (the LaunchAgent host stayed up).
- Two clusters: 06:50:13-06:50:22 (four turns, up to 323 ms), and 07:40:56-07:42:01 (four turns, 190-238 ms) while my live test sessions were capturing.

Also seen this morning: the Claude desktop app takes a screen capture every 5 s (unified log). Around the 06:00:00 and 06:42:08 endings those captures took 1-2 s, while python sleepers in the same windows stalled under 300 ms. Likely something WindowServer-wide slows at those moments, and CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary waits on it (inferred, not shown).

Separate from the mass endings: the early host_stopped ends I saw today (one per host in the fr-foub A/B) left frd serving with share Desktop(Ok). They are not evidence expiry.

Implication for the VALID_NS decision (owner): a 500 ms window from the START of the read leaves ~150 ms of margin over the worst stall seen this hour. One more option to weigh beside (a)/(b): read CGSession less often or off the evidence path. SessionGetInfo answered in ~0 ms in every logged turn.

comments.author: ClaudeOpus55
comments.text:
2026-11-11 (Claude): a 2 s window keeps a host through the mass endings that stop 500 ms hosts. Measured with idle hosts on mac-studio.

How often: the installed host's frd.log (started 11-09 19:37) has 86 session-evidence stops (EvidenceExpired) and 41 policy-lease stops (Policy(Expired)) by 11-11 08:26, about one every 17 minutes. After each stop, launchd's restart was also refused with encoder_unavailable (videotoolbox=Unsupported) 51 times before a probe passed.

A/B, from 08:50 for 3 hours, all hosts idle (no viewer, no capture), beside the installed host:
- 8444: main 3b96affc, unmodified (500 ms).
- 8445: the same build with VALID_NS = 2 s in frd's session_monitor.rs, host_policy/live.rs and the helper's macos_session_policy.rs. Not committed.
A watcher restarts a stopped test host after 15 or 25 s, so every ending counts.

Result over the 3 hours (08:50:20-11:50:21). Three mass endings; in each, every host on 500 ms stopped and the 2 s host did not:

| Time     | Reason          | Stopped                                   | 2 s host 8445 | Measured stall at that moment |
|----------|-----------------|-------------------------------------------|---------------|-------------------------------|
| 08:52:59 | EvidenceExpired | installed (11779), 8444                   | kept running  | CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary 456 ms (ws_probe) |
| 09:40:12 | Policy(Expired) | installed (28253), 8444, 8446             | kept running  | policy-store path walk 805 ms at 09:40:11.3 (stall_probe) |
| 10:32:56 | EvidenceExpired | installed (72799), 8444, 8446             | kept running  | ws_probe turn 600 ms (CGSession 571); scd_probe CGSession 560 ms, configd 0 ms |

8445 ran the whole 3 hours as one process (pid 18037, 2:59:15 elapsed at the end). 8446 was a separate fr-foub test host on main (500 ms), so it is a third 500 ms sample. Caveat: the 10:32:56 ending coincided with a release build I ran on mac-studio, so that one was load I caused; 08:52:59 and 09:40:12 had no build of mine running.

Probe totals: ws_probe (06:45-10:45, 460,361 turns) had 8 turns of 300 ms or more; its only two above 450 ms are the 08:52:59 and 10:32:56 endings. scd_probe (09:24:40-11:54:40, 234,608 turns) never saw configd and CGSession disagree, and none was missing; worst configd 960 ms, worst CGSession 560 ms.

Cause, for the session-evidence lease:
- ws_probe (read-only, repeats the helper's native reads every ~30 ms) logged a 480 ms turn ending 08:52:56.796. CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary took 456 ms of it, the slowest seen. Both 500 ms hosts stopped within the next 2 s; the 2 s host did not.
- stall_probe (100 ms timed waits at default and user-interactive QoS, plus the policy store's path walk) logged nothing over 150 ms around 08:52:56. So that ending was not CPU scheduling or the filesystem. It is the CGSession call: SessionGetInfo answered in about 0 ms throughout.

Cause, for the policy lease (09:40:12): the policy store's load walks "/" and opens each path component (Store::load in host_policy). stall_probe timed that same walk at 805 ms at 09:40:11.3, right before the stop; on the rest of the run its slowest walks were 388 ms and 352 ms (both at 11:48:00-01). The later policy ending at 11:59:26 (below) also came with a slow walk (605 ms). So the policy lease lapses on filesystem latency, not on WindowServer. Option (c) below would not touch it.

Decision (owner). The options and what this data says about each:
(a) VALID_NS 2 s for both leases (frd and helper): a logout, user switch or policy change takes effect up to 2 s later instead of 0.5 s. The A/B supports this directly: 3 of 3 endings stopped every 500 ms host and none stopped the 2 s host. The slowest single stall measured in 5 hours of probes was 960 ms (configd, see (c)), under 2 s.
(b) On a lapse, pause capture and input, and resume on fresh evidence for the same session, ending only after a longer bound: keeps the 500 ms freshness for what is sent, but needs new pause/resume code in the host.
(c) Take the session evidence from a source that does not wait on WindowServer, for example the console user from SCDynamicStore instead of CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary. It needs a live user-switch test I can't run without disturbing the owner's session. The probe data weakens (c): over 2.5 hours, SCDynamicStore's console-user read was itself slow once (960 ms at 10:38:02, while CGSession took 41 ms; I was restarting test host 8446 at that moment), so switching sources alone would still lapse a 500 ms lease. And the fr-uvji spec names typed CoreGraphics console/login properties, so (c) also changes the spec.
My recommendation: (a) now, since it is a three-constant change and the A/B shows it removes these endings, and (b) later if 2 s turns out too slow. I have not changed VALID_NS on main; it was posted here as an owner decision.
After the A/B, two more mass endings while I ran live viewer tests against a 500 ms test host (8446); the 2 s host was no longer running, so they have no comparison:
- 11:59:26 Policy(Expired): installed host 72961 -> 63037 and 8446. stall_probe timed the policy-store walk at 605 ms at 11:59:26.141.
- 12:06:50 EvidenceExpired: installed host 63037 -> 8237 and 8446 (no CGSession probe was running then). At 12:07 mac-studio's load average was 35, from other work on the machine (an rch ftx build, ld/rustc, FSEvents at 110% CPU, du); my last build had ended at 12:05:58.
That is five mass endings today between 08:52 and 12:07, about one per 40 minutes.
The test hosts 8444 and 8445 were stopped by the watcher at 11:50:21. I did not stop or restart the installed host; launchd restarted it after each ending (now pid 8237).

title: Version 1 release: signed artifacts reproducing tested behavior
description:
WHY: The definition of done: install a small process family on a supported host already on Tailscale, grant OS permissions, and use the desktop from qualified native desktop, mobile, and browser clients — no account, no pairing — with every failure honest and every claim evidenced.

EXIT CRITERIA: signed/notarized macOS family, signed Windows packages, reproducible Linux package, mobile store-signed builds, browser assets versioned with the protocol — all built by repository-owned commands through the dsr lanes; installation artifacts reproduce the tested behavior (release-candidate re-run of the fault and security suites on the shipped binaries); unsupported states fail specifically; no performance claim outruns retained evidence; license/provenance manifests complete for every native component (FFmpeg configuration and license notices, opus, the Windows audio component, platform SDKs) with the distribution decision recorded; the v1.4 completion rules honored — expired input never executes, approval gates observation, shared encoders outlive subscribers, recovery works under the advertised loss envelope, browser idle/flush and endpoint-audio scopes have qualification evidence; codebase under the 240k ceiling by the fixed counting command.

Provenance: plan sections 20.3, 23 Phase 5, 26.

Certificate/authentication/binding failures remain terminal; preserve total attempt/deadline limits and never replay or reacquire control. title: Serial native host drops a concurrent client's handshake between attempts (second dial stalls ~5 s)
description:
WHY: frd's serial native host (native_connection/host/serial.rs) serves one connection at a time and takes a fresh listener per attempt (the previous socket is consumed, the next one is bound after the retirement wait and the 250 ms cooldown). A second client that dials while the first is served loses its QUIC Initials in that gap; with the client's retransmit backoff (1.5 s, then 3 s) it misses its 5 s handshake budget and only connects on a reconnect attempt, about 5 s later. Any two viewers, or one app doing a directory fetch and a session, hit this.

EVIDENCE (2026-11-10, ts2 host at a678fc10 nvenc --once, iOS simulator on mac-studio, review-fixes WIP client): tcpdump on ts2 udp/8443 showed two client flows from 100.89.198.71 (ports 57285 and 53455, the app's launch-time directory fetch and its session) at 10:52:10.93. The host answered 57285 at 12.437 (directory exchange done by 12.46); 53455's retransmit at 13.935 got no answer, and the host logged attempt 2 as refused `Err(Accept(HandshakeTimeout))` while the app stayed "connecting (attempt 1)". Earlier runs r6/r8 counted 6 and 10 refused attempts before the admitted session. Per-attempt reasons are not logged (only the totals in peer_finished).

CLIENT MITIGATION (landed with the iOS review fixes): the app no longer fetches the directory while a session is starting or open, and a session start waits for an in-flight fetch to the same machine (at most 3 s) plus 400 ms for frd's cooldown. This does not help two different viewers.

SCOPE: keep accepting (or at least keep the socket bound and queue Initials) across attempts in the serial host without weakening its retirement rule (each attempt's transport destroyed before the next is served); or answer a concurrent Initial with a typed busy refusal the client can retry at once. Log each refused attempt's typed reason (content-free). Test: a second client dialing during a served attempt connects within its first handshake budget after the first ends (real UDP, not a mock).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Client mitigation landed in the iOS app (c79d7415): no directory fetch while a session is starting or open, and a start waits for a same-machine fetch (at most 3 s, then 400 ms for frd's cooldown), shown as "Connecting to...", dropped and offered again on backgrounding. Live after it: ts2 host log attempts 1 refused 0, first picture 2050 ms (before: refused 6 and 10 with ~5 s stalls). The host-side gap stays open; the busy refusal it needs is fr-0kyf (upstream foreign-source Initial refusal) and izv6 part 1.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: The host-side fix this needs is fr-rc-transport-multiclient-qda (one listener demultiplexing several clients, a cold accept without dropping the first Initial); fr-0kyf is the interim typed busy refusal.

comments.author: ClaudeOpus55
comments.text:
2026-11-11 (Claude): f8a2f179 is a client-side mitigation for one case of this: a reopen to the same serial host. It does not fix the host-side gap.

A Mac viewer reopens viewing in a new attempt when its window is resized, or on a display change, and that attempt dialed at once. Against mac-studio (test host, a21cbf5b-era build), a resize reopen on mac-mini-old either never reconnected within 20 s or took about 20 s. The host logged two Accept(HandshakeTimeout) ends in the run that recovered (timestamped: peer finished 10:38:15.995, next share listening 10:38:16.092, timeouts 10:38:27.514 and 10:38:38.276). A full-screen reopen, whose seal waits ~0.55 s for AppKit, connected at once in 3 of 3 runs.

f8a2f179 makes both reopen paths wait policy.delay(1) (initial_backoff, 250 ms by default) before the next attempt. After it, 3 of 3 resize reopens showed the new picture about 2 s after the resize, with no handshake timeout logged. The namespace reopen test now requires the gap; without the wait it measured 2.9 and 2.6 µs and failed.

Not explained: why a too-early Initial costs about 20 s rather than one retransmission. The host accepted later Initials that then hit its handshake timeout, and the serial host stays busy with each one. Under host load, 250 ms may be too short. The host-side fix is still fr-rc-transport-multiclient-qda (or fr-0kyf's busy refusal).

It is not only reopens. At 12:12, a fresh `fr connect` from mac-mini-old to the same test host (port 8446), started about 10 s after the previous session ended, hit 4 HandshakeTimeout attempts before one connected. The host had been listening since 12:12:15.499 and logged Accept(HandshakeTimeout) at 12:12:37.194 and 12:12:47.956. mac-studio's load average was about 30 then, from other work on the machine. So a listening serial host under load can also miss a first dial.

title: Workspace bootstrap: root Cargo.toml plus fr-core first slice (typed IDs, generations, limits)
description:
WHY: Everything else in the project consumes typed identifiers and one tested limits structure, and the cargo workspace cannot exist safely without its first real crate (a virtual workspace with zero members breaks every cargo command in the checkout — verified empirically before this tracker existed).

SCOPE: In ONE commit, create the root Cargo.toml (resolver "3", members = ["crates/*"], [workspace.package] edition 2024 + license-file, [workspace.dependencies] with asupersync pinned default-features=false and an fr-core path entry, workspace lints with unsafe_code = "forbid"), Cargo.lock, and crates/fr-core with #![forbid(unsafe_code)] as line 1. fr-core's first vertical slice: (a) distinct newtype identifiers for host boot, OS session, remote session, input lease, display geometry, codec configuration, recovery generation, and viewport mapping — deliberately NOT interchangeable, no raw u64s crossing module boundaries; (b) the single limits structure holding the protocol/resource ceilings: 64 KiB ordinary control message, 1 MiB clipboard item, 16 MiB max encoded access unit, 8192 max per axis, 16,777,216 max coded pixels, 2-12 picture reassembly window, 32 MiB per-viewer compressed budget — all as negotiate-downward ceilings with checked arithmetic helpers that validate length/stride/product before any allocation.

CONSTRAINTS: Asupersync is the only runtime dependency. No unsafe. Never leave a directory under crates/ without a manifest, even briefly.

ACCEPTANCE: cargo fmt/check/clippy/test green; unit tests prove identifier non-interchangeability (compile-fail tests where practical), ceiling validation rejects over-limit and overflow-adjacent values, and the limits structure round-trips its negotiated-downward logic. Provenance: plan sections 7.2, 17.2, 22.1; AGENTS.md section 8.1.
close_reason: Implemented at c9fb756: root workspace + fr-core first slice (8 typed ID/generation types with compile-fail non-interchangeability proofs; ProtocolLimits with all section 17.2 ceilings, downward-only overrides, negotiation, checked arithmetic). Gates run remotely via rch at this revision: fmt clean, clippy -D warnings clean, 14 unit + 2 doc-tests pass. Independent review by AzureBasin caught and I fixed the per-viewer-budget floor bug (regression test included); self re-verification pass performed — peers may reopen on any failure.

title: In-process X11 input executor keeps an X connection reader alive after its session ends
description: Found 2026-10-13 making client_x11 pass: after an fr-native start_x11 session finishes (running.finish() handoff_safe, seat released) and the Agent and InputClient are dropped, some thread in the test process still reads an X connection to that test's Xvfb for at least 500 ms (probed). Killing that Xvfb then makes Xlib's default I/O error handler exit(1) the whole test process (CI run 38362585122; deterministic on trj). Production impact is bounded: frd never loads Xlib and fr-input-agent runs one process per lease, which exits. The client_x11 harness now starts Xvfb with -terminate and does not kill it (the server exits when its last client goes away). Work: find the owner (native executor thread, its X11Pointer, or a runtime worker), make shutdown close it, then restore an explicit server kill in the harness as the planted negative.
close_reason: No longer reproduces at 2aef00b: with the explicit Xvfb kill restored, client_x11 passed 15 of 15 (parallel) on ts1 and 5 of 5 on trj, where it had been deterministic on 2026-10-13. The leaking owner was NOT identified, so this is not a root-cause fix. The kill is restored in the harness (commit after 2aef00b) as the guard: a returning leak would make Xlib exit the test process and fail CI.

title: Lossy 40-120 ms paths: host send starvation expires unsent pictures and renewal records before any recovery can run
description:
Found 2026-10-01 while qualifying fr-4vf5 (controlled reference recovery, 8052213). The namespace control matrix never exercised the new controlled recovery: every held row reports recovered_streams 0. Lossy rows at 40 and 120 ms RTT end the same way on 67acc95 and on 8052213.

Host diagnostics (a scratch build with FRDIAG prints at the host serve round, recover, controlled_outcome and the three SendCache OriginalExpired sites; never committed; 4 complete matrix runs) show what ends them. All of them end in the host's FIRST serving round, before any viewer recovery request. Runs 2-4, lossy ends at 40/120 ms: 13 of 20 are MediaTransport(Media(Send(OriginalExpired))). The rest are a renewal record past its delivery deadline (4), an input or control-renewal record (1 each), and clock synchronization (1). Run 5 split the OriginalExpired sites:
- 3x SendCache::authorize_write: a prepared PacketOffer submitted 0.3-3.4 ms past its send_by after waiting for transport admission. frd's QuicEgress::transmit_frame_authorized then CLOSES the transport and the egress ('an uncertain/partial reliable write is never continued').
- 1x SendCache::tick: frame 13, announced, 2 of 3 fragments sent, 2926 bytes, 254 ms old. The cache clears and sets needs_recovery. frd's VideoServices::maintain (stream_check) still ends the session.
A 3 KB picture missing a 250 ms deadline at 40 ms RTT is send starvation, not picture size.

Likely mechanism: Asupersync 0.5.0 quic_native/transport.rs is NewReno. on_loss_congestion halves cwnd once per recovery epoch, down to 2 x max_datagram_size, and there is no pacing. A lost last packet in flight is detected only by PTO (srtt + 4 rttvar, doubling). At 1-5% loss the window sits near its floor and tail losses stall sends for hundreds of ms.

How the client sees it: host_control_revoked with reason local_revoke (a mislabel; any serve error was labelled so, fixed by the follow-up commit to host_control_failure / host_failure), or transport_deadline_expired.

Options (each needs a decision; none is done):
1. Upstream Asupersync: tail-loss probing (RFC 9002 PTO sends a probe early; RACK-TLP-like), pacing, and a measured loss response for unreliable datagrams. Bounded, counted upstream work (AGENTS.md 3.1).
2. frd egress: an offer whose send_by passed BEFORE any byte was admitted is obsolete work, not an uncertain write. Drop it and fence the picture (needs_recovery) instead of closing the transport. Check that quic::send reports 'nothing written' distinctly from a partial reliable write.
3. frd host round: with negotiated recovery, a send-cache reference loss (needs_recovery, picture announced) waits, bounded by the recovery horizon, for the viewer's recovery request instead of ending. MEDIA_DELIVERY.md already says the caller must recover. The viewer requests once its reference deadline passes on the announced, incomplete picture.
4. OWNER DECISION: the 250 ms reference horizon is the protocol maximum (SendPolicy validation, PROTOCOL.md limits). A path-aware horizon (like the f7ts source-age bound) would need a plan/protocol change.

Acceptance: in the namespace control matrix, the 40 ms RTT + 1% loss row holds in most runs, and some lossy rows report recovered_streams >= 1 on a held lease. Planted negative per option implemented.
notes:
2026-10-01: the client-side label of these ends is fixed. A serve failure under a live authority, including in the round that granted control, now reports host_control_failure / host_failure instead of host_control_revoked / local_revoke (134b6d7 plus the follow-up lease-registration commit). The starvation itself is unchanged.

The post-dispatch observation path now rechecks the original sender before presentation sees its cleared source snapshot, preserving the typed recoverable reference failure rather than ending as PresentedState(Closed). The canonical host/viewer regression interposes this failure and continues recovery and renewal on the original transport/worker owners. This is real TLS/UDP plus subprocess IPC with synthetic codec/presentation fixtures, not live impairment or hardware evidence. New daemon regression awaits CI: local full checking hit ENOSPC, then pinned Asupersync rustc SIGKILL under the shared 8 GiB memory limit. Broader lossy-path acceptance and upstream transport work remain OPEN.

Commit b27dc725af27a7720e930fc6cc17dac9b7bcadaf uses the canonical presentation-capable viewing bootstrap, retains original input attachments and asserts the host remains Host::Observe with no control grant. It keeps the presentation precondition, typed reference-failure, recovery/renewal, same-connection and original-worker assertions. The prior source review was not a passing execution; runtime rerun is still required. No production recovery deadline, authority rule or lossy-path acceptance was relaxed.

The same live subscriber now validates and consumes only canonical obsolete PresentedState reports under the original media binding instead of passing missing progress to the presentation verifier and closing QUIC. Original source/viewer authorities, accepted-evidence counts and the one fixed recovery deadline remain unchanged. Early local-failure and active-handoff paths also fully parse these reports; wrong routes, malformed bytes, foreign bindings and an unselected capability remain refused. Added three regressions using the actual production dispatch seam and existing real UDP/TLS/source-IPC fixture, including ordinary replacement to the next IDR on the original worker. Pinned formatting, changed-line whitespace checks and independent source review passed. The new daemon regressions are NOT runtime-validated: the shared host exhausted disk/memory and full Cargo dependency setup was killed; hosted CI is queued. This is a narrow source fix, not lossy-path, hardware or full-suite qualification. Broader starvation and impaired-path acceptance remain OPEN.

After the original source recovery schedule and deadline check, the existing handoff now carries the controller's single token and target on that scheduled capture, keeping force=false and all original authority, queue, native/network cancellation and failure budgets. It records validated actual bitrate before decoder startup or later expiry; a native old-rate result is honest deferral and the existing generation-evidence reset explicitly cancels retained old-scope intent. This permits a measured cut that lacked normal sender credit to reach the recovery IDR. Added original-session regressions for static deferral followed by recovery application, and a recovery IDR that still defers its target. Full frd runtime execution and 40/120 ms lossy-path acceptance remain unqualified; no recovery deadline was extended. Five actual synthetic-worker subprocess scenarios passed: both applied/deferred paths, both legacy-recovery refusals and old-scope replay refusal. The existing pure bitrate suite passed 20/20 again. Pinned formatting and independent source/ownership review passed; these fixture checks do not execute the two new full-daemon regressions. Source fix: SendCache now anchors its recovery deadline at the first local reference-failure detection, before later host service or peer recovery admission. next_deadline exposes the bound immediately, and delayed local waits, peer requests, polling and direct replacement cannot restart it. Deadline overflow closes the sender; existing independent recovery-rate accounting remains at actual admission. comments.text: 2026-10-13 related finding (bisected): frd integration test fanout::round_robin_budget_survives_backpressure_and_one_viewer_leaving passes at b2181e2 (asupersync 0.5.0) and fails from 6037b60 (the pin) on — also with the host datagram cap put back to 1500, so the pin itself. The test stops driving viewer A's socket and expects A's member to report datagram backpressure (pending) within 12 transmits; on the pin A never reports pending even after 200 transmits (probe). Datagram ENQUEUE is identical in both versions (bounded 256, drop-oldest); the difference is in how the queue drains without ACKs (cwnd gating of DATAGRAM frames in the 1-RTT packet assembly). If the pin emits datagrams regardless of an exhausted congestion window, FrankenRemote's pacing loses its congestion signal exactly on lossy/congested paths — a candidate contributor to the lossy-row failures here. Next: compare connection.rs datagram flush gating (0.5.0 ~line 3009 vs ee72b66 ~3563) and the driver's cwnd-blocked branch.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
2026-10-13 evening (commits a11a27f, 0e42b24, 19e46cc; ts1 namespace with tailnet-path emulation, instrumented scratch builds never committed).

Diagnosis of the busy view-only failure (3 of 6 runs, at HEAD and on the 10-12 build alike): the host's shared publisher found Send(OriginalExpired) on its own (a picture still unsent at its 250 ms horizon; cwnd at the 2400-byte floor, the media margin then allows ~1 packet per RTT), closed that viewer, and a sole viewer's departure closed the publication. The client saw an unnamed HostStopping, or NamespaceExhausted(DecodeFailed) after the host's Failed notice.

Done:
- 0e42b24 host: option 3 for the SHARED publisher (the single-viewer path already had it): Entry::absorb keeps a sender-discovered broken chain, fences the entry, its session sends one Failed progress record, the viewer's bound request inherits the deadline. Real-QUIC test with planted negative. Busy e2e 6/6 (was 3/6); the 1% row held every run, twice via recovered_streams 1.
- a11a27f client: the host's Failed notice is ReferenceExpired (an abandoned chain), not DecodeFailed; NamespaceExhausted(ReferenceExpired|RecoveryExpired) -> video_reference_lost; host-ended sessions named from their Closed report.
- 19e46cc transport: delivery allowance 3 -> 7 probe timeouts. The pinned stack's PTO sends only a PING; the lost data is resent after the PING's ACK, so one tail loss costs ~3 PTOs (one 67-byte record unacked 248 ms at 40 ms RTT after one PTO).
- 88a0345 (fr-t4lj): the client names the host's close-packet reason.

Matrix after all of it (one run each): view-only optional rows 16 of 17 show every change (only 120 ms RTT + 5% unlimited ended, video_startup_expired); before, the 120 ms lossy 5 Mbit rows and 200 ms RTT ended at 1-2 of 6. Controlled lossy 40/120 ms rows still end within 1-5 steps.

What the controlled ends actually are (client's typed chain, printed by a scratch build): Control(Expired) x2 (the controlled viewer's own pending input record passed its send deadline = min(view deadline, ticket deadline, receipt timeout); the CLI labels this transport_deadline_expired, which is misleading), Control(View(Input(Stopped(InvalidControl)))) x2 (control_renewal_failed), Startup(Expired) x2 (decoder restart), Control(Session(Transport(Expired))) x1 (the only true record-deadline end). Host-side 'no ACK for 2 PTOs' dumps were after the client had already gone. Filed separately.

Ruled out: receiver reassembly limits (4096 fragments), ACK-only packets gated by cwnd (they are exempt), client drive-loop stalls (none >60 ms during rows).

Still open here: upstream asks (PTO probe should carry the oldest unacked data, RFC 9002 6.2.4; NewReno halving per random loss pins cwnd at the floor at 1-5% loss); one complete replacement per connection limits sustained-loss sessions to seconds. Acceptance (40 ms RTT + 1% control row holds in most runs) is NOT met.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
2026-10-14 root cause of the 120 ms RTT / 1% loss controlled ends. Ran 16 rows (4 runs x 4) with host diagnostics: which transport gate refused (with frames), observation/check_lease errors, renewal latency, and every InputServices::permitted term. Only 2/16 rows held 8/8.
- Renewals are healthy: every observation and control renewal completed with 2.5-2.8 s of its 3 s left. The lease is not lapsing.
- Host ends: the observation-renewal drive's gate (drive_checked -> InputServices::permitted) turns false. The false term is always InputServices.other (10/10, files/clipboard/renewal/bridge true), i.e. the video/recovery services: recovery::Admission::permitted fails once the pending RecoveryDemand deadline passes, and recovery::Waiting fails at its until. The refused I/O closes the connection (native io Unauthorized), reported as host_session_ended.
So a reference recovery that misses its budget (ReceivePolicy::recovery_budget_micros = 2 s, max 5 s) ends the whole session. At 120 ms RTT with 1% loss the recovery IDR cannot cross in 2 s: the pinned stack's NewReno window keeps collapsing under random loss, and PTOs are PING-only. Client-side the same budget shows as Startup(Expired) or ReferenceExpired.
Levers: (1) upstream congestion control (the existing asks); (2) a recovery budget that scales with the measured path, like the delivery allowance; (3) a lower bitrate/IDR size under loss (ADAPTIVE_CAPTURE); (4) naming: a host recovery expiry should close with a recovery reason, not SessionEnded. None landed yet.

A = ReceivePolicy::recovery_budget_micros 2 s (default): 1/16 held 8/8, 86/128 steps; ends host_session_ended 12, host_control_failure 2, video_startup_expired 1. comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: 2026-10-14 A/B arm C (host SendPolicy: recovery_horizon 5 s instead of 2 s, max_recoveries_per_window 8 instead of 4; client = arm A HEAD): 1/16 held, 91/128 steps (A 86, B 82). The end mix moved: host_session_ended 12 -> 2, video_startup_expired 1 -> 10. So the host's 2 s recovery horizon was the HOST's ending mechanism at 120 ms / 1%; relaxed, the client's decoder-restart deadline ends the session at about the same step. Conclusion across A/B/C: recovery itself is too slow on this path, and whichever recovery deadline is shortest ends the session. The levers are recovery speed (IDR throughput under loss on the pinned stack: NewReno collapse, PING-only PTO, the upstream asks), fewer recoveries (stronger repair, smaller IDRs under loss: ADAPTIVE_CAPTURE), and then deadlines that follow the measured path. Not landed: no clear step gain.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
2026-11-10 E17 path 2 (Claude; e328dbf5 on main; the owner delegated this decision to me). Decision: keep the 250 ms drive-turn bound and its terminal rule, but judge the bound only after the turn's own poll. Rejected alternatives: a longer bound (it would hide real stalls and let a dead peer hold resources longer) and a non-terminal Expired (a dropped native I/O operation may have partly happened).
What changed: fr-transport quic.rs drive() now runs lifetime::within_turn_bound(turn, sleep(250 ms)). It polls the turn first and returns its result if ready; only then does it poll the bound, failing Expired if that has passed. A turn whose I/O finished while frd's thread was away (the measured case: a 252 ms hub poll, then "expired after 259 ms" on a 10 ms receive wait) now finishes. A turn still pending past the bound fails as before (Expired, dropped through Held, terminal), at most one poll late. Both futures stay pinned in drive, so its future does not grow (clippy large_futures).
Unchanged, still open: a record whose deliver_by passes during a stall still ends the session, and a turn that is truly still pending at 250 ms still fails.
Tests: tests/turn_bound.rs (Linux, real UDP/TLS). A server turn is parked on a 10 ms receive wait while the thread is held 300 ms outside it; it finishes Ok and the connection still carries a record. Planted negative: main plus only this test fails Err(Expired). quic::lifetime::turn_bound_tests: 3 deterministic tests; a bound-first ordering fails all three.
Verified (trj builder image): fmt, workspace clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings, fr-transport suite, turn_bound. On csd, CI's Linux lane (scripts/builder/smoke.sh) on the landed tree: fmt, check, clippy and examples pass. In test, only the pre-existing audio receive_expiry test fails, plus two umask-002 scratch-tree refusals that pass once the directories are not group-writable.

Pinned to 2 CPUs next to 3 busy loops, 9 paired rounds: host drive() unwrap failures 4 (fix) vs 31 (main); the peer_retirement::unfinished_files_offer_... flake 8 vs 8 (pre-existing, it reproduces on main); other failures 19 vs 11, all tests' own 1 s wall-clock budgets or expiry under starvation, at the same sites as main's. title: Reserve X11 shared-image backing before mmap to avoid late SIGBUS
description:
Plan §§5.4, 9.1, 11.1 and 19.1 require bounded native memory ownership and explicit failures. The active Linux X11 transfer path in crates/fr-native/src/x11_image.c creates and truncates a memfd, seals its size, and maps it without reserving backing storage. Truncation alone leaves sparse pages: later shared capture/presentation can fault with SIGBUS under backing-storage exhaustion instead of using the existing socket-transfer fallback.

Reserve the entire checked shared image before mapping or attaching it to the X server. Any reservation refusal must retain the existing typed SharedAllocationUnavailable fallback, close the descriptor, and never advertise an attached shared image. Preserve the decoder sandbox, checked bounds, synchronous X11 ownership and allocation accounting.

Acceptance: production C/Xvfb capture and presentation retain pixel-correct normal SHM/socket behavior; kernel-injected ENOSPC, ENOMEM and unsupported reservation failures select the typed socket fallback; descriptor resources are not leaked; native checks fail against the original sparse-allocation implementation. These are native component checks, not live tailnet or physical GPU qualification.
close_reason: Implemented full-image fallocate before sealing/mmap/X11 attachment; source blob 2c0a29e589f5d917ed9a1a692cbcffb929a9556c. Actual production boundary compiled with -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror and scripts/test_x11_image.sh passed normal MIT-SHM/socket plus kernel-injected ENOSPC, ENOMEM and EOPNOTSUPP, each with four capture/presentation cycles, independent pixel readback, exact fallback/byte accounting and descriptor cleanup. The ENOSPC regression failed against the original sparse-allocation code. No production sandbox changes. UBS native slice exit 0 with no critical findings. This closes the scoped allocation defect only; full workspace validation is running and broader loaded/tailnet/hardware acceptance remains open.
